title: checks: require point-to-point differential pair traces
description: Defines differential-pair conductors as strictly point-to-point, providing clear diagnostics for ambiguous connections.
body:
## What changed

- Define differential-pair conductors as strictly point-to-point.
- Show invalid multi-endpoint and valid point-to-point examples.
- Recommend pin selectors over ambiguous net references.
- Specify an actionable error message that identifies the ambiguous net and terminal pins.

## Why

Differential-pair routing requires two unambiguous endpoints per conductor. Validating that requirement before autorouting prevents invalid routing input and tells users exactly how to correct an ambiguous connection.

## Developer impact

Users receive a clear diagnostic when either differential-pair conductor has more than two terminal pins, while vias and intermediate routing points remain valid.

## Validation

- `git diff --check`
- Reviewed the Markdown structure, TSX examples, and diagnostic wording.

title: fix: stop shrinking CAD models rotated off-axis
description: Fixes CAD model scaling issue where models with declared sizes shrink when rotated at angles that are not multiples of 90 due to incorrect bounding box calculations.
body:
## Problem

A CAD model that declares a `size` matching its own mesh is shrunk whenever its component sits at a rotation that is not a multiple of 90°.

This 6×6mm tactile switch (9.5mm lead span) is the same part four times, at 0°, 30°, 45° and 90°. Only the right-angle ones meet their pads:

| rotation | rendered scale |
| --- | --- |
| 0° | 1.00 |
| 15° | 0.56 |
| 30° | 0.42 |
| 45° | 0.39 |
| 90°, 180° | 1.00 |

## Cause

`getObjectBoundsRelativeToParent` measured each mesh by transforming its bounding box into world space and then back into the parent's frame, as two separate calls:

```js
transformedBounds.applyMatrix4(node.matrixWorld)
transformedBounds.applyMatrix4(parentInverseMatrix)
```

`Box3.applyMatrix4` re-derives an axis-aligned box around the eight transformed corners, so it is **not invertible**. Applying a rotation and then its inverse doesn't cancel — each call grows the box:

```
9.50 × 6.05  ──rotate +30°──►  11.25 × 9.99  ──rotate −30°──►  14.74 × 14.28
```

`getCadModelFitScale` then divides the declared `size` by that inflated measurement and shrinks the model to 0.42 to make it "fit".

Right angles are unaffected because an axis-aligned box is rotation-invariant there.

## Fix

Compose the two matrices and apply them once, so the ancestor transform genuinely cancels:

```js
const localMatrix = parentInverseMatrix.clone().multiply(node.matrixWorld)
transformedBounds.applyMatrix4(localMatrix)
```

Rotations at or below the measured object are still included — the existing `fit includes loader transform group rotation in measured bounds` test covers that and still passes.

## Why this went unnoticed

Two things hid it:

- **`size` is optional, and the fit is skipped without it** (`if (!targetSize) return [1,1,1]`). Parts that don't declare one were never affected.
- **The headless pipeline is correct.** `circuit-json-to-gltf` applies component rotation as a scene-graph property *after* `fitMeshToCadBounds`, so its fit always measures an unrotated mesh. I confirmed it returns `9.500 × 15.000 × 6.050` at 0°, 30° and 45°. Snapshot tests, `tsci build` and poppygl renders are all correct — so no existing test could have caught this. It is visible only in the browser viewer.

## Tests

- `tests/cad-model-fit.test.ts` — asserts scale 1.0 at 0/15/30/45/90/180°. Verified it fails without the fix.
- `stories/Bugs/RotatedModelFitScale.stories.tsx` — visual regression. Pads use `rotated_rect` with `ccw_rotation` and the silkscreen outline is rotated point-by-point, so both turn exactly with the part and a shrunken model visibly pulls away from them. Each instance declares `size` deliberately, since the fit is skipped without it.

Full suite matches `main` exactly: the 4 pre-existing failures (faux-board z defaults, Atari SVG outline) are unchanged, and the fit tests go 4 → 5 passing.

No new Circuit JSON properties are used; everything is in the pinned `circuit-json@0.0.446`.

title: Fix four-pin crystal trace length propagation
description: Fixes trace length propagation for four-pin crystals to ensure that only signal pins are constrained by maximum trace length, preventing autorouting errors related to ground connections.
body:
## Summary

- expose semantic `X1` and `X2` labels on crystal signal ports
- propagate a crystal's maximum trace length through those typed semantic ports
- keep GND-connected crystal ports and the wider ground network unconstrained
- add a routed regression test using the standard `footprint="crystal"`

## Root cause

`Crystal.doInitialSourceDesignRuleChecks` collected every source port belonging to a crystal. For a four-pin crystal, that included the two case/ground ports. Because those ports shared the board-wide GND connectivity map, the crystal's default 10 mm maximum trace length propagated to unrelated GND traces.

The autorouter's precheck then rejected otherwise valid boards whenever distant GND endpoints were more than 10 mm apart.

## Fix

Crystal signal ports carry the semantic labels `X1` and `X2`, included in the component's typed port map. Trace-length propagation now starts directly from `this.portMap.X1` and `this.portMap.X2`. It does not inspect physical pin numbers or scan raw port-hint strings.

Physical pin-to-role mapping remains only in `initPorts`, where a component's package pinout belongs. The design-rule behavior depends solely on the semantic signal roles.

## Impact

RP2040 and other designs using four-pin crystals can route normally without adding an artificial large `maxLength` workaround. The oscillator traces still retain the intended short-trace constraint.

## Validation

- focused four-pin crystal routing regression: pass
- all related crystal tests: 7 pass
- TypeScript `--noEmit`: pass
- Biome check: pass
- regression connects through `X1`/`X2`, asserts exactly 4 PCB traces, and asserts zero `pcb_autorouting_error` records

title: Use canonical net label text for schematic solver bounds
description: Fixes discrepancies between schematic trace solver input and rendered net label dimensions, ensuring accurate routing decisions based on correct label sizes.
body:
## Problem

Core could tell the schematic trace solver that a net label had one name and width, then render a different canonical label for the same connection.

The RP2040 repro makes this visible on the shared QSPI connection. The rendered labels use `QSPI_SS`, but the solver input previously measured local trace names such as `BOOT_SW` and `BOOT_R`, and also used a different font-size assumption. For example, the solver received widths of `0.75` or `0.65` where the rendered `QSPI_SS` label is `0.96` wide. This meant routing decisions were made against undersized or incorrectly named obstacles, and exported solver bug reports did not faithfully represent the final core schematic.

## Root cause

Schematic label text was resolved independently in `createSchematicTraceSolverInputProblem` and `applyNetLabelPlacements`. Those paths had different precedence rules for source-net names, explicit display labels, trace names, and source-port labels, so solver input and rendered output could diverge.

## Fix

- Add a connection-keyed canonical schematic net-label resolver.
- Reuse that resolver when creating solver input and when applying solver label placements.
- Resolve source-net names and explicit trace display labels consistently before falling back to trace or source-port names.
- Measure solver label bounds using the same canonical text and typography used by the renderer.
- Assert the corrected `QSPI_SS`, `BOOT_SW`, and `BOOT_R` solver widths in the complete RP2040 repro.
- Update only the schematic snapshots whose canonical label bounds or placement changed.

## Impact

The schematic trace solver now receives obstacle dimensions for the labels core actually renders. This keeps standalone solver reproductions aligned with core output and prevents routing based on stale, smaller label bounds.

## Validation

- `bun test` for the five affected schematic snapshot tests — 5 passed
- `bunx tsc --noEmit`
- `bunx biome check` for the changed TypeScript files

## Follow-up

The corrected RP2040 input exposes a separate downstream solver issue: the V1V1 trace between RP2040 pins 45 and 50 can be returned through the `ADC_VREF` label after a failed detour. This PR intentionally does not add a core-side workaround for that trace-solver behavior.

title: Clarify differential pair ambiguity warnings
description: Clarifies warnings for differential pairs with ambiguous trace names by providing specific diagnostics without prescriptive advice.
body:
Follow-up to #3011.

## What changed

- Report a named differential-pair trace with more than two terminal pins as an ambiguous trace name.
- Include the pair, connection property, trace name, and complete terminal-pin list.
- Report selector and incomplete-connection failures factually as `expected exactly 2 terminal pins, found N`.
- Remove all advice to delete connections or switch to a pin selector.
- Remove the unnecessary singular/plural message construction.

## Why

Core does not ignore or rewrite the differential-pair connection. The diagnostic should state the topology problem without prescribing a circuit or selector change. A named trace is ambiguous when its resolved connection contains more than two terminal pins; other invalid counts are simply not point-to-point.

## Developer impact

Users receive concise, non-prescriptive diagnostics that identify the actual connection problem and list the affected pins.

## Validation

- Focused differential-pair warning tests: 3 passing, 10 assertions
- `bunx tsc --noEmit`
- Biome checks on all changed files
- `git diff --check`
- Three independent review passes covering wording, edge cases, and minimal-diff quality

title: Warn when differential pairs are not point to point
description: Adds a warning mechanism for differential pairs that do not connect point-to-point, enhancing design rule checks in the circuit.
body:
Implements [tscircuit/rfc#13](https://github.com/tscircuit/rfc/pull/13).

## End-to-end workflow

1. Core parses `<differentialpair>` and retains its `name`, `positiveConnection`, and `negativeConnection` in the component tree.
2. Core renders the subcircuit's source traces, source ports, source nets, and connectivity-map keys.
3. During `SourceDesignRuleChecks`, the differential-pair component validates the positive and negative connections independently.
4. For each connection, Core resolves a named trace or port selector to one subcircuit connectivity group.
5. Core collects the terminal source ports in that connectivity group.
6. Exactly two terminal ports is valid and produces no diagnostic.
7. Any other terminal count stores a `source_property_ignored_warning` in Core's Circuit JSON database. The warning identifies the pair, property, resolved net or selector, terminal pins, and suggested correction.
8. When the component updates or is removed, Core deletes the warnings previously owned by that differential pair before recalculating, preventing stale or duplicate warnings.
9. `circuit.getCircuitJson()` serializes the warning with the rest of the circuit.
10. A follow-up CLI change will classify and display this stored diagnostic when a user runs `tsci check netlist <file>`.

title: Track generated stitches in clearance-aware routing
description: Fixes clearance-aware stitch selection to ensure generated bridge segments are considered, preventing selection of stitches that cross newly created copper.
body:
Stacked on #1920.

## Issue

Clearance-aware stitch selection only indexed the original high-density route fragments. After one route was assembled, its generated bridge segments were invisible, so a later net could select a stitch that crossed newly created copper.

## Implementation

Keep a shared clearance validator and add each accepted merged route before stitching the next connection. Topology trials require clear stitches. Final assembly keeps the existing feasibility rules while ranking every clear candidate ahead of colliding candidates, so the new collision geometry does not make existing routes unsolvable.

The focused SVG snapshot shows the old nearest colliding choice, the clear selection, and a later stitch rejected against an accepted generated stitch.

## Validation

- Focused stitch tests: 5 passed
- Existing routing regressions: 7 passed
- Production build passed
- Dataset 18 sample 10: solved, DRC passed, 176 vias ([result](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/pull/1927#issuecomment-5188399843))
- Dataset 24 sample 6: solved, DRC passed, 275 vias ([result](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/pull/1927#issuecomment-5188427081))
- Controls: dataset 18 samples [1](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/pull/1927#issuecomment-5188479403), [5](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/pull/1927#issuecomment-5188501412), and [11](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/pull/1927#issuecomment-5188522829); dataset 24 samples [8](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/pull/1927#issuecomment-5188553736) and [10](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/pull/1927#issuecomment-5188613252). ## What changed

- add `bugreport82-0e99ec` using the full, unminimized F1C200s board Simple Route JSON
- add an `AutoroutingPipelineDebugger` fixture
- add a focused characterization test for the `PostProcessingSolver` layer-transition exception
- add the last-step SVG snapshot captured at the failure state

## Why

The default autorouter creates an HD route named `source_net_8_mst3` whose layer transition does not resolve to exactly one via. `PostProcessingSolver` rejects that route and aborts the board route.

The fixture retains all 218 obstacles and 26 connections. Its canonical SRJ SHA-256 matches the original `tsci build --autorouter-dump-srj failed` output: `5023393d62bf7b3845dd3da50fe5cc112a5ddd3ef06bc2b87a3e8ab5fd1c1475`.

## Validation

- `bun run build`
- `bun test --timeout 9999999 tests/bugs/bugreport82-0e99ec.test.ts`

The focused test reproduces the exact exception, asserts the failed solver state, and verifies the SVG snapshot while remaining green for CI.

## Follow-up

- #1925 implements non-ideal fallback output for this reproduction.
- tscircuit/length-matching-solver#39 implements the core solver behavior.

title: fix: complete sample 11 safe trace repair
description: Fixes the issue where Dataset 18 sample 11 fails to complete exact DRC repair due to a bounded trace detour not finishing the repair process after canonicalizing a via.
body:
## Issue

Dataset 18 sample 11 enters exact DRC repair with 16 errors and previously exits with one same-net via error plus one trace contact. After the via is canonicalized, the safe trace phase can replace the remaining trace contact with another one-error state. The parent portfolio rejects and rolls back that state, so the existing bounded trace detour never completes the repair.

## Implementation

Pin [high-density-repair03#50](https://github.com/tscircuit/high-density-repair03/pull/50), stacked on the via canonicalization in [high-density-repair03#49](https://github.com/tscircuit/high-density-repair03/pull/49). The new fix makes safe topology repair transactional: a safe move must reduce the DRC count, otherwise the solver preserves the input and continues its existing bounded copper-detour search across both trace sides.

No new solver or candidate geometry is added.

## Validation

- [Reproduction PR #1900](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/pull/1900): production exact repair shows `16 → 2` before the fixes.
- [Final hosted test run](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/actions/runs/30909982872): all five test shards passed; the same snapshot now shows `16 → 0`.
- [Dataset 18 sample 11 benchmark](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/actions/runs/30910132488): solved in 115.2s and passed relaxed DRC; main solved but failed relaxed DRC.

Developers and coding agents can use bun run debug -- to: discover all pipelines and tasks list retained jobs and traces inspect a task input and its referenced paths run one task from its input run a complete pipeline from an input envelope replay an old jobs task, suffix, or full pipeline Replay clones the source job into .runtimereplays by default and never mutates the retained historical job.  Validation bun test --timeout 30000  625 passed, 10 skipped, 0 failed bun run typecheck bun run format:check bun run build:web CLI smoke checks for catalog and help output end-to-end replay regression proving standalone and old-job task commands leave the source job checkpoint unchanged local browser verification of all three debugger entry points and the SPICE stage modal, with no console errors
body:
## Summary

- split datasheet processing into three authoritative, typed pipelines for component generation, typical applications, and SPICE generation
- make every pipeline stage consume only its declared dependency output and persist exact debug input/output bundles
- reshape SPICE generation into explicit reference discovery, comparison graph, model inference, TSX generation, simulation, comparison, repair, and publication stages
- add server endpoints and UI controls to run a whole pipeline, one isolated step, or a selected step and everything after it
- add a machine-readable local CLI for task inspection, standalone task execution, full pipeline execution, and replaying old jobs at one task, from a task, or end to end
- persist a versioned `pipeline_task_input` envelope containing task identity, complete JSON execution context, and dependency outputs
- run local replays in fresh cloned workspaces with rewritten job-local paths, immutable summaries, event streams, and artifacts while leaving historical jobs untouched
- preserve retained inputs for untouched stages across repeated debug runs and restore the new pipeline snapshots across server restarts
- update architecture documentation and regression coverage for pipeline registries, isolated execution, and non-destructive replay

## Why

The previous workflow mixed component and typical-application work and did not expose a reproducible way to rerun an individual stage. The UI debugger also was not sufficient for a local coding agent: the agent needed a deterministic CLI contract to discover, inspect, and execute the same work from retained inputs.

The new pipeline/task contract gives each stage an explicit input boundary and creates fresh, inspectable invocation artifacts for debugging. Pipelines are now composition only: they pass one task output to the next, while the same task can be invoked directly from its retained input.

## User and developer impact

Completed tasks expose separate Component, Typical application, and SPICE debugger controls. Developers and coding agents can use `bun run debug --` to:

- discover all pipelines and tasks
- list retained jobs and traces
- inspect a task input and its referenced paths
- run one task from its input
- run a complete pipeline from an input envelope
- replay an old job's task, suffix, or full pipeline

Replay clones the source job into `.runtime/replays` by default and never mutates the retained historical job.

## Validation

- `bun test --timeout 30000` — 625 passed, 10 skipped, 0 failed
- `bun run typecheck`
- `bun run format:check`
- `bun run build:web`
- CLI smoke checks for catalog and help output
- end-to-end replay regression proving standalone and old-job task commands leave the source job checkpoint unchanged
- local browser verification of all three debugger entry points and the SPICE stage modal, with no console errors

title: Render native Altium schematic images as SVG
description: Summary extract the native TMetafile and TdxPNGImage payloads stored after Altiums embedded bitmap preview add a bounded EMF-to-SVG renderer for the GDI record subset used by the TI TMDS62LEVM design preserve vector paths, Unicode text, fonts, rotation, alignment, and anisotropic coordinate mapping compose TIs adjacent SRCPAINT 1-bit masks and SRCAND 24-bit bitmap records into transparent native-resolution images prefer native SVGPNG content in schematic serialization while retaining the existing bitmap fallback for malformed or unsupported payloads add focused extraction, rendering, malformed-input, and format-selection coverage  Root cause Altium image streams contain a bitmap preview followed by the original native image payload. The existing parser stopped after the bitmap, so the browser viewer embedded a low-resolution PNG preview. Zooming therefore enlarged fixed pixels even when the source document contained an EMF vector drawing or a higher-resolution PNG.  Impact The affected TI sheets now use their original artwork: sheet 05 renders 5,870 vector paths and 491 text elements as SVG sheets 0508 and 11 retain their vector content sheet 09 uses its two native high-resolution PNGs sheet 10 renders its native transparent bitmap tiles instead of the small preview Unknown EMF operations and invalid native payloads continue to fall back safely to the existing preview behavior.  Validation biome check on all changed source and test files library and site TypeScript checks focused embedded-image tests: 2 passed, 25 assertions Vite production site build ESM, declaration, CLI, and package verification build browser verification using the exact TI ZIP from Downloads: sheet 05 remained crisp and readable after 3 zoom, with no browser console errors
body:
## Summary

- extract the native `TMetafile` and `TdxPNGImage` payloads stored after Altium's embedded bitmap preview
- add a bounded EMF-to-SVG renderer for the GDI record subset used by the TI TMDS62LEVM design
- preserve vector paths, Unicode text, fonts, rotation, alignment, and anisotropic coordinate mapping
- compose TI's adjacent `SRCPAINT` 1-bit masks and `SRCAND` 24-bit bitmap records into transparent native-resolution images
- prefer native SVG/PNG content in schematic serialization while retaining the existing bitmap fallback for malformed or unsupported payloads
- add focused extraction, rendering, malformed-input, and format-selection coverage

## Root cause

Altium image streams contain a bitmap preview followed by the original native image payload. The existing parser stopped after the bitmap, so the browser viewer embedded a low-resolution PNG preview. Zooming therefore enlarged fixed pixels even when the source document contained an EMF vector drawing or a higher-resolution PNG.

## Impact

The affected TI sheets now use their original artwork:

- sheet 05 renders 5,870 vector paths and 491 text elements as SVG
- sheets 05–08 and 11 retain their vector content
- sheet 09 uses its two native high-resolution PNGs
- sheet 10 renders its native transparent bitmap tiles instead of the small preview

Unknown EMF operations and invalid native payloads continue to fall back safely to the existing preview behavior.

## Validation

- `biome check` on all changed source and test files
- library and site TypeScript checks
- focused embedded-image tests: 2 passed, 25 assertions
- Vite production site build
- ESM, declaration, CLI, and package verification build
- browser verification using the exact TI ZIP from Downloads: sheet 05 remained crisp and readable after 3× zoom, with no browser console errors

Developer impact parser callers can catch EasyEdaParseError and inspect stable structured fields SVG callers can use renderEasyEdaSvgWithDiagnostics and opt into remote images, net highlights, or selected-shape metadata contributors can exercise the format from the new CLI and rely on deterministic robustness suites  Validation bun test  53 passing tests, 2,923 assertions bun run typecheck bun run lint bun run format:check git diff --check visually reviewed the new embedded-image SVG snapshot
body:
## Summary

- add structured EasyEDA parse errors with document paths, record tokens, field positions, and configurable safety limits
- render raster data images safely, add an explicit remote-image policy, and expose SVG diagnostics for blocked, unsupported, or partially rendered content
- add opt-in PCB net highlighting and shape-selection metadata
- add focused mutation coverage for every documented Standard token plus deterministic property and fuzz suites
- provide inspect, validate, normalize, round-trip, and SVG CLI commands
- verify the public API in Bun, bundled Node.js ESM, and a browser-targeted bundle
- mark the corresponding ten existing support-checklist items complete

## Why

These capabilities make malformed and unsupported EasyEDA input observable without weakening lossless round trips, make SVG image handling safe by default, and give contributors executable tooling for reviewing parser and serializer behavior across runtimes.

## Developer impact

- parser callers can catch `EasyEdaParseError` and inspect stable structured fields
- SVG callers can use `renderEasyEdaSvgWithDiagnostics` and opt into remote images, net highlights, or selected-shape metadata
- contributors can exercise the format from the new CLI and rely on deterministic robustness suites

## Validation

- `bun test` — 53 passing tests, 2,923 assertions
- `bun run typecheck`
- `bun run lint`
- `bun run format:check`
- `git diff --check`
- visually reviewed the new embedded-image SVG snapshot

Adds an optional `source_trace_id` to `schematic_text`, mirroring the field `schematic_net_label` already carries.

## Why

I'm adding **inline net labels** to [core](https://github.com/tscircuit/core) and [schematic-trace-solver](https://github.com/tscircuit/schematic-trace-solver): a net name drawn parallel to the wire it belongs to — above a horizontal trace, or to the left of a vertical one reading bottom-to-top — instead of a tag anchored to the end of the trace. It keeps the visual line between two pins unbroken on point-to-point signals like `USER_LED_ANODE`.

Because an inline label is rotated, it can't be a `schematic_net_label` — that element is always axis-aligned, with an `anchor_side` and a tag symbol. So it's emitted as a `schematic_text` with `anchor: "center"` and `rotation` of `0` or `-90`.

That leaves two gaps:

- the label is indistinguishable from free-standing text such as a reference designator, and
- consumers have no way to resolve which net it names.

`source_trace_id` closes both. It's what core naturally has on hand — the label is derived from a specific `source_trace` while building the solver input — and it's more reliably available than `source_net_id` here, since a trace labeled via `schDisplayLabel` has no `source_net` at all.

## Verified against a real consumer

Core populates it and it round-trips:

```
inline label source_trace_id: source_trace_0
resolves to source_trace: source_trace_0  ports: 2
refdes text ("U1") source_trace_id: undefined
```

The full core suite (1345 tests) passes with the field populated.

## Notes

- Purely additive and optional — no existing producer or consumer changes behavior.
- `bun test` (287 pass), `bunx tsc --noEmit`, `lint:zod`, and `check-snake-case` are all clean.
- I did **not** regenerate `README.md`. It's stale on `main` for unrelated reasons (`PcbPin1Location`, `pcb_via` source ids, `source_manually_placed_via`), so regenerating pulls in drift that isn't mine — and the closest precedent, #672, didn't touch it either. Happy to include it if you'd rather.
- I considered adding `source_net_id` alongside, for symmetry with `schematic_net_label`. I left it out because it isn't populatable in this case, but say the word if you want both.

title: fix: layer-blind endpoint attribution stamps routed traces with wrong source_trace_id
description: Fixes incorrect attribution of routed traces to source traces due to layer-blind endpoint geometry matching, preventing detection of genuine shorts in PCB design.
body:
## Problem

`getSourceTraceIdForRoutedTrace` recovers the `source_trace_id` for autorouted traces (whose route points carry no `pcb_port_id`s) by testing route endpoints against pads geometrically — **without comparing layers**.

On [tscircuit/nrf52810](https://github.com/tscircuit/nrf52810), the CR2032 holder's `VBAT_N` (GND) terminal is a 10×10mm pad on the **bottom** layer covering much of the board interior. Every **top**-layer routed endpoint above that footprint also "hit" the battery pad, adding a phantom GND port to the endpoint set. That made the exact source-trace match (`sourcePortIds.every(...)`) fail, and the net-based fallback ended in `candidates[0]` — the first source trace in db order across *any* endpoint's net, which was GND's first trace (`.BT1 > .VBAT_N to net.GND`). 27 pcb_traces got stamped with that GND `source_trace_id`, including both 32.768 kHz crystal-pin traces and the antenna node trace.

## Downstream effect: DRC and check-shorts blinded to real shorts

`circuit-json-to-connectivity-map` unions `[pcb_trace_id, source_trace_id]`, so all mis-stamped traces merged with GND into one connectivity group. As a result, two **genuine same-layer trace crossings** produced by the autorouter went undetected:

- X2 crystal `OSC1` × `OSC2` traces crossing at (-1.86, 5.52), top layer
- `U1.ANT` antenna feed × GND trace crossing at (6.02, 3.11), top layer

`checkEachPcbTraceNonOverlapping` skips pairs where `connMap.areIdsConnected(...)` → 0 DRC errors. `tsci check shorts` defines a short as one pixel owned by two connectivity groups → "No shorts detected". The PCB viewer's hover highlight showed the merged group, which is how the short was noticed by a human.

## Fix

Endpoint-geometry attribution now only matches pads and ports on the endpoint's own layer (when the endpoint carries a `layer`). Plated holes still match regardless of layer since they span all layers. Endpoints without layer info keep the old behavior.

## Test

`tests/repros/repro-routed-trace-attribution-ignores-opposite-layer-pad.test.tsx` reproduces the nRF52810 scenario minimally: a large bottom-layer GND pad under two small top-layer pads connected by a signal trace. Without the fix the synthetic routed trace is attributed to the GND source trace; with the fix it resolves to the correct signal trace. Verified red on `main`, green with the fix; `tests/repros`, `tests/features`, `tests/components`, and `tsc --noEmit` all pass.

## Possible follow-ups (not in this PR)

- The autorouter's `pcb_trace_id` already encodes the true connection (`source_trace_51__source_trace_53_mst1_0`, `source_net_1_mst15_0`); resolving attribution from the connection name would avoid geometry entirely.
- The `candidates[0]` fallback can still pick a trace from a different net when endpoint ports span multiple nets; requiring the net to be common to all endpoints would be safer.

title: fix: render chip footprints named by their pads instead of by size
description: Fixes rendering issue where chip footprints named parametrically by their pads were not displayed, resulting in missing components in the 3D view.
body:
Footprinter names a chip either by EIA size (`0402`) or parametrically by
the pads it wants (`res_p0.8656mm_pw0.5657mm_ph0.54mm`). Only the first
form had a 3D model.

`Footprinter3d` has no `case "res"`; named sizes work because a second
switch on `fpJson.imperial` catches them further down. A parametric string
carries no `imperial`, so it matched neither switch and reached
`return null`. An empty model is not an error anywhere downstream --
circuit-json-to-gltf drops such a component silently -- so every passive
authored this way vanished from the 3D view with nothing logged. On the
board this was found on, that was 26 of 36 passives, and every resistor.

`case "cap"` had a worse version of the same gap: no `break`, so a
parametric capacitor fell through into `case "sot235"` and rendered a
3.4 x 2.9 x 1.35mm transistor. A wrong body is worse than a missing one,
because nothing about it looks wrong.

Derive a body from the land pattern when there is no size to look up:

- length is the pad pitch, which tracks body length within 10% across
  every EIA size from 0201 up (0402: 1.02 vs 1.0mm, 0603: 1.65 vs 1.6mm),
- width and height are the pad height less a fillet allowance, since a
  land pattern is drawn 5-30% wider than the part it solders.

Named sizes keep their exact hand-modelled bodies; this only fills the gap
where there was nothing, and the path is keyed on the chip functions
rather than on the presence of a `p`, since a pin header is not a chip.

Also adds `toMm`: footprinter returns `p: 2.54` for a pin header but the
string `"0.8656mm"` for a chip, so a reader that assumes numbers sees
`undefined` for one whole family of footprints.

Tests state the estimate's accuracy rather than assuming it -- each EIA
size's own land pattern fed back in must land within 15% of the real part
-- and pin the fall-through, the untouched named sizes, and the pin header.

title: Fix contribution pagination and historical README updates
description: Fixes pagination for closed pull requests to ensure all relevant contributions are included in scoring and updates the README generation process to prevent overwriting current week data with historical data.
body:
## Summary

- Paginate closed pull requests used for contribution scoring instead of reading only the first 100 results.
- Stop pagination once a full page's oldest `updated_at` is before the reporting window, while continuing at the exact boundary so timestamp ties are not lost.
- Make README current-week replacement explicit and safe by default.
- Let scheduled weekly generation update README, while a dated manual run updates it only when both its start and end cutoffs exactly match the actual current reporting window.
- Add regression coverage for pagination boundaries, multi-page aggregation, Tuesday cutoffs, historical windows, and README block replacement.

## Root cause

`getMergedPRs` requested one page of 100 closed PRs sorted by `updated_at`. On active repositories, valid PRs merged inside the reporting window moved past page 1 as other PRs were updated, so stored analyses remained present but the PRs disappeared from scoring.

Separately, every overview generation unconditionally replaced README's current-week block. A historical manual run could therefore replace the current week with an older report.

## Behavior after this change

- Scoring includes all closed-PR pages that can still contain an in-window merge.
- Pagination remains bounded and does not scan repository history after crossing the reporting-window boundary.
- Scheduled weekly runs continue updating README.
- Historical and monthly generation leave README unchanged.
- A dated manual run can update README only when its complete reporting window is the actual current window.
- Missing or malformed README markers fail clearly rather than silently doing nothing.

## Validation

- `bun test` — 56 pass, 0 fail.
- `node_modules/.bin/tsc --noEmit` — pass.
- `bun run format:check` — pass.
- `bun run build` — pass.
- `git diff --check` — pass.

description: Fixes junction splitting issue in MST branches by ensuring shared-site repairs do not split sites, allowing for valid final-error repair without creating clearance errors.

## Issue

MST branches can contain separate route nodes for one physical same-root via. Moving one node independently splits the junction and creates new clearance errors; freezing the site entirely prevents valid final-error repair.

## Implementation

- Pin the shared-site repair from tscircuit/high-density-repair03#56 (repro: tscircuit/high-density-repair03#55). Broad repair cannot split a site, and targeted repair can move all copies together when clearing the final DRC error.
- Give Pipeline 7's existing constrained exact-repair branch 12 iterations.

## Results

| Sample | Main | PR | Via–via clearance | Via count |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Dataset 18 sample 8 | 24 DRC | 19 DRC | 4 → 0 | 301 → 301 |
| Dataset 24 sample 2 | 75 DRC | 75 DRC | 2 → 0 | 331 → 331 |

Both boards solved in separate hosted runs with concurrency 1: [dataset 18 sample 8](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/actions/runs/31061554653) and [dataset 24 sample 2](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/actions/runs/31061929332).

## Summary

Adds a focused Simple Route JSON (SRJ) reproduction from the Allwinner F1C100S Linux laptop motherboard routing experiment.

The board uses an LCD connector `<breakout autorouter="default">` to route the connector breakout separately. The breakout phase completes, but a later six-route LCD phase fails during the static reachability precheck.

## Reproduction

Source project: `tscircuit/motherboard-allwinner-f1c100s`

```bash
bun run build -- --autorouter-debug \
  --autorouter-debug-dir dist/autorouter-debug-breakout-final \
  --autorouter-dump-srj all \
  --autorouter-timeout 60s --profile
```

The checked-in SRJ is the input to routing phase index `4` (phase ordinal `5`):

- 6 connections
- 889 obstacles
- 4 routing layers
- 87 previously routed traces represented in the obstacle reservations

The preceding LCD connector breakout phase routed 23 connections successfully. The failing input contains `source_trace_178` through `source_trace_183`.

## Observed failure

```text
Static reachability precheck failed: 5 route(s) have no legal path under the current reservation and start-region rules source_trace_182 (50683->50684), source_trace_181 (50685->50686), source_trace_180 (50687->50688), source_trace_179 (50689->50690), source_trace_178 (50691->50692) (capacity-autorouter@0.0.722)
```

The debugger fixture and exact phase-input SRJ are in `fixtures/bug-reports/bugreport83-f1c100s-breakout/`.

## Validation

- Parsed the SRJ with `jq` and Bun JSON import.
- Confirmed the copied SRJ is byte-for-byte identical to the debug dump.

title: Reject unfit candidates before network mapping
description: Rejects outline candidates that cannot fit before constructing their network target mappings, improving efficiency by reducing unnecessary network target builds.
body:
## Summary

- reject outline candidates that cannot fit before constructing their network target mappings
- add a focused regression test that verifies an unfit candidate never builds network targets

## Why

Network target mappings depend on the component, rotation, and packed components—not on whether the current outline segment has enough room. Building those mappings before the geometric fit check wasted the most expensive connectivity work for candidates that were immediately rejected.

On the large weighted-connections repro, the same 100,000-step workload now builds 31,394 target mappings instead of 50,902, skipping 19,508 unnecessary builds. Runtime in the instrumented run decreased from about 69.85s to 55.97s. The repro still reaches the existing global iteration limit; that is separate from this focused change.

## Validation

- `bun run typecheck`
- `bun test tests/outline-candidate-fit-rejection.test.ts lib/OutlineSegmentCandidatePointSolver.test.ts tests/PackSolver2.test.ts tests/PackSolver2_01.test.ts` (6 pass, 2 pre-existing skips)
- Biome format check on the two changed files

title: refactor: one shared triangle/position bounds scan
description: Consolidates multiple bounding box calculations into shared functions to ensure consistent handling of edge cases and reduce code duplication.
body:
## Summary

Follow-up to #175, as flagged there: fold the duplicated bounding-box scans into
the shared `boundsOfTriangles` that PR introduced.

Six copies of the same min/max scan had accumulated:

| Copy | Over |
|---|---|
| `loaders/stl.ts` | `Triangle[]` |
| `loaders/obj.ts` | `Triangle[]` |
| `loaders/glb.ts` | `Triangle[]` |
| `loaders/step.ts` | `Triangle[]` |
| `utils/mesh-scale.ts` | `Triangle[]` |
| `gltf/geometry.ts#getBounds` | flat `[x, y, z, ...]` array |

## Why bother

The scan is trivial, and duplicating it costs little by itself. What it costs is
**the edge cases** — every copy had to re-decide them, and they did not decide
alike:

- **Empty input.** Five copies returned a zero box. The sixth (in
  `triangles-from-loops.ts`, fixed in #175) left `Infinity`, which serializes to
  `null` and reads downstream as a mesh of infinite size.
- **Non-finite vertices**, from a malformed OBJ/STL or a degenerate transform.
  The five `Math.min` copies propagated `NaN` straight into the box. `obj.ts`,
  which compared instead of calling `Math.min`, silently dropped it *per axis* —
  reporting a box that mixes a real extent on one axis with a fabricated one on
  another.

A rule that has to be re-remembered at each copy is one the next loader will
miss, so both rules now live in one accumulator that the public helpers share:
bounds are taken over the finite points, and a stream with no finite points
reports the zero box.

## What changed

- `boundsOfTriangles` and a new `boundsOfPositions` share a small internal
  accumulator that owns the empty-input rule.
- `getBounds` keeps its name, signature and call sites, and delegates to
  `boundsOfPositions`.
- The five private `calculateBoundingBox` copies are gone.

Net **−150 lines**.

## Behaviour

Unchanged for well-formed input. Two deliberate differences from the code being
removed, both at inputs that were already malformed:

| Input | Before | Now |
|---|---|---|
| vertex with `NaN`/`Infinity` | `NaN` bounds (`Math.min` copies) or one axis dropped (`obj.ts`) | point skipped whole |
| positions array not a multiple of 3 | reads past the end; `undefined` makes those axes `NaN` | trailing partial triple ignored |

`NaN` in a box is worth avoiding specifically: it reaches a glTF accessor's
`min`/`max`, and `NaN` there is invalid glTF.

## Testing

The existing suite is the real guard — every loader's bounds are asserted
through it, and all 103 still pass. Added direct tests for the shared helpers:
both empty cases, the flat-array triple layout, the trailing partial triple,
non-finite points, and a stream whose points are all non-finite.

110 pass / 0 fail, plus type-check, format-check and playwright.

title: fix(jscad): put JSCAD-plan geometry in the same frame as every other loader
description: Fixes the JSCAD-plan loader to align its geometry frame with other loaders, resolving a 180-degree rotation issue in rendering.
body:
## Summary

The JSCAD-plan loader put its geometry in a different frame from every other
loader, so `model_jscad` components rendered rotated 180° about X relative to
the OBJ/STEP models beside them — and relative to their own `position` offset.

## The bug

`loadJscadPlan` moved plan geometry into the Scene3D frame with
`rotateX(-PI/2)`, which sends **Circuit +Y → scene −Z**. Every other route into
that scene sends **Circuit +Y → scene +Z**:

| Path | Circuit +Y lands at |
|---|---|
| OBJ loader (`OBJ_Z_UP_TO_Y_UP`) | +Z |
| board mesh | +Z |
| `cad_component.position` (applied on the node) | +Z |
| **JSCAD plan loader** | **−Z** |

Geometry offsets and node offsets are applied in different places, so they only
agree if the loader and the node placement share one frame. They didn't: moving
a shape +4mm inside the plan and moving the component +4mm with `position`
landed **8mm apart**.

## What changed

**One shared basis.** `loadJscadPlan` now uses a named
`CIRCUIT_Z_UP_TO_SCENE_Y_UP` config, identical to `OBJ_Z_UP_TO_Y_UP` by
construction — JSCAD geometry has to share a frame with the OBJ models it sits
beside.

X is deliberately left un-negated. `GLTFBuilder.convertMeshToGLTFOrientation`
applies the single canonical X-mirror (and winding flip) to *every* mesh at
export, so mirroring here as well would move JSCAD geometry alone. The constant
is named `..._TO_SCENE_...`, not `..._TO_GLTF_...`, to keep that distinction
visible at the use site.

**Bounds measured from the triangles the mesh ships.** The geometry stays Z-up
while only the triangles are remapped, so measuring the source `Geom3` describes
the wrong frame. The alternative — measure the source and move its box into the
new frame — is exact only while the transform keeps axes aligned: a box survives
a transform intact only if the geometry fills it, so rotating the box of a
cylinder inflates its empty corners by √2 instead of following the shape.
Scanning the transformed triangles is exact for any transform and costs one pass
over vertices that were just built. It is also what the STL/OBJ/GLB/STEP loaders
and `rotateMesh` already do.

**A shared `boundsOfTriangles`** (`lib/utils/bounding-box.ts`), zero-safe for
empty input — an unguarded min/max scan leaves `Infinity`/`-Infinity`, which
serializes to `null` where every other loader reports a zero box.
`triangles-from-loops.ts` had a private copy with exactly that hole and now uses
the shared one.

## Follow-up (intentionally not in this PR)

`boundsOfTriangles` is the deduplication target for the copies already in the
tree, but folding them in here would bury a behavioural fix under a
tree-wide refactor. Left for a follow-up PR:

- five identical private `calculateBoundingBox(triangles)` copies —
  `loaders/stl.ts`, `loaders/obj.ts`, `loaders/glb.ts`, `loaders/step.ts`,
  `utils/mesh-scale.ts`. All are already zero-safe, so this is pure dedupe with
  no behaviour change.
- `gltf/geometry.ts#getBounds(positions: number[])` computes the same thing over
  a flat position array for the glTF accessor `min`/`max`; it can share the core
  with a small adapter.

(`cad-mesh-placement.ts#getBoardContactBounds` is *not* a target — it scans a
filtered subset of vertices, those on the board-contact plane.)

## Testing

New tests, each verified to fail against the pre-fix loader:

- a plan translated +4 in Circuit Y must span +3..+5 in scene Z — was −5..−3
- geometry offsets and `cad_component.position` offsets must agree per axis. The
  **Y** case failed before this change; X and Z are kept as guards so a fix
  can't over-correct into mirroring X twice
- the `CIRCUIT_Z_UP_TO_SCENE_Y_UP` basis must equal `OBJ_Z_UP_TO_Y_UP`

Tests covering the bounds path:

- reported bounds must equal the bounds of the triangles shipped with them —
  including for a **cylinder**, which does not fill its own bounding box and so
  distinguishes measuring the shape from moving its box
- a plan producing no geometry reports a zero box, not Infinities

Full suite: 103 pass / 0 fail, plus type-check, format-check and playwright.

## Snapshot

`jscad-plan-with-electronics` is refreshed: the enclosure walls now sit the same
way round as the board they enclose.

title: Prefer shorter valid schematic label detours
description: Generates compound candidates for simple five-segment elbows instead of stacking local four-point notches, ranks valid reroutes by Manhattan length, rendered-label overlap count, and point count, and adds an exact regression test for the U1.pin1 route from core repro148.
body: ## Summary - generate a compound candidate for simple five-segment elbows instead of stacking local four-point notches - rank valid reroutes by Manhattan length, then rendered-label overlap count, then point count - reject simple candidates that move an existing net-label anchor or transfer the trace into more rendered labels - add an exact regression test for the U1.pin1 route from core repro148 ## Root cause The label rerouter only generated local detours around the label currently being processed. In the DRV8323 case, repeated passes stacked those detours into the long U-shaped VM route. The first fix generated the missing simple route, but candidate selection still prioritized removing a generated label overlap over path length. In core repro148 that made U1.pin1 take a longer four-point notch around a GND label that core does not ultimately render. ## Fix `generateSimpleElbowDetourCandidates` produces the missing compound route by moving the elbow transition and then shifting the colliding segment beyond the neighboring label. `SingleOverlapSolver` admits that route only when it: 1. reduces overlaps across the complete rendered-label set; 2. preserves existing label anchors; 3. has the same Manhattan length as a standard detour candidate; 4. uses fewer points than that standard candidate. All candidates then use the same deterministic ordering: shortest path first, fewer label overlaps second, and fewer points third. The existing target-label, obstacle, other-trace, retry, and solver-lifecycle checks remain in place. There are no circuit IDs or caller-controlled strategy flags. ## Result | Case | Before | After | Collision result | | --- | ---: | ---: | --- | | DRV8323 VM rail | 14 points / 14.322 length | 6 points / 12.002 length | no overlap | | DRV8323 neighboring GND | 8 points / 10.582 length | 6 points / 7.382 length | same existing C_CP/CPL overlap | | Full DRV8323 output | 38 points / 50.224 length | 28 points / 44.704 length | same single overlap | | Core repro148 U1.pin1 | 10-point label notch | original 6-point route | no added rendered collision | ## Snapshot audit Every changed existing snapshot was compared by path length, point count, collision identity, crossings, and visual geometry: - `bug-report-20260806T093501Z`: 5.52 shorter and 10 fewer points; final overlap set is unchanged - `bug-report-20260706T220324Z`: two routes are 1.362 and 1.15 shorter; no added overlap - `example33`: same length with 8 to 6 points and 6 to 4 bends - `bug-report-20260706T213649Z`: one route drops from 8 to 6 points at the same length; an equivalent six-point route now remains at its upstream position instead of being replaced by an equal-score candidate; length, bends, crossings, and label-overlap count do not worsen - `bug-report-20260707T092615Z`: unchanged from `main` - new `repro-core-148-pin1-label-detour` fixture: asserts the exact clean six-point U1.pin1 path ## Validation - linked the local solver build into current core and regenerated repro148; the U1.pin1 notch is gone - `bun test` — 170 passed, 4 skipped, 0 failed - `bunx tsc --noEmit` - `bun run build` - `bun run format:check` - `git diff --check`

title: Relocate rail labels around crossing traces
description: Fixes rail label placement issues when crossing different-net trace segments, ensuring proper clearance and avoiding collisions in schematic layouts.
body:
## Summary

- generate clearance-shifted rail corner candidates from crossing different-net trace segments
- reconsider rail labels already placed on a corner when that placement is crossed
- keep short existing signal routes by moving the obstructing rail and its attached label
- add collision assertions to the merged RP2040 pin 45 bug report

## Root cause

The rail net-label placement solver could shift a rail around a chip, but it did not derive shift candidates from a trace crossing the label. In the RP2040 repro, the V3V3 label therefore remained fixed in front of the short pin 50-to-pin 45 V1V1 route. The later trace collision solver detoured V1V1 around V3V3 and into the ADC_VREF label.

## Fix

For a vertical rail label crossed by another net, the solver now derives left and right x-coordinates from the crossing segment, the label width, and the existing 0.1 schematic label/trace clearance. Each candidate reroutes the rail's vertical segment and moves its attached label. Existing candidate validation still rejects chip, text, trace, and net-label collisions, so there are no component- or net-specific cases.

The resulting RP2040 layout moves the V3V3 rail outward to approximately x=3.161 and preserves the original four-point V1V1 route. The final regression assertion verifies that no different-net trace crosses any net label.

## Snapshot changes

- The RP2040 bug-report snapshot shows the intended V3V3 relocation and short pin 45 trace.
- `example01` also improves: its VCC label previously remained mid-segment because its ordinary corner candidates collided. The new generic candidate shifts the rail from x=-1.4 to x=-1.075, places VCC on the upper corner, and leaves 0.1 clearance from the EN trace.

## Validation

- `bunx tsc --noEmit`
- `bun run format:check`
- `bun test` — 168 passed, 4 skipped, 0 failed

## Problem

After the canonical schematic net-label bounds fix landed in `@tscircuit/core`, the complete RP2040 repro170 input exposes a trace/label collision in the schematic trace solver.

The V1V1 trace connecting U1 pin 50 (`DVDD1`) to U1 pin 45 (`VREG_VOUT`) detours below the nearby labels, then returns upward through the `ADC_VREF` label connected to pin 43. In solver IDs, `schematic_port_49-schematic_port_44` intersects `connectivity_net17` on path segment 5.

The earlier `bug-report-20260805T061316Z` input did not expose this because it was captured before core consistently supplied canonical rendered label widths. With the older, smaller label obstacles, the solver selected a shorter non-colliding V1V1 route.

## What this adds

- The complete, unminimized repro170 solver input regenerated from the latest core `main` at `2a61efbd`.
- A standard `SchematicTracePipelineSolver` SVG snapshot test.
- A `PipelineDebugger` page for interactive stage inspection.
- The generated solver snapshot showing the current routing result.

The input retains all 13 chips, 18 direct connections, and 4 net connections so the surrounding routing and label-placement constraints remain faithful to core.

## Impact

This gives the trace-solver repository a faithful standalone reproduction of the route returned by core after the canonical label-width fix. A future solver change can now be developed and visually reviewed against the exact input that creates the pin 45/50 V1V1 collision.

This PR adds the reproduction only; it does not change solver behavior.

## Validation

title: Preserve shared same-root via sites during repair
description: Fixes clearance errors caused by independent movement of colocated same-root via nodes during repair processes.
body:
## Issue

MST branches can contain separate route nodes for one physical same-root via. Moving one node independently splits the junction and creates new clearance errors.

## Implementation

Treat colocated same-root via nodes as one site. Broad repair cannot move one copy independently. When one DRC error remains, targeted repair may translate every copy together; the existing candidate check accepts that move only if it clears the final error.

## Verification

The same three-panel snapshot now labels the fixed output and shows both copies colocated in a 100× close-up. Typecheck, formatting, and all 54 tests pass.

Stacked on #55.

title: Reproduce shared same-root via site splitting
description: Adds a focused snapshot test to reproduce the scenario where two MST route branches share the same physical via site, demonstrating the independent movement of duplicated via nodes during force repair.
body:
## Issue

Two MST route branches can represent the same physical via site. During force repair, those duplicated via nodes can be moved independently, splitting one electrical junction into nearby vias.

## Reproduction

title: Follow RP2350 hardware design guide for crystal/BOOTSEL/inductor, and fix snapshot reproducibility
description: Updates the RP2350 design to use specific components as per the hardware design guide and resolves issues with PCB snapshot reproducibility across different architectures.
body:
Two independent things, one commit each.

## 1. Datasheet-specified parts

The buck-converter network here was already correct. These are the remaining spots where the module used a generic part, or omitted one that [Hardware design with RP2350](https://datasheets.raspberrypi.com/rp2350/hardware-design-with-rp2350.pdf) (RP-008280-DS) specifically calls for.

| | before | after | why |
|---|---|---|---|
| Crystal | `X322512MSB4SI` | `ABM8-272-T3` | The guide names this exact part (Pico and Pico 2 use it) and warns that deviating requires re-testing across temperature |
| Load caps | 18pF | 15pF | Suits the ABM8's 10pF load capacitance once ~3pF of board parasitics are added |
| XOUT damping | *absent* | `R_XOUT` 1k | Without it the 50Ω-max-ESR crystal is overdriven at IOVDD = 3.3V |
| BOOTSEL | button shorts `QSPI_SS` to GND | `R_BOOTSEL` 1k in series | `QSPI_SS` is a live flash signal (R6 in the guide) |
| `L_CORE` | generic 3.3µH, `0805` | `AOTA-B201610S3R3-101-T`, `0806` | The regulator is sensitive to coil winding direction relative to `C_VREG_OUT`, so the guide calls for this polarity-marked reeled part |

Both new parts are stocked on JLCPCB (C20625731, C42411119) and their footprints match the JLCPCB library at 100% copper. Three tests cover the crystal choice, the damping resistor sitting in the XOUT path, the BOOTSEL series resistor, and the inductor MPN. BOM table updated.

## 2. Why PCB snapshots are x86_64-only

`72177b7` checked the PCB snapshots in as "Linux-generated" on the theory that the autorouter takes different paths on macOS. **The OS isn't the variable.** Running `tsci snapshot --update` on one commit, same Bun 1.3.14, same frozen lockfile, on two GitHub runners:

| | `index-pcb` | `index-schematic` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Linux **x86_64** | `b1591158` | `8aa18d70` |
| Linux **arm64** | `f6e41275` | `8aa18d70` |
| macOS **arm64** | `f6e41275` | `8aa18d70` |

Linux arm64 and macOS arm64 agree **exactly**, and both disagree with x86_64. The split is **CPU architecture** — most likely ARM contracting `a*b+c` into a fused multiply-add, moving a cost by one ulp and flipping tie-breaks in the router's search. Placement is byte-identical either way and the via count matches; only the routes differ. Schematic snapshots are identical everywhere.

So `72177b7`'s practical guidance (take CI's output) was right, but the stated reason wasn't — and that matters, because it sends anyone on Apple Silicon hunting a macOS problem that doesn't exist. README now states the real constraint.

This also removes a source of drift that made the above harder to see: CI installed with a bare `bun install`, and the four workflows ran **three different Bun versions** (1.3.5, 1.3.1, `latest`), none matching what developers run. All four now pin Bun 1.3.14 and install `--frozen-lockfile`.

### Possibly worth an upstream issue

`@tscircuit/capacity-autorouter` not being architecture-deterministic is arguably a bug in its own right — it means snapshot-based PCB testing can't be verified on Apple Silicon dev machines at all. If the cost functions were made FMA-stable (or tie-breaks were made to depend on a discrete key rather than a float comparison), snapshots would be portable everywhere.

## Verification

`test`, `type-check`, `format-check` pass. PCB snapshots are CI's own x86_64 output, so `snapshot` should now pass too.

title: feat(group): accept `placementDrcChecksDisabled` on subcircuits and boards
description: Adds support for placementDrcChecksDisabled on subcircuits and boards, allowing users to bypass placement design rule checks for specific subcircuits during autorouting.
body:
## Problem

When autorouting is skipped because of placement errors, core emits:

> Autorouting was skipped because N PCB placement errors were found. Fix the placement errors or set `placementDrcChecksDisabled` to true to route anyway.

Following that advice does nothing. `placementDrcChecksDisabled` lives only on `PlatformConfig`, so `<board placementDrcChecksDisabled>` is stripped by zod with no error and the board stays unrouted — the user is left with pads, no traces, and a message pointing at a setting they cannot reach.

## Fix

Add the key to `subcircuitGroupProps` (inherited by `boardProps`). No core change is needed: `Board_doInitialPcbPlacementDesignRuleChecks` already resolves it as

```ts
board.root?.platform?.placementDrcChecksDisabled ??
  board.getInheritedProperty("placementDrcChecksDisabled")
```

so the prop reaches the gate as soon as it survives parsing. Being a subcircuit prop rather than board-only is the useful shape here — it lets you exempt one dense subcircuit (a fine-pitch QFN escape, say) without disabling placement checks for the whole board.

## Tests

`tests/board.test.ts` — asserts the prop survives `boardProps.parse`. Full suite: 414 pass.

## Related

tscircuit/cli#4071 makes `tsci build --ignore-placement-drc` lift the same gate; today it only filters the diagnostics while leaving the board unrouted.

title: Fix parent routing through breakout traces
description: Fixes routing issues where parent traces incorrectly treated breakout copper as unrelated obstacles, ensuring stable routing behavior for child and parent nets in PCB designs.
body:
## Summary

- preserve stable `pcb_breakout_point_id` values in child and parent Simple Route JSON inputs
- route nets explicitly declared as direct `<breakout>` children in the breakout phase
- keep inferred component-connection nets on their existing enclosing-group routing behavior
- add Game Boy-like passing regression coverage for parent routing through a pre-routed MCU breakout
- include the minimal parent/child obstacle repro moved from #3018

## Root cause

Parent routing did not receive the same point identity used at the pre-routed breakout boundary, so the existing breakout copper could be treated as an unrelated obstacle instead of a continuation target. In addition, explicitly declared internal breakout nets were deferred to a later routing phase because breakout plans always used an empty `nets` array. Those nets then had to route around the already completed breakout copper and could exhaust the autorouter iteration limit.

## Impact

A dense MCU can be routed inside a virtual breakout first, after which board-level signals attach to the breakout boundary without physical pin headers. Explicit breakout-owned power nets are solved with the MCU routing, while inferred nets retain the previous behavior.

The minimal repro remains intentionally marked `test.failing` for the related different-net parent/child overlap. Its flat control now routes successfully with both connections visible to one routing phase; the nested case reaches its snapshot and shows the parent trace crossing preserved child copper. This separate overlap is not claimed as fixed by this PR.

## Validation

## Summary

- represent direct cross-subcircuit traces with one visible endpoint as single-pin net connections in the schematic solver input

## Root cause

A direct trace crossing a subcircuit boundary has only one endpoint visible in each schematic solver scope. Core only emitted explicit direct connections when at least two endpoints were visible, so the cross-boundary label was missing from the solver input. The label was inserted after routing, which allowed another trace to route through its eventual bounds.

## Fix

Core now emits a single-pin net connection when a two-port direct trace crosses a subcircuit boundary and exactly one endpoint is visible in the current scope. The label text is resolved through the same shared helper used by the post-routing fallback path, covering both explicit trace names such as `LCD_CS` and generated endpoint labels such as `J_RIGHT_GP17`.

The implementation is scoped by source-port and subcircuit identity; it does not contain circuit-specific names, component IDs, or coordinates.

title: Detect and constrain decoupling capacitor traces during source render
description: Automatically detects two-pin capacitors connected to power and ground, applying a default trace-length constraint for decoupling capacitors during source rendering.
body:
## Summary

- Automatically detect two-pin capacitors whose power-side port directly shares a trace with an eligible chip power-input pin and whose other port connects to ground.
- Apply the existing 1 mm default decoupling trace-length constraint before source traces render.
- Accept a direct ground port or named ground net, but do not infer decoupling through a shared power net.
- Honor `requiresPower`, inferred common power-pin labels, and explicit `shouldHaveDecouplingCapacitor` overrides.
- Preserve explicit `maxDecouplingTraceLength` values and leave unrelated traces unconstrained.

## Architecture

Detection is owned by `Capacitor.doInitialSourceRender()`. At that point, `CreateTracesFromProps` has created connectivity instances, while `SourceTraceRender` has not yet run. The capacitor asks its two `Port` instances whether they are connected to power or ground using `isConnectedToPower()` and `isConnectedToGround()`.

Power connectivity is intentionally strong: the capacitor port and eligible chip power pin must occur on the same trace. Separate traces that merely terminate at the same `net.VCC` do not qualify. Ground connectivity may terminate directly at a ground port or ground net.

The capacitor source component is inserted with the inferred `max_decoupling_trace_length`, and the existing trace render phase propagates that value to attached `source_trace.max_length` records. `Group` remains unchanged, and unresolved trace selectors continue through the normal trace diagnostic flow.

This is an alternative implementation to #2955 and implements the behavior described in the [automatic decoupling capacitor detection RFC](https://github.com/tscircuit/rfc/blob/main/rfcs/2026-07-31-automatic-decoupling-capacitor-detection-and-enforcement.md).

## Impact

Qualifying decoupling capacitors receive `max_decoupling_trace_length: 1` by default, and their attached traces receive `max_length: 1`. Capacitors connected only between shared power and ground nets are not automatically designated.

## Validation

- `bunx tsc --noEmit`
- `bun run build`
- focused direct-connectivity, shared-net exclusion, opt-out, and existing trace-length regression tests
- full suite: 1305 passed, 31 skipped, 0 failed

title: fix(build): `--ignore-placement-drc` should unblock autorouting, not just hide it
description: Fixes autorouting failure when placement errors are present by allowing the --ignore-placement-drc flag to enable routing despite placement errors.
body:
## Problem

Placement DRC is not report-only. Core skips autorouting for any subcircuit that carries a placement error (`shouldSkipAutoroutingBecauseOfPlacementErrors`), so `--ignore-placement-drc` filtered the diagnostics while the board stayed unrouted — and the build summary cheerfully printed `Ignored DRC 1 (placement: 1)` on the way out.

The emitted error tells you how to override the gate:

> Autorouting was skipped because 1 PCB placement error was found. Fix the placement errors or set `placementDrcChecksDisabled` to true to route anyway.

but that setting is unreachable from every surface a user would try:

| attempt | routes? |
|---|---|
| `tsci build` | no |
| `tsci build --ignore-placement-drc` (prints `Ignored DRC 1 (placement: 1)`) | **no** |
| `<board placementDrcChecksDisabled>` | no — the key is on `PlatformConfig`, not `boardProps`, so zod strips it silently |
| `tscircuit.config.json` | no — not in the schema |
| `CircuitRunner({ platform: { placementDrcChecksDisabled: true } })` | **yes** |

The last row is the control: the mechanism works, it just had no path from the CLI.

The failure mode is nasty because one unrelated placement error silences routing for the whole subcircuit, and the derived `pcb_port_not_connected_error` / `pcb_trace_missing_error` then point at innocent nets rather than at the placement problem. I lost a while to this on a 4-layer board where 32 escape pads sat inside a QFN courtyard: the build "succeeded" in 20s with pads and no traces.

## Fix

`commandPlatformConfig` in `cli/build/register.ts` already translates CLI flags into `PlatformConfig` (`--disable-pcb`, `--routing-disabled`, `--disable-parts-engine`). This adds `--ignore-placement-drc` → `placementDrcChecksDisabled`, so the flag lifts the gate as well as filtering the report.

Scoped to placement deliberately: the other `--ignore-*-drc` categories really are report-only, and mapping them to `*DrcChecksDisabled` would change which checks run at all.

## Tests

`tests/cli/build/build-ignore-placement-drc-routes.test.ts` — a board with one out-of-board component plus one unrelated routable trace:

- default build: placement error present, `Autorouting was skipped`, 0 `pcb_trace`
- `--ignore-placement-drc`: no autorouting error, 1 `pcb_trace`

Reproduces on this repo's pinned core (0.0.1453), so it is longstanding rather than a recent regression.

## Follow-ups not in this PR

1. Accept `placementDrcChecksDisabled` on `boardProps` (and/or `tscircuit.config.json`) — that is where the error message sends people. Otherwise the message should name something reachable.
2. When routing is skipped by the gate, suppress the derived `pcb_port_not_connected_error` / `pcb_trace_missing_error` for nets the router never attempted.

title: Use original pad geometry for relaxed DRC
description: Fixes relaxed DRC evaluation by preserving original pad geometry and connectivity for sibling pads, eliminating false terminal errors.
body:
## Summary

Stacked on #1969.

Relaxed DRC was rebuilding SMT pads from srjWithPointPairs. Rotated pads are decomposed there into shifted, axis-aligned routing fragments, so the evaluator could select a fragment as the physical pad and report false missing-terminal errors.

The corrected invariant restores both halves of the original circuit model together: physical pad geometry and original logical net connectivity always come from inputSrj. Routed point-pair traces are still evaluated jointly with any preloaded traces.

Keeping original connectivity is required for colocated or sibling pads on one net. Without it, dataset-18 sample 10 incorrectly treated pcb_port_17 as foreign to the pcb_port_20-to-pcb_port_12 route and emitted the same accidental-contact error twice. The route produced by this branch and PR #1941 is byte-identical; only that incomplete connectivity model caused the apparent regression.

The repro fixture naturally changes from shifted square fragments with missing-connection annotations to the original rotated pads with no false terminal errors. Sample 10 now exposes 6 pre-repair findings and the exact repair stage resolves all of them to 0.

## Validation

All local test files and samples were run serially.

- bun test tests/evaluate-relaxed-drc-original-connectivity.test.ts --timeout 9999999
- bun test tests/evaluate-relaxed-drc-original-pad-geometry.test.ts --timeout 9999999
- bun test tests/evaluate-relaxed-drc-joint-traces.test.ts --timeout 9999999
- bun test tests/pipeline7-relaxed-drc-evaluator.test.ts --timeout 9999999

- bun test tests/features/same-net-via-clearance-repair-visual.test.ts

The full dataset-18 benchmark with a 2000-second sample timeout completed 100% of samples and passed relaxed DRC on 31.3% (samples 1, 5, 10, 11, and 12). This exactly matches PR #1941's same-timeout pass/fail set and sample-by-sample via counts.

title: Repair terminal traces crossing SMT pads
description: Fixes autorouting failure when terminal-side traces remain on foreign SMT pads due to improper layer handling during repairs.
body:
## Issue

A terminal-side trace can remain on foreign SMT pads when the valid repair requires moving its complete span to another layer. Local layer moves consumed the repair candidate window before that escape was evaluated.

## Implementation

Pin tscircuit/high-density-repair03#58 (reproduction: tscircuit/high-density-repair03#57). For trace-vs-obstacle errors, complete-span layer escapes are now tried before local layer moves. Other DRC errors keep their existing candidate order.

## Results

- Dataset 24 sample 9: DRC failed on the logical base; [the fix passes DRC](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/pull/1941#issuecomment-5200705163).
- Dataset 18 sample 16: still solves and still fails DRC, so this fix does not claim to cover that SMT-pad shape ([result](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/pull/1941#issuecomment-5200747060)).
- Regression check: all previously passing samples remain passing—[dataset 18 samples 1, 5, 10, 11, 12](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/pull/1941#issuecomment-5200767505) and [dataset 24 samples 6, 8, 10](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/pull/1941#issuecomment-5200878895).

title: Cache target mappings and raise packing iteration budget
description: Caches rotated pad offsets and network target mappings by rotation while packing a component, and raises PackSolver2s iteration budget from 100,000 to 500,000 to accommodate larger boards.
body:
## Summary

- cache rotated pad offsets and network target mappings by rotation while packing a component
- share that cache across every outline-segment candidate created by `SingleComponentPackSolver`
- clear the cache for each component-placement run
- raise `PackSolver2`'s iteration budget from 100,000 to 500,000
- run the large weighted-connections repro as a completion regression

## Why

Each `OutlineSegmentCandidatePointSolver` previously rebuilt the same mapping from the component's pads to already-packed target pads. That mapping depends on the component, its rotation, and the fixed set of packed components—not the outline segment—so viable segments repeated expensive pad and weighted-connection scans.

The large repro also could not finish under the inherited 100,000-step limit. `PackSolver2` counts nested candidate and optimizer work against its parent budget, and the captured 218-component board needs about 246,892 parent steps. The increased limit gives large valid boards enough room to complete.

## Impact

- The same 100,000-step partial workload decreased from about 55.97s on `main` to 30.22s with the cache.
- 31,394 viable candidates collapse to only 504 component/rotation mapping constructions.
- With the 300,000-step budget, the full repro packs all 218 components successfully in about 83.36s instead of failing after 126 components.

## Validation

- `bun run typecheck`
- `bun test tests/network-target-mapping-cache.test.ts tests/outline-candidate-fit-rejection.test.ts tests/PackSolver2.test.ts tests/PackSolver2_01.test.ts` — 7 pass, 0 fail
- `bun test tests/repros/repro-large-weighted-connections.test.ts` — 2 pass, 0 fail
- Biome formatting and `git diff --check`

title: Index weighted connection lookups
description: Builds an adjacency index for explicitly weighted pad connections, enabling constant-time lookups for strong connections and improving performance significantly during candidate evaluations.
body:
## Summary

- build an adjacency index for explicitly weighted pad connections
- build a set for pads that reject weak connections
- cache the index by the immutable weighted-connections array
- use constant-time lookups in both `isStrongConnection` and `getStronglyConnectedPadIds`
- cover index reuse and multi-pad weighted groups with regression tests

## Root cause

`isStrongConnection` previously scanned the entire `weightedConnections` array twice for every pad-pair check: once to find an explicit pair and again to determine whether either pad rejects weak connections.

Candidate generation and scoring call this function inside nested component/pad loops. On the captured large board, that repeatedly scanned 670 weighted connections across tens of thousands of candidate evaluations.

## Impact

For the same 100,000-step workload in `repro-large-weighted-connections.test.ts`:

- before: about 55.97 seconds
- after: about 3.95 seconds
- improvement: about 14× faster

The indexed run preserves the same solver state at the existing limit: 126 components packed and `failed=true`. Raising the parent iteration budget remains a separate change.

## Validation

- `bun run typecheck`
- `bun test` — 127 pass, 11 pre-existing skips, 0 fail
- focused weighted-connection tests — 7 pass, 0 fail
- large repro benchmark — 100,000 iterations and 126 packed components in about 3.95 seconds
- Biome formatting and `git diff --check`

title: Fix duplicate subcircuit child names
description: Fixes duplicate child names in subcircuits PowerBoost_MT3608 and AudioAmplifier3W_PAM8403 to prevent integration errors in larger boards.
body:
## Summary

- remove the explicit `<port>` children from `PowerBoost_MT3608` and `AudioAmplifier3W_PAM8403`
- keep the natural internal net names such as `GND`, `VSYS`, and `AUDIO_PWM`
- leave every internal net private by default
- use tscircuit's existing `exposedNets` property for selective exposure and `exposeNets` when all internal nets are intentionally exposed
- update the tests, usage documentation, and affected snapshots

## Root cause

Both subcircuits declared a `<net>` and a `<port>` with the same name as immediate children. When integrated into a larger board, tscircuit reported errors such as `Multiple immediate children found with name "GND"` and equivalent errors for `VSYS`, `VBUS`, battery, and audio nets.

The duplicate-name problem is solved by removing the redundant port wrappers. The nets do not need aliases such as `GND_INTERNAL` because tscircuit already provides opt-in subcircuit net exposure.

## Usage

Expose only the nets required by the parent circuit:

```tsx
<PowerBoost_MT3608
  exposedNets={["BAT_POS", "BAT_SWITCHED", "VBUS", "VSYS", "GND"]}
/>

<AudioAmplifier3W_PAM8403
  exposedNets={["AUDIO_PWM", "V3V3", "VSYS", "GND"]}
/>
```

The power circuit's `BAT_POS` and `BAT_SWITCHED` nets must both be exposed when the power switch is placed in the parent circuit. Consumers can use `exposeNets` instead when intentionally exposing every internal net.

## Impact

By default, no internal net leaves either subcircuit. Consumers explicitly choose which nets are bridged into the parent circuit, avoiding accidental API exposure while preserving normal electrical net names.

The regression tests verify:

- immediate child names remain unique
- the subcircuits contain no fixed public port wrappers
- both exposure properties are forwarded
- each selected net receives an actual child-to-parent source-net bridge
- both complete circuits render without errors

## Validation

- `bunx tsc --noEmit` — passed locally and in GitHub Actions
- `bun test` — 17 passed, 0 failed, 140 assertions
- `bun run build:lib` — ESM and declaration builds passed
- targeted PCB and schematic snapshots regenerated with the latest lockfile
- GitHub Actions test, type-check, format-check, and snapshot jobs — passed
- `git diff --check` — passed
