body:
## Summary

Adds the **TI AM62L32** low-power dual-core Cortex-A53 Sitara SoC — the processor on the [TMDS62LEVM](https://www.ti.com/tool/TMDS62LEVM) evaluation module — as a chip component.

- **`AM62L32BOGHAANBR`** — the exact orderable variant on the TMDS62LEVM (the EVM user's guide SPRUJG8 lists `AM62L32BOGHAANB`; this is its reel-packaged orderable, ACTIVE on TI.com)
- **`AM62L32`** — short-name export with a `footprintVariant` selector (`fccsp_373_anb`), following the existing `CC3235SF` pattern
- Exported from `lib/chips/index.tsx`, root `index.ts` (`TiChipComponents`), and listed in the README chip table

## Pin map

All **373 balls** extracted from the AM62L datasheet ([SPRSPA1B](https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/am62l.pdf), Table 5-1 Pin Attributes, ANB package). Each pin carries two aliases: its **ball ID** (`A1`, `AC23`, …) and its **primary ball name** (`UART0_TXD`, `DSI0_TXCLKP`, …). Repeated power/ground names are deduplicated (`VSS1`–`VSS97`, `VDD_CORE1`–`VDD_CORE14`, `VDDSHV0_1`/`VDDSHV0_2`, …) so every label is unique. Spot-verified 16 balls against verbatim datasheet pairs; ball total matches the package exactly (373), with zero extraction conflicts.

## Footprint

Per the datasheet ANB0373A package drawing / land-pattern example:
- 23×23 via-channel array (rows A–AC, JEDEC letter skips), 0.5 mm pitch
- 373 × Ø0.3 mm circular pads (datasheet land-pattern example)
- 11.9 mm body silkscreen outline, A1 corner dot, 12.4 mm courtyard

The chip builds cleanly via `tsci build` (`dist/lib/chips/AM62L32BOGHAANBR/circuit.json`: 373 smtpads, 373 ports, 0 errors).

## tscircuit devDependency bump

`^0.0.2139` → `^0.0.2246`: the pinned version fails at import on any fresh install (`getRotationBetweenPcbPin1Locations` missing from the resolved `circuit-json`), so `tsci build` was broken on clean clones — reproduced on an unmodified checkout. With the bump, the full build passes (110 circuits, same pre-existing warnings as before).

## Notes

- No `supplierPartNumbers`/`cadModel`: this part isn't stocked on JLCPCB and has no easyeda model.
- `bun run format:check` passes; `tsc --noEmit` adds no new errors beyond the repo-wide pre-existing TS5097 (.tsx import extension) class.

title: Recover staggered SMD pin headers
description: Recognizes staggered SMT pad rows and seeds the existing smdpinheader family with measured parameters, improving footprint recovery for specific SMD connectors.
body:
## Summary

- recognize explicitly labeled staggered SMT pad rows
- seed the existing `smdpinheader` family with measured `p`, `py`, `pw`, and `ph`
- add a C2883760 regression test while preserving discovery for geometrically similar packages

## Motivation

C2883760 uses an alternating two-row 2.54 mm SMD connector footprint. Discovery found `smdpinheader`, but omitted its supported `py` row-pitch parameter, limiting copper IoU to 87.20%.

## Implementation

When source metadata says `staggered` or `交错`, detect uniform rectangular SMT pads arranged at a constant pitch across two alternating rows. Emit a fully measured `smdpinheader` seed. The source guard avoids reclassifying geometrically similar three-pin transistor packages.

## Validation

- C2883760: 87.20% -> 99.997%

title: Improve LED2835 and asymmetric QFN discovery
description: Enhances the accuracy of footprint discovery for LED2835 and asymmetric QFN components by implementing specific geometry measurements and regression tests.
body:
## Motivation

Some real JLCPCB footprints require geometry that the generic discovery seeds did not preserve:

- C210314 uses asymmetric LED2835 pad widths and offsets.
- C128396 uses wider left/right UQFN pads than its top/bottom pads.

Without measured seeds, discovery could select a less accurate family or lose the per-side pad geometry.

## Implementation

- Analyze two-pad rectangular SMD geometry generically as `twoPadSmd`, with measured pin widths, offsets, and shared pad height.
- Use the `2835` source hint only when selecting the existing `led2835` family and mapping those generic measurements to `p1w`, `p2w`, `ph`, `p1x`, and `p2x`.
- Measure top/bottom and left/right pad dimensions independently for four-sided QFN targets.
- Emit asymmetric QFN seeds using the full `leftrightpadwidth` and `leftrightpadlength` parameter names.
- Preserve square pad geometry with `rounded0`.
- Add real-footprint regression tests for C210314 and C128396.

## Impact

- C210314 improves from 89.2708% to 99.9995% copper IoU.
- C128396 improves from 93.0006% to 99.9564% copper IoU.
- The full JLC5000 ≥95% result improves from 488/600 to 490/600.
- No other benchmark score changed and no regressions were found.
- No new Footprinter family is introduced.

## Validation

- `bun run format`
- `bunx tsc --noEmit`
- `bun test tests/jlcpcb-led2835.test.tsx tests/jlcpcb-ts3usb221a.test.tsx` — 2 passed
- Full 600-part CJTF benchmark on `upstream/main` and this PR using identical JLC5000 data and Manifold comparison — 0 errors in both runs
- `bun test` — 110 passed; two unrelated BGA precision assertions remain at 98.56% versus a 99% threshold with the locally linked latest Footprinter. Both failures reproduce unchanged on upstream `main` without this patch.

title: test: RP2350A QFN60 breakout routes 0/27 connections (reproduction)
description: Reproduction only  no fix. I could not root-cause this, so the PR pins the behaviour and records what I ruled out.
body:
Reproduction only — no fix. I could not root-cause this, so the PR pins the behaviour and records what I ruled out.

## What fails

Serialized four-layer fanout input captured from `@tscircuit/core`'s `<breakout>` around an RP2350A on a dual-RP2350 handheld board. The package is a QFN60: 0.4mm pitch, 7x7mm body, 3.4mm centre thermal pad. Twenty-seven of its sixty-one pads are connected — the rest are power, ground or unused — and all twenty-seven must cross the breakout boundary.

```
FanoutSolver: best layer assignment routed 0/27 connections
```

All 27 buses fail. On the `@tscircuit/fanout-solver` 0.0.11 build bundled in core it routes 9/27, so `main` is currently worse on this input.

## Narrowing

| variation | result |
|---|---|
| as captured | 0/27 |
| `componentBounds` + `sharedBoundary` at 0.6 / 1.0 / 2.0mm margin | 0/27 |
| only the package's own 61 pad obstacles (drop the 134 belonging to decouplers, flash, crystal) | 0/27 |
| dataset04 sample005, the synthetic RP2040-class QFN56 at the same 0.4mm pitch | 64/64 |

So it is not the neighbouring parts, not the missing boundary on its own, and not 0.4mm pitch as such.

One thing that stands out while reading the captured options: core supplies **neither `sharedBoundary` nor `componentBounds`** here — `solverOptions` is just `{ borderDistribution, compactBusTracks }`. That looks wrong against the `AGENTS.md` invariant that "all footprints in one problem escape through the same shared boundary", and may be a core-side bug worth its own issue. Supplying them by hand does not fix this input, though, which is why the reproduction lives here.

The difference I did not get to test properly: the passing synthetic connects every pad, while this one connects a sparse 27 of 61. Subsetting the synthetic's connections to check that orphans the helper's bus specs (`bus "central-bga:south:row-01" references unknown connection`), so it needs the buses subsetted in step — I left that alone rather than guess.

## What is in the PR

- `datasets/fixtures/rp2350a-qfn60-breakout-fanout.json` — the captured input (165KB, same pattern as dataset06's serialized clad1 fixture)
- `datasets/dataset07.ts` — wraps it as a `FanoutDatasetSample`
- `tests/dataset07-rp2350a-breakout.test.ts` — asserts the input is preserved, pins the current 0/27 behaviour, encodes the three narrowing variations above, and carries a `test.failing` that flips green when the input routes

Everything uses the public solver surface. Full suite: 29 pass, typecheck clean.

body:
A design review of `main` against Microchip's [USB2512B QFN schematic checklist (SC571233 Rev A)](https://ww1.microchip.com/downloads/en/DeviceDoc/Schematic%20Checklist%20USB2512B%20QFN%20Rev%20A.pdf) and the [AP2166/AP2176 datasheet (DS31814)](https://www.diodes.com/assets/Datasheets/AP2166_76.pdf) turned up four issues that would stop the board working, plus a set of layout problems. This fixes them.

`CHECKLIST.md` was already honest about Type-C source control, power budget, ESD and signal integrity — those stay open. This PR is about what that checklist did *not* cover.

## Vendor-checklist deviations

| Finding | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `TEST` (pin 11) | `noConnect` — checklist: *"must be tied directly to digital ground in order to ensure proper operation"* | tied to GND, with `requiresGround`/`mustBeConnected` so DRC enforces it |
| `VBUS_DET` | 100 k/100 k divider from VBUS — that's the **self-powered** wiring, but the part is strapped bus-powered (`CFG_SEL[1:0]=10`) | 10 kΩ series resistor to VDD33, which is what the checklist specifies for bus-powered mode |
| `RESET_N` | 10 k + 1 µF RC — checklist: *"Microchip does not recommend the use of an RC circuit for this required pin reset"* | MIC809SUY-TR push-pull supervisor, SOT-23-3, 2.93 V, 140 ms |
| `VDDA33` | tied straight to `V3_3` — checklist wants a ferrite bead with bulk on both sides | fed through `FB1`, 1 µF bulk each side |
| `CRFILT` / `PLLFILT` | one 100 nF each; checklist wants a 0.01 µF bypass **and** a ≥0.1 µF low-ESR bulk, *"as close as possible … without using vias"* | 10 nF + 100 nF on each, placed 1.1–1.7 mm from the pin |
| Unswitched `V5_SYS` bulk | 14.7 µF, over the USB-IF 10 µF inrush limit the checklist quotes | 9.4 µF |

## Other electrical fixes

- **AP2176 fault outputs had no pull-ups.** `FLGA_N`/`FLGB_N` are open-drain (the datasheet's own application circuit shows 10 kΩ pull-ups) and went straight to `OCS_Nx`, so the hub would have seen a permanently asserted over-current fault. Added 10 kΩ pull-ups to 3.3 V.
- **The fuse was 500 amps in the circuit data.** `currentRating="500mA"` produces `current_rating_amps: 500`, and the schematic rendered "500A / 6V". Changed to `"0.5A"`. This is a tscircuit unit-parsing bug — any SI prefix on this prop is silently dropped (`"750uA"` → 750 A, `"2000mA"` → 2 kA); plain amps parse fine. Worth a separate upstream issue.
- **Downstream `Rp` referenced unswitched `V5_SYS`,** so each port advertised a 500 mA source even with its power switch off. `Rp` now references the switched `VBUS_Px`.

## Placement and routing

The root cause was orientation, not spacing: with U1 unrotated, its four downstream data pins faced the **upstream** connector, and four of the six supply pins sat on package edges their decoupling capacitors weren't on. U1 is now rotated 180°, and every passive re-placed on its own pin's edge.

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| Worst supply-pin decoupling distance | 8.40 mm | **1.80 mm** |
| Connector A/B shorting links | 31–49 mm branches | **2.7–5.0 mm** local hops |
| Traces using the bottom layer | 63 of 130 | **42 of 141** |
| Total vias | 152 | **86** |

The Type-C A/B duplicates are now shorted at the connector pads with a short bottom-layer crossover (`pcbRouteHints`) rather than joining at an arbitrary point on a shared net.

## Repo hygiene

CI workflow running typecheck + build + snapshot; `bun.lock` committed and `tscircuit` pinned to `0.0.2242`, so the committed snapshots are a meaningful regression signal.

## Verification

Typecheck passes. `tsci build` routes **141 traces, 0 jumpers, 0 router errors, no DRC warnings**, including the placement DRC (courtyard overlaps, board-edge and mounting-hole clearance). `tsci snapshot` matches the regenerated snapshots.

## Deliberately not fixed

- **High-speed nets still reach the bottom layer, and intra-pair skew varies 0.07–5.26 mm between runs.** tscircuit has no per-trace layer constraint, and `<differentialpair>` can't be attached here — it requires a two-terminal connection, and the Type-C A/B duplicates make each pair net three-terminal. Placement now makes a top-only matched route feasible; doing it is a manual step, promoted to an explicit gate in `CHECKLIST.md`.
- **The 3.4 × 3.4 mm exposed pad** on the hand-rolled QFN footprint is still an estimate, and it's the part's only ground connection. I couldn't extract the package drawing from any datasheet copy I could reach, so it stays a verify-before-fab item rather than something changed on a guess.
- **The `OCS_N` pull-ups may be redundant.** They match the AP2176 application circuit, but I couldn't read the USB251xB pin-description table to confirm whether `OCS_N` has an internal pull-up. Fitting them is the safe direction; `CHECKLIST.md` notes they can be depopulated if the datasheet says otherwise.
- **Power budget and Type-C source control** were already open items. Added the specific arithmetic: 56 kΩ advertises default USB power (500 mA) on *each* downstream port, against a 500 mA bus-powered input.

title: Use pipeline names for autorouter versions
description: Replaces legacy autorouter version strings with pipeline-specific beta names, retains compatibility with unknown version strings, and normalizes them to latest.
body:
## Summary

- replace the legacy `v1`–`v6` autorouter version strings with pipeline-specific beta names
- expose `beta_pipeline1`, `beta_pipeline3`, `beta_pipeline4`, `beta_pipeline5`, `beta_pipeline7`, and `beta_pipeline9`, while retaining `latest`
- accept unknown version strings for compatibility, emit a warning, and normalize them to `latest`
- regenerate the generated props documentation

## Why

The former version numbers did not consistently match the underlying capacity-autorouter pipeline. In `tscircuit/core`, `v1`, `v3`, `v4`, and `v5` select their same-numbered pipelines, while `v6` selects pipeline 7. `v2` has no dedicated mapping and falls through to the pipeline-7 default. Naming supported values after the actual pipelines makes the API explicit without breaking consumers that still supply a legacy or future string.

## Impact

Consumers receive autocomplete for the pipeline-specific `beta_pipeline${number}` names. Legacy or otherwise unknown string values remain parseable, produce a console warning, and use `latest`.

## Validation

- `bun test` (415 passing)
- `bun run typecheck`
- `bun run build`

- all required documentation generators

title: Add a generic linear SMD pad footprint
description: Add a generic linear SMD pad footprint with support for an optional wider geometric center pad on odd pad counts, including regression fixtures for specific components.
body:
## Summary

- add a neutral `smdpads` family for an evenly pitched linear row of SMD pads
- support an optional wider geometric center pad on odd pad counts
- add real regression fixtures for C78322 and C7464756
- avoid both a component-specific GDT family and the semantically incorrect `pinrow` model

## Motivation

A human would describe this copper geometry as three evenly pitched SMD pads with a wider center pad. It is not a connector pin row, and it is not specific to GDTs or one manufacturer: C78322 and the unrelated C7464756 LED use the same reusable geometry at different dimensions.

The footprint is therefore represented by the explicit geometric name `smdpads3`, following the review suggestion.

## Implementation

The family uses:

- `p`: pad center pitch
- `pw`: outer pad width
- `ph`: pad height
- `centerpadwidth`: optional geometric center-pad width

`centerpadwidth` is accepted only for odd pad counts, where a single geometric center pad exists.

C78322 is represented by:

```
smdpads3_p3.299968mm_pw1.7999964mm_ph5.7999884mm_centerpadwidth2.3999952mm_rounded0
```

C7464756 is represented by:

```
smdpads3_p1.299972mm_pw0.3999992mm_ph3.0999938mm_centerpadwidth1.1999976mm_rounded0
```

## Validation

- C78322 copper IoU: **100.00%**
- C7464756 copper IoU: **100.00%**
- `bun test`: **521 pass, 0 fail**
- `bun run build`: pass
- new C78322 SVG regression snapshot

title: fix: add mirrored underside light rig so bottom board views are no longer near-black
description: Adds mirrored underside lighting to improve visibility of bottom board views in 3D rendering.
body: ## Problem Viewing a board from below rendered the solder mask as near-black, with bottom-layer traces, silkscreen, and pads effectively invisible. The light rig in `src/react-three/Lights.tsx` is top-side only — all three directional lights (key/fill/rim) sit at positive Z. This was harmless while the board surface planes used an unlit `MeshBasicMaterial`, but once they became `MeshPhysicalMaterial` the faces are genuinely lit, and a `-Z` normal receives zero directional contribution. Measured, using the normalized Z component of each light: | Light | intensity | `dir.z` | contribution to a `+Z` normal | |---|---|---|---| | key `[0.68, -0.8, 1.08]` | 1.35 | 0.717 | 0.968 | | fill `[-0.85, 0.55, 0.75]` | 0.25 | 0.595 | 0.149 | | rim `[-0.35, 0.85, 0.95]` | 0.50 | 0.719 | 0.359 | | **total** | | | **≈ 1.48** | A `-Z` normal got **0** from all three, leaving the underside lit only by ambient (0.22) plus hemisphere (~0.1) — roughly a 5.6x gap against the top face. ## Fix ### Before ### After Add three directional lights mirroring the existing key/fill/rim across the board plane: same azimuth and colors, negated Z, scaled by a single `UNDERSIDE_LIGHT_FACTOR = 0.75`. Because a light below the board contributes nothing to `+Z` normals, this is a no-op for the top face by construction. The underside lands at `1.476 x 0.75 = 1.107` of directional light versus `1.476` on top (0.79x), so the bottom is legible while the top stays the hero side. Reuses the existing `addDirectionalLight` helper (board-center offset, target aiming, rig parenting). `castShadow` is left at its default `false` — the top key light remains the only shadow caster, so there is no second shadow map and no competing shadow direction. ## Verification Measured in-browser by toggling only the new lights at a fixed camera (mean luma, 0-255): | View | Before | After | Change | |---|---|---|---| | Straight-on bottom | 23.82 | 70.91 | **2.98x** | | Near-vertical top | 36.78 | 36.87 | +0.09 (0.04%) | | Three-quarter, tall components | 48.00 | 53.13 | +5.13 (+10.7%) | The three-quarter lift is confined to downward-facing bevels on component bodies and the `DoubleSide` plated-hole barrels; only 0.22% of opaque pixels change by more than 60/255, so it reads as reduced crushed shadow rather than a wash. `UNDERSIDE_LIGHT_FACTOR` is the single knob if a softer result is preferred. `tsc --noEmit` and `biome format` are clean. Test suite is unchanged versus `main` (27 pass / 5 fail, all 5 pre-existing) — no test touches `Lights.tsx`, and the SVG snapshot tests use their own light setup in `src/convert-circuit-json-to-3d-svg.ts`. ## Out of scope - `HemisphereLight` takes its direction from the light's world position, which defaults to `(0,1,0)` — perpendicular to both faces in this Z-up scene, so top and bottom currently get an identical 50/50 sky/ground mix. Correcting it to `(0,0,1)` would push the bottom to the raw ground color and needs a `groundColor` re-tune alongside it. - `scene.environment` is deliberately nulled, which makes the `envMapIntensity: 0.18` on both board-plane materials inert. Re-enabling it would also address this, but it changes every view.

title: fix(fanout): explain how to fix a breakout that has no room to escape
description: Fixes unclear error messaging in the autorouting process when a breakout has insufficient space for pin escape, providing specific guidance for board authors on how to resolve the issue.
body:
## Problem

When a `<breakout>` hugs a fine-pitch package there is genuinely not enough room to escape its pins, and the solver correctly refuses. But `FanoutAutorouter.solveFanout` rethrew the solver's internal phrasing verbatim:

```
FanoutSolver: best layer assignment routed 0/27 connections
```

Nothing there tells a board author what to change — it reads like a solver defect rather than a design constraint. I chased it as a solver bug and got as far as opening a reproduction against tscircuit/fanout-solver before realising the fanout simply needed more space.

## Fix

Translate the failure into board terms at the point where core owns the context:

```
Fanout failed for U1: only 2 of 24 connections could escape to the breakout
boundary. The breakout boundary is 0.05mm from the pads at its narrowest point,
which all 24 escapes have to share. Give the fanout more room by increasing the
breakout's padding, or by extending the breakout to include the parts crowding
it (decoupling capacitors, series resistors) so their pads sit inside the
boundary instead of against it.
```

Three things it adds over the old message:

1. **Names the component.** `componentNamesById` is plumbed from `Group` through the local-autorouter strategy, so obstacles' `pcb_component_id` values are resolved to source names — `U1`, not `pcb_component_0`.
2. **Quotes the number that matters.** The narrowest gap between the fanned-out pads and the boundary is the space every escape shares, so that is what gets measured and reported.
3. **Names both remedies**, because which one is right depends on the layout: widen the breakout, or pull the crowding parts inside it so the boundary sits outside them rather than between them.

New files are small and single-purpose: `get-fanout-space-error-message.ts` builds the message, `get-pcb-component-names-by-id.ts` does the id → name lookup.

## Tests

`tests/breakout/breakout-insufficient-fanout-space-error.test.tsx` — a QFN56 in a `padding="0.05mm"` breakout with 24 pins escaping. Asserts the `pcb_autorouting_error` names `U1`, explains the failure, names both remedies, and no longer leaks `best layer assignment`.

Typecheck clean. `tests/breakout` is 12 pass / 2 skip / 2 fail, and both failures (`fanout-soic8-sensor-to-i2c-header`, `breakout-sot23-regulator-power-rail`) reproduce unchanged on a clean checkout of this branch point — they are not from this change.

## Note

The gap is only reported when a shared boundary is available. Worth a separate look: for a `<breakout>` core currently passes neither `sharedBoundary` nor `componentBounds` to the solver — `solverOptions` is just `{ borderDistribution, compactBusTracks }` — which sits awkwardly against the fanout solver's "all footprints in one problem escape through the same shared boundary" invariant.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: Clip traces at copper pour boundaries
description: Fixes rendering issues where traces were incorrectly displayed over copper pours by implementing a geometric mask that clips traces at the boundaries of copper pours, ensuring accurate visual representation in PCB designs.
body:
## Stack

Fixes the trace-over-ground-pour reproductions merged in #656. This PR is based directly on `main` and contains the renderer fix, geometry tests, and updated after-state snapshots.

## Summary

- mask every trace stroke with the finalized copper-pour geometry on its layer, so no trace is painted over actual pour copper
- preserve signal traces through BRep clearance rings because those holes remain unmasked
- retain exact segment-boundary clipping for route points annotated as entering a pour
- support rectangular, rotated rectangular, polygon, and BRep pours, including inner rings and curved bulge edges
- update both real-circuit Game Boy snapshots and assert that every rendered trace on their poured layers uses the layer mask
- split the boundary geometry cases into one-test files as requested in review

## Root cause

The renderer only skipped a segment when both route points were annotated as inside a copper pour. The first version of this fix additionally masked only traces whose source net could be matched to the pour net. That still left 731 top-layer Game Boy pixels where trace strokes with other or incomplete routing metadata were painted over actual BRep copper.

The mask is now geometric rather than dependent on net metadata: every trace on a poured layer uses the exact SVG geometry used to draw all pours on that layer. Finalized BRep clearance rings remain white, so legitimate different-net signal traces stay visible in their routed clearances while any stroke actually covered by copper is removed.

## Game Boy before and after

These snapshots use the same `abse/gameboy@1.0.16` PCB fixture from #656. It contains 253 traces and 93 ground-pour regions. The bright red route fragments visible through the maroon pour in the before image are absent after the fix; signal traces in clearance channels remain.

| ![Game Boy traces visible over the ground pour](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/circuit-to-svg/b607b00/tests/pcb/__snapshots__/real-circuit-gameboy-top-layer.snap.svg) | ![Game Boy traces terminating at the ground pour](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/circuit-to-svg/e45adaa/tests/pcb/__snapshots__/real-circuit-gameboy-top-layer.snap.svg) |

The bottom-layer Game Boy snapshot changes as well.

## Focused before and after

| --- | --- |
| ![Trace overshooting into the pour](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/circuit-to-svg/b607b00/tests/pcb/__snapshots__/trace-enters-copper-pour-repro.snap.svg) | ![Trace stopping at the pour boundary](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/circuit-to-svg/e45adaa/tests/pcb/__snapshots__/trace-enters-copper-pour-repro.snap.svg) |

- allow six bounded retries for idempotent full-catalog commands
- mark FTS ready after all ranges are populated without requiring the optional global optimize operation

## Why
Production run 31240275880 retained progress and recovered from several individual transient errors, proving per-command retries work. One late command then failed three consecutive attempts. Smaller FTS ranges reduce per-command work, the larger retry budget tolerates a longer Cloudflare disturbance, and skipping global optimize avoids making optional maintenance a correctness gate.

title: Retry D1 sync batches in place
description: Retry individual D1 commands instead of restarting the full catalog sync, making batches idempotent and requiring unique, non-null LCSC keys before replacing remote catalog tables, while upgrading Wrangler from v3 to 4.120.0.
body:
## Summary
- retry each individual D1 command instead of restarting the full catalog sync
- make table and FTS batches idempotent so ambiguous import-status failures are safe to retry
- require unique, non-null LCSC keys before replacing remote catalog tables
- upgrade Wrangler from v3 to 4.120.0

## Production evidence
Run 31236649480 showed why whole-sync retries are counterproductive:
- attempt 1 reached component_catalog rows 633001-634000 before Wrangler reported `Not currently importing anything`
- attempt 2 uploaded all 730289 catalog rows in about 22 minutes, then hit Cloudflare 7009 while creating search_index
- attempt 3 restarted from row 1 and failed at rows 10001-11000

This change keeps completed batches and retries only the failed schema, data, or FTS command.

## Validation
- 141 worker tests pass
- TypeScript check passes
- Bun formatting passes
- shell syntax checks pass
- workflow YAML parses
- frozen install succeeds with Wrangler 4.120.0
- retry-safe INSERT preserves rowids and FTS range replacement is idempotent in SQLite

title: Document all platform configuration options
description: Provides a complete reference for all 34 PlatformConfig properties, grouped by purpose, enhancing discoverability for platform integrators.
body:
## Summary

- replace the partial platform configuration list with a complete reference for all 34 `PlatformConfig` properties
- group options by engines/routing, project metadata, render/DRC controls, and platform hooks
- document types, behavior, and known defaults while retaining the link to the authoritative TypeScript source

## Why

The platform configuration guide only described a small subset of the options exposed by `tscircuit/props`, which made advanced configuration such as custom autorouters, SPICE engines, caches, file loaders, resolvers, and granular DRC controls difficult to discover.

## Impact

Platform integrators can now discover every available configuration property from the guide without reading the source interface first.

## Validation

- `bun run typecheck`
- `bun run build`
- completeness check: 34 expected properties, 34 documented, no missing or extra entries

## Summary

- add bug report 86 (`40bf8e8c-5c86-4cd4-85a2-e022ecd8ee5a`) from the F1C100S motherboard
- add a debugger fixture that runs `AutoroutingPipelineSolver9_PreloadedTraceGraph`
- add a focused regression for routing six LCD connections around 76 preloaded traces

## Reproduced failure

Pipeline9 reaches high-density node `cmn_4`, where B01 cannot route `source_trace_181`. The regional fallback then exhausts its via/iteration strategies.

The test is intentionally red. Initial investigation indicates that Pipeline9 loads boundary-crossing preloads into the hypergraph, but later rebuilds high-density fixed geometry from the original SRJ. The regional fallback then promotes every XY-overlapping preloaded section, including unrelated top-layer-only fragments.

Bug report: https://api.tscircuit.com/autorouting/bug_reports/view?autorouting_bug_report_id=40bf8e8c-5c86-4cd4-85a2-e022ecd8ee5a

## Validation

- `bunx tsc --noEmit`
- `git diff --check`
- `bun test tests/bugs/bugreport86-40bf8e.test.ts --timeout 9999999` reproduces the failure on current main (about 269 seconds)

body:
## Summary

- add a Pipeline7-only crossing-via reduction phase to TraceSimplificationSolver
- detect an A-B-A two-via detour crossing a route with an adjacent transition via, then atomically flatten the detour and relocate the existing via beyond the crossing
- validate both candidate routes against trace, via, obstacle, outline, immutable-route, terminal-layer, and through-obstacle constraints before accepting the swap
- use a layer-pair-filtered Flatbush segment index so candidate discovery scales with nearby geometry instead of every route/section pair
- cover forward and reversed route order, blocked relocation, through-obstacle transitions, Pipeline7 integration, and visual output

## Performance

The first implementation exhaustively compared every eligible detour against every route section, then rebuilt two full-board clearance indexes for every geometrically valid candidate. This revision first identifies viable A-B-A detours, indexes only transition segments with the matching layer direction, and exact-tests only bounding-box hits. Candidate validation uses one lazy shared board index plus tiny candidate-pair indexes.

Local isolated stage benchmarks:

| Workload | Cases | Before | After | Speedup |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Disjoint candidate discovery | 3,000 routes | 1,436 ms | 12 ms | **~120×** |
| Rejected-candidate clearance | 1,000 crossings | 5,684 ms | 43 ms | **~132×** |

The regression test verifies that 1,000 separated detours issue exactly 1,000 spatial queries and zero exact segment-intersection checks, then exercises 500 rejected candidates through the shared clearance index. This guards both hot paths against returning to per-route-pair or per-candidate full-board work.

## Before / after

![Pipeline7 crossing via reduction](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/fix/pipeline7-crossing-via-reduction/tests/solvers/__snapshots__/crossing-via-reduction-visual.snap.svg)

The reproduced crossing drops from three vias to one: the detour remains on its terminal layer, while the existing transition via moves to the far side of the crossing clearance.

## `/benchmark-all` via-count results

Via totals compare only samples solved by both the paired main and PR runs. This avoids treating a timed-out scenario as a via-count reduction.

| Dataset | Paired solved samples | Main vias | PR vias | Vias removed | Improved samples | Via-count increases |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| dataset01 | 85 | 3,407 | 3,369 | **38** | 12 | 0 |
| srj18 | 9 | 1,586 | 1,580 | **6** | 3 | 0 |
| srj19 | 160 | 12,790 | 12,786 | **4** | 2 | 0 |
| srj20 | 140 | 12,281 | 12,255 | **26** | 13 | 0 |
| srj21 | 10 | 121 | 121 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| srj23 | 75 | 1,006 | 1,006 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| **Total** | **479** | **31,191** | **31,117** | **74** | **30** | **0** |

| Dataset | Samples with fewer vias (main → PR) | Dataset reduction |
| --- | --- | ---: |
| dataset01 | #19 71→69; #24 34→28; #37 160→158; #41 47→45; #60 70→68; #66 182→180; #67 107→105; #69 114→112; #73 107→101; #79 23→19; #80 30→24; #83 37→35 | **38** |
| srj18 | #5 159→157; #7 235→233; #11 190→188 | **6** |
| srj19 | #2 22→20; #199 85→83 | **4** |
| srj20 | #9 26→24; #11 34→32; #42 63→61; #44 120→118; #61 72→70; #66 49→47; #67 68→66; #68 90→88; #112 197→195; #114 32→30; #146 52→50; #180 92→90; #195 52→50 | **26** |

Completion matched for dataset01 (85→85), srj18 (9→9), srj21 (10→10), and srj23 (75→75). The near-timeout datasets completed at 164→160 for srj19 and 141→140 for srj20. All five PR-only losses timed out downstream in `exactGeometryDrcForceImproveSolver`; their main counterparts completed in 326–354 seconds against the 360-second cap. The optimized PR has zero SRJ20 timeouts in `TraceSimplificationSolver` (main has one), eliminating the original simplifier timeout regression.

Results: [dataset01](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/pull/2000#issuecomment-5224254415), [srj18](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/pull/2000#issuecomment-5224254458), [srj19](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/pull/2000#issuecomment-5224254551), [srj20](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/pull/2000#issuecomment-5224254606), [srj21](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/pull/2000#issuecomment-5224254691), [srj23](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/pull/2000#issuecomment-5224254779).

title: Continue length matching after rerouting failure
description: Fixes autorouting failure when rerouting returns no valid candidates by preserving pairs for length matching.
body:
## Summary

- pin `@tscircuit/length-matching-solver` to the fix from tscircuit/length-matching-solver#46
- preserve autorouter's existing boundary: provide routes, consume `hdRoutes`, and ignore diagnostics

## Root cause

When coupled rerouting returned `no-valid-candidate`, the post-processing pipeline excluded that preserved pair from the subsequent length-matching input. The upstream fix includes every declared pair in length matching even when rerouting could not improve it.

## Stack

- depends on tscircuit/length-matching-solver#46
- unblocks the routing-phase regression currently visible in tscircuit/core#3082

## Validation

- `bun install`
- upstream fix reproduced against the exact Core routing-phase input: skew improves from 4.386862395114932 mm to 2.7361224397282058e-11 mm after rerouting reports `no-valid-candidate`

title: Integrate best-effort post-processing without route repair
description: Integrates best-effort post-processing into autorouting pipelines, allowing for direct use of post-DRC routes while ignoring certain diagnostics and removing unused components.
body:
## Summary

- use `PostProcessingSolver as DifferentialPairPostProcessingSolver` directly in Pipeline 7 and Pipeline 9
- pass each pipeline's existing post-DRC routes into the solver and consume only `hdRoutes`, intentionally ignoring required `postProcessingErrors` diagnostics for now
- remove the post-processing input adapter, the unused local compatibility solver, and post-processing-boundary route repair
- preserve the pre-existing Global DRC terminal-locking path unchanged
- convert legacy oval obstacles to rectangular bounds in the existing SRJ obstacle-conversion path used by both pipelines
- clear stale `through_obstacle` metadata where `TraceSimplificationSolver` produces finalized route points
- pass Pipeline 9 route metadata through unchanged instead of deleting interior port identity to satisfy solver validation

## Boundary

Best-effort behavior is owned by `length-matching-solver`. The autorouter passes its routes directly to the solver and does not normalize topology, bind overlapping vias, or repair unsupported pair geometry. The solver retains only basic shape and finite-number safety checks; topology that cannot be improved returns usable input routes with diagnostics. Physical vias may overlap at one coordinate, while `through_obstacle` transitions carried by existing same-net multilayer copper intentionally do not create a physical via.

## Stack

- Solver contract foundation: tscircuit/length-matching-solver#43 (merged)
- Best-effort solver foundation: tscircuit/length-matching-solver#44 (merged)
- Depends on: tscircuit/length-matching-solver#45, pinned at `ce7f5d92319cfe40f94dc50611f4420f51706bec`, for permissive topology handling and valid overlapping physical vias
- Depends on: tscircuit/high-density-repair03#63, pinned at `6943de12da0ac5f47358b0861110f3ae7edcd8c1`, for exact ordinary vias and marker-only `through_obstacle` crossings
- This PR is the downstream integration point for both open upstream PRs.

## Validation

- full solver suite: 72 passing
- overlapping/stacked via regression with distinct layer spans
- unresolved pair member returns unchanged routes plus `trace-resolution-failure`
- Pipeline 9 direct metadata regression
- representative Pipeline 9 focused test
- autorouter formatting, typecheck, build, deployment, and all eight Bun test shards pass

title: Use fixed RectDiff for board outline routing
description: Fixes autorouting failure by ensuring that the source_trace_26 remains within the board outline, addressing a bug that allowed traces to cross outside the outline.
body: ## Issue ## Summary - pin `@tscircuit/rectdiff` to commit `9205fa534c1b9ecc9aa5af364f5df27e5d52d835` - update the bugreport84 regression to assert `source_trace_26` no longer produces a `0.000mm` board-edge violation - refresh the route SVG snapshot to show the corrected path ## Root cause RectDiff's inverse-rectangle mesh could classify a large cell along a concave diagonal board edge from its center alone. That left a triangular region outside the polygon available to the autorouter. The pinned RectDiff commit subdivides diagonal boundaries and conservatively checks cell corners for ordinary outlines. For outlines that must first be simplified, it classifies the resulting small boundary cells by their center; requiring every corner inside a simplified outline eroded legal routing regions and broke SRJ18 port reachability. ## Impact The bugreport84 route stays within the board outline without breaking routing around complex rounded outlines. Strict DRC still reports positive-distance board-edge clearance errors; this change specifically fixes the trace crossing outside the outline. ## Verification - `bun test --timeout 30000 tests/bugs/bugreport84-726193.test.ts` - `bun test --timeout 120000 tests/features/pipeline7-dataset-srj18-sample006-selective-rerip.test.ts` - `bun run format:check` - `bun run build` - RectDiff: 70 tests pass, TypeScript and format checks pass - dense local sampling of every bugreport84 routed segment found zero points outside the board polygon and zero `0.000mm` board-edge violations Fixes #1952 Related RectDiff fix: tscircuit/rectdiff#140

title: Always use conservative approximation for connected rotated pads remove the fallback
description: Removes the global connected-rotated-obstacle threshold and ensures a consistent conservative approximation for connected rotated pads, addressing routing behavior inconsistencies.
body:
## Summary

- remove the global `> 20` connected-rotated-obstacle threshold
- always use the conservative approximation introduced in #1951 for connected, non-trace rotated obstacles
- preserve the existing trace-obstacle and unconnected-obstacle strategies
- add a regression proving the approximation does not change between 20 and 21 obstacles
- refresh the two affected route snapshots

## Why

The obstacle-count threshold selected two different geometry implementations for the same connected rotated pad. That made routing behavior depend on unrelated board complexity. This follow-up makes the corrected conservative implementation the single path for connected rotated pads.

## Validation

- `./node_modules/.bin/tsc --noEmit`
- focused approximation tests: 5 passed, 1 skipped
- `bugreport66`: passed
- affected `bugreport80` and `bugreport84` snapshots visually reviewed, updated, and verified: 2 passed
- full suite: 476 passed, 56 skipped; two expected snapshot changes and three load-sensitive hardcoded timeouts were the only reports
- all three timeout files passed when rerun in isolation

title: ci: balance test shards by recorded runtime, scale to 8 machines
description: Redesigns CI test distribution to balance test shards based on recorded runtimes, reducing overall test execution time significantly and scaling to 8 machines.
body:
## Problem

`Bun Test` is the only slow check in this repo — median **10.2 min**, p90 **14.9 min**. Everything else (Type Check, Build, Format, Vercel) finishes in under 2 minutes.

The 5-way matrix is imbalanced, and always in the same direction. Per-shard means over 16 recent runs:

| shard | mean | median | max |
|---|---|---|---|
| test (1) | 7.3m | 7.2m | 9.0m |
| test (2) | 8.9m | 8.5m | 14.9m |
| **test (3)** | **10.4m** | **11.0m** | **13.0m** |
| test (4) | 6.1m | 5.8m | 8.3m |
| test (5) | 4.5m | 4.2m | 7.9m |

Average total work is 37.2 machine-minutes, so a perfectly balanced 5-way split would finish in **7.4 min** rather than 11.0. Roughly a third of current wall time is pure imbalance.

Setup (checkout, bun, `bun install`, `npm install -g`) is only ~25s per shard, so dependency caching isn't worth pursuing — it can't pay back more than about 20 seconds.

## Root cause

`@tscircuit/bun-test-plan` distributes files **round-robin over an alphabetical sort**, with no runtime weighting (`nodeIdx = idx % nodeCount`). Cost in this repo is extremely skewed:

```
186.6s  tests/bugs/bugreport46-ac4337-no-near-gap-multiroutes.test.ts
183.0s  tests/bugs/bugreport78-dfeaaf.test.ts
167.0s  tests/features/pipeline7-power-trace-expansion-visual.test.ts
128.1s  tests/bugs/bugreport77-07f6a7.test.ts
124.0s  tests/bugs/bugreport68-41562e.test.ts
```

**10 of 354 files are 55% of the 36.9 min total.** The heavy `bugreport*` files are alphabetically adjacent, so the modulus drops several of them on the same shard every single time. `bun-test-plan.json` already pins `bugreport23` into its own glob pattern — that hand-patched exactly one file's worth of this problem.

A round-robin simulation reproduces the observed result to within 1% (predicts 12.14 min for the run measured at 12.0), which is what validates the cost model below.

## Why more machines alone doesn't fix it

The imbalance is a resonance between file order and the modulus, so adding machines is erratic and **not monotonic**:

| machines | round-robin (today) | LPT balanced |
|---|---|---|
| 5 | 12.14m | **7.73m** |
| 6 | 12.34m ← *slower than 5* | 6.53m |
| 8 | 7.28m | **5.02m** |
| 10 | 8.63m ← *slower than 8* | 4.12m |
| 12 | 7.96m | 3.61m |
| 16 | 4.90m | 3.61m |

Going 5 → 6 machines would make CI **slower**. Balancing is the change that matters; extra machines only pay off once it's in place.

## What this PR does

1. **Replaces round-robin with LPT bin packing** (`scripts/generate-balanced-test-plan.ts`) — sorts files by recorded cost descending, assigns each to the least-loaded shard. Achieves a **0.00 min spread** on real data. Also drops a global `npm install` from every shard.
2. **Checks in `test-timings.json`** — measured per-file wall time, parsed from CI logs by `scripts/record-test-timings.ts`. Timings are stable run to run (median ratio 1.00, p90 1.05 across two runs), so this rarely needs regenerating.
3. **Takes the matrix from 5 to 8 machines.** The repo is public so runners are free, and jobs aren't queueing today (median queue delay 3s). Costs ~3 extra machine-minutes per run.
4. **Adds a `concurrency` group with `cancel-in-progress` for PRs.** `bun-test.yml` had none, and three recent PRs each ran 2-3 full Bun Test runs because pushes superseded each other. This saves machine time rather than wall time. `main` runs are not cancelled.

**Net effect: ~12.0 min → ~4.7 min critical path**, a ~60% cut. At the current ~67 Bun Test runs/day that's roughly 7 hours/day of reclaimed waiting.

## Where the floor is

**Don't scale past ~10-12 machines.** `bugreport46` is a single atomic `test()` call taking 187s, so no sharding can beat **~3.6 min** (187s + 30s setup). At 12 machines that one file is alone on its shard; beyond 12, added machines do nothing at all.

Breaking below that requires making the tests themselves faster, which is a code change, not a CI change.

## Known limitation

New test files have no recorded timing and are costed at the p90 of known files (~12s). Because the distribution is so skewed, **no default fully protects balance** — a new file that genuinely takes 187s will push its shard from 4.7 to ~7.5 min regardless of what we guess. The default bounds the damage (still better than the 12 min this replaces) and stops a batch of new files from clustering; refreshing `test-timings.json` is the real fix. The generator prints every unmeasured file it encounters, so this is visible in the log rather than silent.

## Validation

- Cost model reproduces observed shard times to within 1%
- Packer output on current `main`: 8 shards, 4.69 min each, **spread 0.00 min**
- Shard coverage is exact: 357 files, no duplicates, none missing
- Both scripts pass the repo's own `bunx tsc --noEmit`
- `bunx biome format .` clean repo-wide (only the two new files were formatted)
- Ran files from a generated plan end to end: 3 pass, 0 fail

## Follow-ups (not in this PR)

- `bugreport68-41562e` has an internal 200s timeout but takes 124-260s, so it flakes on timeout — it caused the failures in runs `31178537084` and `31181521101`.
- The LPT packer could go upstream into `@tscircuit/bun-test-plan` as optional timing-weighted distribution, so other tscircuit repos benefit. Kept local here to keep this PR self-contained and reversible.

## Reproduction

The real-circuit reproduction and before-state snapshots were merged in #263. This PR is rebased onto `main` and now contains only the renderer fix, focused tests, and after-state snapshot changes.

## Summary

- render each copper layer's traces on a transparent drawing layer
- subtract the exact finalized copper-pour geometry with `destination-out`, then composite the trace layer onto the main canvas
- treat overlapping pour regions as a union while retaining BRep inner rings as signal clearances
- reuse the exact rect, rotated-rect, polygon, and BRep paths used to paint pours
- keep traces without pours on the direct rendering path, avoiding extra canvas work
- support top, bottom, and inner copper layers

## Game Boy before and after

The same PCB-only `abse/gameboy@1.0.16` fixture contains 253 traces, 290 annotated in-pour route points, and 93 ground-pour regions.

| Before — #263 | After — this PR |
| --- | --- |
| ![Game Boy traces painted over the top ground pour](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/circuit-to-canvas/17cab1a/tests/board-snapshot/__snapshots__/abse-gameboy-top-layer.snap.png) | ![Game Boy traces terminating at the top ground pour](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/circuit-to-canvas/3259de7/tests/board-snapshot/__snapshots__/abse-gameboy-top-layer.snap.png) |

The bottom-layer snapshot is updated as well.

## Correctness coverage

## Summary

- export the exact STM32C071 example from TSX to raw Circuit JSON, fabrication-safe Circuit JSON, a combined `.lbrn2`, per-operation `.lbrn2` files, an SVG preview, and a manifest with `bun run export:lightburn`

## Drill-free fabrication contract

The raw Circuit JSON remains complete for inspection. Before conversion, the LightBurn preparation:

- removes `pcb_hole` and `pcb_cutout` elements
- omits every unused prefabricated via
- retains only prefabricated vias consumed by routed traces, associates them with the trace, and sets `hole_diameter` to zero so copper is preserved at the existing via while the surrounding copper is ablated

The converter is configured for the top layer only with hole punching disabled. A final LightBurn post-processing pass removes the entire through-board cut setting and every shape using its cut index, including the board outline and any drill geometry. The generated XML therefore has no bottom layers, hole-punch layers, `Cut Through Board` layer, or `CutIndex="2"` shapes.

## Generated operations

- `Ablate Top Copper Outline` — 26 vector shapes
- `Ablate Top Pads` — 41 scan/fill shapes, one for every top SMT pad
- `Ablate Around Top Copper` — 43 scan/fill shapes using the default 0.5 mm margin

title: Add autorouted BiscuitBoard wrapper and STM32 example
description: Add a reusable BiscuitBoard component that allows users to place ordinary tscircuit TSX inside a prefabricated 75 mm  55 mm board, implementing a local autorouter and providing a complete STM32C071FBP6 example with necessary components and routing validation.
body:
## Summary

- add a reusable `BiscuitBoard` component so consumers can place ordinary tscircuit TSX inside a prefabricated 75 mm × 55 mm board
- preserve the physical mounting-hole layout and all 51 pre-drilled 0.8 mm / 2 mm prefabricated vias as `netIsAssignable` existing copper; generated copper pours are intentionally disabled
- implement the wrapper as a `<board>` with a local `autorouter.algorithmFn`
- route through the dedicated [`@tscircuit/biscuit-board-autorouter`](https://github.com/tscircuit/biscuit-board-autorouter/pull/1), which runs Pipeline7 and then attracts layer transitions to the prefabricated holes
- represent a selected hole as `through_obstacle`, so routing consumes the existing PCB via instead of manufacturing a duplicate
- add a complete STM32C071FBP6 example with decoupling, bulk capacitance, reset, SWD, power LED, and PA8 user LED
- check in PCB and schematic SVG snapshots for the STM32 example

## Usage

```tsx
import { BiscuitBoard } from "@tsci/tscircuit.biscuit-boards"

export default () => (
  <BiscuitBoard>
    <chip name="U1" footprint="soic8" />
    {/* ordinary components and traces */}
  </BiscuitBoard>
)
```

## Routing architecture

The standalone solver follows the handbook bootstrap pattern with a staged `BasePipelineSolver`, React Cosmos, `GenericSolverDebugger`, `graphics-debug`, SVG matching, a real-project repro, and test/type/format CI.

Its first stage runs `AutoroutingPipelineSolver7_MultiGraph` from `@tscircuit/capacity-autorouter` with a 0.2 mm minimum clearance. Its post-processing stage assigns Pipeline7 vias to compatible unused prefab holes, pulls the via coordinates onto those holes, and reroutes attached copper with visibility-graph/Dijkstra and grid A* searches. Global trace/obstacle and trace/trace passes push either trace aside when movement would violate clearance. Unreachable targets or unresolved collisions are hard failures.

[`tscircuit/core#3067`](https://github.com/tscircuit/core/pull/3067) teaches core to claim the existing `netIsAssignable` PCB via traversed by a `through_obstacle` result. This branch carries the same small dependency patch so the PR is buildable before that core change is released; the patch can be removed after the core release.

## Fixed-via guarantee

- unused prefabricated vias are hard obstacles during Pipeline7 routing
- each Pipeline7 layer transition must be assigned to one unused, layer-compatible prefab via
- validation rejects any remaining manufacturing `via`
- final layer transitions are zero-length `through_obstacle` segments at prefab coordinates
- the STM32 integration test asserts that the output still contains exactly the original 51 PCB vias

## Validation

- `bun run check`
  - TypeScript passes
  - 3 Bun tests pass
  - STM32 PCB and schematic snapshots match
  - package entrypoint and STM32 SVG builds pass
- STM32 example produces all 17 routed traces with zero circuit error elements and no manufactured vias
- independent `@tscircuit/checks` assertions report zero trace/trace, pad/trace, or via/trace violations at 0.2 mm
- focused fixed-via test forces a top-to-bottom route and verifies the selected existing PCB via is claimed by the emitted trace

## Dependencies

- tscircuit/biscuit-board-autorouter#1
- tscircuit/core#3067

body:
## Summary

- subdivide diagonal board-outline edges before computing inverse rectangles
- classify ordinary outline cells conservatively using their center and corners, including boundary points
- classify refined cells by center when the source outline had to be simplified, preserving narrow legal routing regions
- use the SRJ minimum trace width as the minimum subdivision size
- add the full `bugreport84-726193` fixture, per-layer SVG snapshot, and targeted inverse-rectangle regressions
- update affected simplified-outline SVG snapshots

## Root cause

`computeInverseRects` previously built its grid only from polygon vertex coordinates and classified each cell by its center. For a diagonal edge, a cell whose center was inside the board could still contain a large exterior triangular sliver. RectDiff exposed that entire cell as routable space, allowing the high-density router to create a segment outside the board.

Bounded subdivision creates small cells along diagonal edges. Ordinary outlines use conservative center-and-corner classification. Outlines with more than 120 points are simplified before grid construction; requiring every original-polygon corner inside those already approximated cells eroded valid interior space and caused SRJ18 static reachability failures, so those refined cells retain center classification.

## Impact

RectDiff mesh nodes no longer extend through large angled-boundary slivers, while complex rounded outlines retain legal port connectivity. In the autorouter reproduction for [tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter#1952](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/issues/1952), the original 0.000 mm/out-of-board error disappears.

## Validation

- `bun test --timeout 9999` — 70 passed, 1 skipped
- `bun run format:check`
- `bunx tsc --noEmit`
- autorouter bugreport84 regression passes with no `0.000mm` board-edge violation

- visually inspected affected RectDiff mesh snapshots

body:
## What this update brings

This improves the editor experience while TypeScript definitions and workspace dependencies are loading.

- Prevents valid imports and dependent symbols from briefly flashing red.
- Keeps the editor fully interactive during type acquisition.
- Adds a delayed, accessible **Loading types…** indicator to the workspace editor.
- Avoids showing a loading indicator for fast, cached acquisitions.
- Respects reduced-motion preferences.
- Restores Monaco's normal or caller-provided validation behavior as soon as loading finishes, so genuine errors remain visible.

## How it works

Monaco can run diagnostics before automatic type acquisition has registered downloaded definitions. During that incomplete dependency window, the editor now temporarily hides validation decorations instead of presenting unresolved imports as real errors.

Both editor variants use the type-acquisition readiness state to control diagnostics. The workspace editor also provides visible progress feedback without blocking editing or changing the standalone editor's DOM structure.

## Regression coverage

Added tests confirming that:

- Validation decorations are disabled while types load.
- Monaco's default validation mode is restored afterward.
- Consumer-provided validation preferences are preserved.

description: Reproduces the rejection of internal PCB terminal metadata in the post-processing passthrough of HD routes when no differential pairs are present.
body:
## Stack

This reproduction is based on `09ecefb`, the exact Pipeline7-compatible commit currently pinned by `tscircuit-autorouter`.

## Problem

When there are no differential pairs, `PostProcessingSolver` uses its pass-through path: it returns a structured clone of the HD routes and does not reroute them.

A shared-root route can legitimately contain a PCB terminal inside the path where another branch joins. The pass-through validator currently applies the active-rerouting rule that PCB-terminal metadata may appear only at the first or last point, so it rejects data it would otherwise copy unchanged.

This fixture uses the IDs and coordinates from `srj24` sample 4:

- route: `source_trace_261__source_net_261_mst1`
- output endpoints: `pcb_port_933` and `pcb_port_691`
- internal branch terminal: `pcb_port_873`

## Snapshot

The snapshot uses the production post-processing visualization. Red boxes are PCB pads, blue is routed copper, and the blue circle is the layer transition via. The three labels show the real start, internal branch terminal, and end.

The reproduction captures the current rejection without changing or sanitizing the route.

![Internal terminal pass-through reproduction](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/length-matching-solver/f619a8fa2f787676d50f9cf7739d2201a20ca07c/tests/post-processing/passthrough/__snapshots__/internal-terminal-metadata.snap.svg)

description: Fixes containment check for fanout exits to allow routing plans to reach the shared boundary, resolving a bug where widening the boundary led to zero routes.
body:
Fixes the repro merged in #28.

## Root cause

Fanout exits are placed on the shared boundary and must terminate exactly on it. But `planIsClear` checked containment against `srj.bounds` alone:

```ts
if (
  !pointIsInsideBounds(plan.exitPoint, srj.bounds) ||
  plan.segments.some((segment) => !pointIsInsideBounds(segment.start, srj.bounds) || ...)
) {
  return false
}
```

So whenever the shared boundary extends past `srj.bounds`, *every* plan is rejected on its first check — before any obstacle, clearance or geometry reasoning happens. Nothing is unroutable; the candidate is thrown away for being where it was asked to go.

That is not a corner case. It is exactly what `fanoutBoundaryPadding` produces: it pads the boundary without widening the routing area. Captured from `@tscircuit/core` on a real board with `fanoutBoundaryPadding="1.2mm"`:

```
srj.bounds   x -6.38..6.68,  y -6.28..4.01
fanoutBounds x -7.58..7.28,  y -7.43..5.21   <- entirely outside on every side
```

The practical effect was that the one prop for giving a fanout more room guaranteed it routed nothing.

## Fix

Containment now follows `srj.bounds` widened to include the bus's shared boundary (`PreparedBus` already carries it, so nothing new is threaded through). Obstacle and clearance checks are untouched and still do the real work — this only stops discarding plans for reaching the boundary they were told to reach.

## Result

dataset07, same input, only the boundary changes:

| shared boundary | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| as core resolves it | 13/23 | 13/23 |
| +0.3mm | 0/23 | **17/23** |
| +0.6mm | 0/23 | **18/23** |
| +1.2mm | 0/23 | **19/23** |
| +2mm / +3mm | 0/23 | **19/23** |

Monotonic in room given, which is the invariant #28 asserted. 23/23 is still not reached — that is a separate question about this geometry and I have not claimed otherwise.

## Tests

`tests/dataset07-wider-boundary-routes-fewer.test.ts` documented the broken behaviour, so it is replaced by `dataset07-wider-boundary-never-routes-fewer.test.ts`:

- the invariant from #28, now a normal test rather than `test.failing`
- routes strictly more once the boundary clears `srj.bounds`
- input-preservation check

Solves are memoized across the file since each takes a few seconds. dataset07's descriptions and the cosmos page carried the old "0/23" numbers, so both are updated and the page is renamed to `repro01-boundary-size-vs-routed.page.tsx` — still useful as a visual regression guard.

Full suite 28 pass, typecheck clean, cosmos export verified. No change to dataset01-06, including RK3588 (1088 balls) and the clad1 RP2040 reproduction.

## Related

- tscircuit/core#3053 warns when `padding` is set without `fanoutBoundaryPadding`; that warning is more useful now that following it actually helps
- tscircuit/core#3052 (merged) explains the genuine out-of-room case in board terms

title: Carry Circuit JSON provenance in SRJ circuitJsonMetadata
description: Add an optional, typed circuitJsonMetadata field to the shared Simple Route JSON obstacle type, carrying SMT-pad, plated-hole, port, and via IDs without adding Circuit JSON fields directly to the routing model.
body:
## Summary

- add an optional, typed `circuitJsonMetadata` field to the shared Simple Route JSON obstacle type
- carry SMT-pad, plated-hole, port, and via IDs without adding Circuit JSON fields directly to the routing model
- include optional `source_component_name` and `source_port_name` labels to make serialized obstacles easier to inspect
- normalize preserved Circuit JSON trace routes into the small SRJ route union while retaining endpoint connectivity through `connectsTo`
- share one Core obstacle type between obstacle generation and Simple Route JSON
- cover the boundary with IDs that deliberately have no type prefix

## Why

Pipeline 9 imports pre-routed traces into its hypergraph so it can update them while routing new connections. Its Circuit JSON conversion adapter also needs enough provenance to reconstruct pad entities for DRC. Circuit JSON IDs are opaque, so consumers cannot infer element kinds from ID text.

This keeps SRJ small: routing behavior depends only on normal SRJ connectivity and geometry. `circuitJsonMetadata` is optional, carries producer provenance through the pipeline, and is explicitly forbidden as an input to routing decisions. Non-routing adapters may use it when reconstructing Circuit JSON entities.

Related autorouter reproduction/fix: https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/pull/2025

## Impact

Existing `connectedTo` data remains unchanged. Preserved traces no longer leak Circuit JSON route-point fields into SRJ, and obstacle provenance is additive under `circuitJsonMetadata`.

## Tests

- `bunx tsc --noEmit`
- `bun run build`
- `bun test tests/utils/autorouting` (31 pass)

title: fix: parse SI-prefixed fuse current and voltage ratings
description: Fixes incorrect parsing of SI-prefixed fuse current and voltage ratings, ensuring accurate representation in both emitted values and schematic display.
body:
### Summary

Fuse parsed `currentRating` and `voltageRating` with `parseFloat`, which drops the SI prefix. A `500mA` fuse emitted `current_rating_amps: 500` (500 A) instead of `0.5` and its schematic symbol read `500A`. This honors SI-prefixed ratings.

Closes #3079.

### Change

`lib/components/normal-components/Fuse.ts` now uses `parseAndConvertSiUnit` from `format-si-unit` (already a dependency, already imported in this file for `formatSiUnit`) instead of `parseFloat`, both for the emitted `source_component` values and for the schematic display label.

- `"500mA"` -> `0.5` A and `"250mV"` -> `0.25` V
- plain values like `"10"`, `"2A"`, `"24V"` or `"220"` are unchanged, so no existing snapshot moves

### Test

`tests/components/normal-components/fuse-si-prefixed-ratings.test.tsx` builds a `500mA / 250V` fuse and asserts `current_rating_amps === 0.5`, `voltage_rating_volts === 250`, the display strings and `symbol_display_value === "500mA / 250V"`, plus a schematic snapshot.

### Verified locally

- `bun test` on the new test, the existing `fuse.test.tsx` and the fuse bounding-box test: all pass
- `bunx tsc --noEmit`: clean
- `biome format`: clean
- existing fuse snapshots unchanged (all use whole-unit values)

### AI assistance

AI (Claude, Anthropic) was used to help find and fix this. The design, review and verification were done by the author. Verified locally before submitting: the tests, typecheck and format checks listed above.

title: Bump schematic-trace-solver to 0.0.129 for span-jog inline labels
description: Updates the schematic-trace-solver dependency to version 0.0.129, allowing inline labels to be centered over routes with small jogs instead of falling back to anchored labels.
body: Follow-up to #3085, picking up [schematic-trace-solver#795](https://github.com/tscircuit/schematic-trace-solver/pull/795) (0.0.129): when no single straight run fits a net name, a route that is straight except for small jogs now gets the label **centered over its overall span** — bridging the jog, never extending past the route's endpoints — instead of falling back to an anchored tag crossing the wire. **Test 3** (soic8 → LED, 3 units apart — the case flagged in #3085 review) now asserts the centered inline label: **New test 4** keeps the genuine fallback covered — at 2.5 units apart even the route's span (~1.36) is shorter than the name (~1.8), so the anchored label remains: No other snapshots changed — 0.0.129 places identically wherever a label already fit a straight run, and the overhang-at-midpoint path it removed had produced no placements in this suite. Full suite: 1368 pass / 0 fail (one slow test flaked under full-suite load locally, passes 3/3 in isolation). 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: Apply padding to breakout bounds
description: Fixes padding application for breakout routing-directive groups in PCB layout calculations, ensuring proper bounds are calculated and tested.
body:
## Summary

- apply existing PCB padding resolution to breakout routing-directive groups
- turn the stacked padding regression from `test.failing` into a passing test
- refresh affected breakout routing snapshots and keep their route assertions valid

## Why

`Group.calculatePcbGroupBounds()` only applied padding to subcircuits, while `<breakout>` is a transparent routing directive. Its parsed `padding` and directional padding values were therefore ignored.

Stacked on #3089.

Fixes #3088

## Checks

- `bun test tests/breakout` (16 pass, 2 skip)
- `bun test tests/breakout/breakout-padding.test.tsx`
- `bunx biome check` on changed test files
- `bunx tsc --noEmit`
- `bun run build`
- `git diff --check`

title: Add failing breakout padding regression test
description: Add a regression test for breakout padding that currently fails, isolating the fixture and deriving expected dimensions based on rendered components.
body:
## Summary

- add a `test.failing` regression for ignored `<breakout padding>`
- isolate the fixture in `BreakoutPaddingReproBoard`
- derive the expected group size from the rendered resistor plus twice the configured padding
- render a PCB snapshot that states what is tested and automatically reports `FAILED` or `SUCCEEDED` with expected and observed dimensions

## Why

Breakout padding is parsed, but PCB group padding is only applied to subcircuits. Transparent breakouts therefore keep the component bounds.

title: Render inline net labels on point-to-point signal traces
description: Adds inline net labels that display the net name alongside point-to-point signal traces instead of as a tag anchored to the end, improving schematic clarity and usability.
body: > [!NOTE] > All dependencies have landed: circuit-json 0.0.465 ([#688](https://github.com/tscircuit/circuit-json/pull/688)) and schematic-trace-solver 0.0.127 ([#792](https://github.com/tscircuit/schematic-trace-solver/pull/792)) are released and bumped here. Rebased onto v0.0.1631. Full suite: 1367 pass / 0 fail (one flaky PCB differential-pair autorouting test passes 3/3 in isolation). The version bump also surfaces upstream solver 0.0.126 layout drift in repro171's snapshot - verified it reproduces on main with 0.0.126 alone, independent of this feature. A named point-to-point trace now shows its net name **alongside the wire** — parallel to it, above a horizontal run or reading bottom-to-top left of a vertical one — instead of as a tag anchored to the end. The line between the two pins stays unbroken. **Horizontal** — `USER_LED_ANODE` runs along the wire: **Vertical** — reads bottom-to-top, left of the wire: **No room** — falls back to the anchored label rather than drawing over a chip: ## Eligibility (automatic, no new props) `applyInlineNetLabelEligibility` marks a direct connection `allowInlineNetLabel` when it's a genuine point-to-point signal: - the whole net is exactly these two ports (a third tap would make the label ambiguous), - not power or ground (those stay as rail symbols), and - the name is one the user chose — `schDisplayLabel` / `displayName` / `name` on the trace, or a named net — not one derived from the ports it happens to hit. The solver has the last word: it only emits an inline label for a connection it routed, slides along the wire to dodge obstacles, and declines when there's no room — the net then keeps its anchored label. A net never gets both. ## Output shape Inline labels are emitted as `schematic_text` (`anchor: "center"`, `rotation` 0 or −90) because `schematic_net_label` is axis-aligned by schema. Each carries the new `schematic_text.source_trace_id` (circuit-json 0.0.465) pointing at the trace it names, so consumers can tell an inline label apart from free-standing text and resolve its net. Renders in circuit-to-svg today with no changes there. ## Test impact - 3 new feature tests (horizontal, vertical, and the crowded fallback-to-anchored case). - 10 of 1382 existing tests changed: 6 were snapshot-only diffs, each inspected — e.g. the whole rp2040-zero schematic changed by exactly one label (`XIN` went inline). 4 asserted on `schematic_net_label` specifically and now read through a `getSchematicNetLabelTexts` helper that accepts either form (filtering inline labels by `source_trace_id`). - Full suite: 1345 pass / 0 fail. `bunx tsc --noEmit` clean. Docs: `CIRCUIT_JSON_SCHEMATIC_COMPONENT_OVERVIEW.md` gains a "Net labels" section describing the two forms. ## Merge order 1. ~~circuit-json#688~~ ✅ merged, released as 0.0.465 2. [schematic-trace-solver#792](https://github.com/tscircuit/schematic-trace-solver/pull/792) — merge + release 3. This PR: bump `@tscircuit/schematic-trace-solver` to that release, mark ready 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: Adapt the platform local cache for every autorouter pipeline
description: Adapts the existing platform local cache to the autorouter CacheProvider interface, allowing for shared topology and artifacts across autorouter phases and pipelines, while supporting both synchronous and asynchronous cache engines.
body:
## What
- adapt the existing `platformConfig.localCacheEngine` to the capacity autorouter `CacheProvider` interface
- reuse one adapter per local cache engine across autorouter phases and pipeline selections
- supply that provider to the default, v1, v3, v4, v5, v6/latest, beta_pipeline9, assignable, auto-jumper, and laser-prefab pipelines
- pass `null` when the platform does not configure a local cache; there is no global cache fallback
- support both synchronous filesystem cache engines and asynchronous platform cache engines

## Why
The platform already owns cache selection through `localCacheEngine`. Core should adapt that existing capability instead of adding another platform field or opting into an autorouter-global cache.

Keeping adapter identity stable lets phased Pipeline9 runs share topology and generated port-point artifacts from tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter#2024. Synchronous local cache engines enable the current solver cache paths immediately. Asynchronous engines are exposed through the provider async methods, while current synchronous solver caches continue to skip them.

Companion to tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter#2024. No props change is required.

## Checks
- `bunx tsc --noEmit`
- `bun run build`
- sync and async local cache adapter regression tests
- all-pipeline provider identity and opt-in regression test
- existing CapacityMeshAutorouter tests
- `git diff --check`

title: fix(pcb): render oval solder paste instead of crashing
description: Fixes a bug where rendering an oval solder paste in circuit-json caused a crash due to missing handling in the SVG generation process.
body:
Closes #659

## Problem

An oval `pcb_solder_paste` is valid circuit-json. It is one of the shapes in the `pcb_solder_paste` union (circle, rect, pill, rotated_rect, rotated_pill, oval) and circuit-json even exports a `PcbSolderPasteOval` type. But `createSvgObjectsFromSolderPaste` handles every shape except `oval`, so for an oval it falls off the end and returns `undefined`.

That `undefined` gets pushed into the SVG object list and `sortSvgObjectsByPcbLayer` then reads `object.attributes` off it:

```
TypeError: undefined is not an object (evaluating 'object.attributes')
    at sortSvgObjectsByPcbLayer (lib/pcb/sort-svg-objects-by-pcb-layer.ts:56)
    at convertCircuitJsonToPcbSvg (lib/pcb/convert-circuit-json-to-pcb-svg.ts:331)
```

So `convertCircuitJsonToPcbSvg(..., { showSolderPaste: true })` throws on any board that has an oval solder paste. `convertCircuitJsonToSolderPasteMask` hits the same gap, since it shares `createSvgObjectsFromSolderPaste` (there the `undefined` reaches `stringify`).

## Fix

Add the missing `oval` branch. It renders an `<ellipse>` with `rx = width/2` and `ry = height/2`, which is how oval plated holes are already drawn. The scale factors match the sibling `rect` branch (`transform.a` for width, `transform.d` for height).

## Test

`tests/pcb/solder-paste-oval.test.ts` builds a board with an oval solder paste and checks both entry points: it no longer throws, renders the ellipse, keeps `NaN` out of the output and carries an SVG snapshot.

## Verification (local)

- `bun test`: the 2 new tests pass and no other test regresses. One unrelated test (`renders a real pcb_pad_trace_clearance_error`) fails in my local full-suite run as an image snapshot diff. It passes in isolation and it is green on CI, so it is an environment-sensitive rendering snapshot, not something this change touches.
- `bunx tsc --noEmit`: clean.
- `bunx biome format` on the changed files: clean.

---

AI assistance (Claude, Anthropic) was used in developing this change. The design, review and verification were done by the author. Verified locally before submitting: `bun test` (the 2 new tests pass, the only failure is the unrelated clearance-error image snapshot noted above), `bunx tsc --noEmit` and biome format on the changed files.

title: Add a draggable divider to resize the code editor and preview in the web editor
description: Replaces the fixed 5050 split between the code editor and preview on the package editor page with a draggable, resizable divider, allowing users to adjust the width of each pane as needed.
body:
## What

Replaces the fixed 50/50 split between the code editor and preview on the
package editor page with a **draggable, resizable divider**, so users can give
each pane the width they need instead of being locked to half the screen.

Before: the editor and preview were hard-coded to `md:w-1/2` each, with no way
to widen the editor for long lines or the preview for detailed PCB/schematic
inspection. After: grab the divider and drag; the layout keeps the split for
the session.


https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/007028d7-5d20-423b-a10b-36df4371fac3

## Why it's a UX improvement

- **Resizable panes.** Drag the divider to rebalance editor vs. preview at any
  ratio; a sensible minimum width keeps either pane from collapsing to an
  unusable sliver, and the minimum is re-enforced when the window is resized
  (not just while dragging).
- **Cleaner affordance.** The drag handle is hidden by default and fades in on
  hover/focus, so the divider stays unobtrusive until you reach for it.
- **Keyboard + screen-reader accessible.** The divider is a real `separator`
  with focus styles and keyboard resizing, rather than a mouse-only element.
- **Responsive.** On mobile the editor pane collapses so the preview fills the
  screen; toggling the preview on/off restores the expected layout every time.

## Implementation notes

- Reuses the existing `react-resizable-panels` wrapper in `ui/resizable.tsx`
  (previously unused) instead of hand-rolling pointer math, so pointer capture,
  min-size clamping, and keyboard support come from a maintained library.
- Dragging is driven by the panel library, not React state, so a resize doesn't
  re-render the Monaco editor or the run-frame tree on every pointer move.
- The min-width `ResizeObserver` only updates state when the computed percentage
  actually changes, avoiding per-frame re-renders of a heavy tree during window
  resizing.
- The Monaco `options` object is hoisted to a stable module constant so the
  editor doesn't reconfigure itself on unrelated re-renders.

## Testing

- Verified the split, drag-handle hover reveal, preview toggle, and mobile
  collapse/restore behavior across desktop (1280px) and mobile (375px)
  viewports.
- Snapshot baselines that include the editor layout will need regeneration
  (`bun run playwright:update`) since the divider changes the rendered output.

title: Add rotation to texts
description: Adds an optional rotation property to text elements, allowing them to be rendered at specified angles in graphics space, improving alignment with vertical traces in debug visualizations.
body: `Text` gains an optional `rotation`: degrees **counter-clockwise about the anchor point in graphics (y-up) space**, so `rotation: 90` reads bottom-to-top. Unset text renders exactly as before. ## Why The schematic-trace-solver's new inline net labels ([schematic-trace-solver#792](https://github.com/tscircuit/schematic-trace-solver/pull/792)) run parallel to the trace they name. On a vertical trace the debug visualization currently draws the name horizontally across the wire: With this PR the solver can pass `rotation: 90` and the text runs along the wire. ## Implementation - Applied in all three renderers — `getSvgFromGraphicsObject` (SVG `transform=rotate(…)`), `drawGraphicsToCanvas` (ctx translate/rotate), and `getPngBufferFromGraphicsObject` (via `strokeAlphabetText`'s existing `rotationRadians`). Each negates the angle into its clockwise screen space. - SVG bounds computation rotates the text box's corners about the anchor, so rotated text still contributes its true extents and is never clipped at the viewport edge. - Verified the PNG path renders bottom-to-top text correctly (software rasterizer). `bun test`: 68 pass / 0 fail (one new snapshot). `bunx tsc --noEmit` clean. Once released, I'll follow up in schematic-trace-solver to pass `rotation` from `InlineNetLabelSolver.visualize()`. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
