title: Remove via pairs with bounded obstacle detours
description: Extends Pipeline7s second via-removal pass with a bounded obstacle-corridor fallback to remove via pairs when direct shortcuts fail, improving routing efficiency and maintaining DRC compliance.
body:
## What changed

- extend Pipeline7's second via-removal pass with a bounded obstacle-corridor fallback when the existing direct 45-degree shortcut cannot remove an A-B-A layer detour
- query only nearby target-layer obstacles, validate every proposed path against the board outline, obstacles, and routed copper, and accept at most 4 mm of added copper per removed via pair
- keep candidate growth linear (`P + N - 1`) by holding one anchor at a layer transition instead of running another Cartesian anchor search
- add a deterministic 64-seed generator that starts from a known zero-via route, injects a DRC-clean two-via layer detour, and verifies Pipeline7 recovers the known optimum without a clearance violation

## Why

The existing simplifier detected the relevant A-B-A layer sections, but it could only move the existing middle geometry or replace it with a non-length-increasing 45-degree path. When a top-layer pad blocked the direct path, it could not synthesize the short local detour needed to remove the via pair.

The new fallback derives horizontal and vertical corridors from nearby obstacle edges. It runs inside the already-enabled second via-removal pass, after the cheaper direct shortcut fails, so it reuses the existing spatial indexes and does not add another whole-board pass.

## Seeded funnel

| Stage | Before | After |
|---|---:|---:|
| Generated DRC-clean two-via mutations | 64/64 | 64/64 |
| Simplified to known zero-via optimum | 0/64 | 64/64 |
| Simplified outputs passing clearance check | 64/64 | 64/64 |

## Via-count and performance results

Paired local runs against merged main:

| Dataset | Scope | Main vias | PR vias | Via reduction | Relaxed DRC | P50 | P95 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| dataset01 | 85/85 | 3,332 | 3,205 | **-127 (-3.81%)** | 77/85 → 77/85 | 2.80s → 3.05s | 16.09s → 16.36s |
| srj19 | samples 1,2,3,4,8,9,10,15,16,17 | 423 | 409 | **-14 (-3.31%)** | 8/10 → 8/10 | 9.3s → 8.6s | 15.9s → 15.5s |
| srj20 | samples 1,2,3,9,10,17 | 180 | 158 | **-22 (-12.22%)** | 4/6 → 4/6 | 3.4s → 3.3s | 5.8s → 5.8s |

Dataset01 total solver time was 431.0s on main and 422.3s on this branch (-2.0%). No paired sample gained vias or changed relaxed-DRC outcome.

## Before / after

![Seeded via detour before and after](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/blob/agent/seeded-via-simplification-fuzz/docs/visuals/seeded-via-detour-before-after.svg?raw=true)

Red is top copper, blue is bottom copper, magenta marks vias, and the dark red rectangle is the top-layer obstacle. The output is the actual seed-1 route produced by Pipeline7.

## Validation

- `bun test tests/solvers --timeout 9999999` — 30 pass
- `bun run build`
- paired dataset01 benchmark (85 cases)
- paired SRJ19 and SRJ20 subsets listed above

title: Speed up intra-node cache key hashing
description: Speed up intra-node cache key hashing by disabling prototypetype metadata hashing and skipping object-key sorting, while preserving the existing SHA-1 cache-key format.
body:
## Summary

- speed up intra-node cache-key hashing by disabling prototype/type metadata hashing
- skip object-key sorting because the cache-key input is already normalized and constructed in deterministic order
- preserve the existing SHA-1 cache-key format
- add focused coverage for deterministic, SHA-1-shaped cache keys

## Why

Profiling Pipeline 7 on `dataset01` identified `object-hash` recursive dispatch as a material hot path. On sample 32 it consumed about 1.55 seconds (15.9% of profiled time), with 4,646 intra-node cache misses requiring key computation.

`keyData` is JSON-shaped, explicitly normalized, and assembled in deterministic property order. The default `object-hash` behavior was therefore spending time hashing type/prototype metadata and sorting object keys without adding useful cache-key semantics.

## Blacksmith end-to-end benchmark

Pipeline 7, effort 1. Latest `/benchmark-all` run for rebased head `895c2df` against `main` `92bb330`. Lower timing is better.

| Dataset | Completion (main → PR) | Timeouts (main → PR) | P50 (main → PR) | P50 improvement | P95 (main → PR) | P95 improvement |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| [`dataset01`](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/pull/2016#issuecomment-5228364672) | 100.0% → 100.0% (unchanged) | 0 → 0 (unchanged) | 7.8s → 5.5s | **+29.5%** | 29.7s → 24.7s | **+16.8%** |
| [`srj18`](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/pull/2016#issuecomment-5228364699) | 43.8% → 50.0% (**+6.2 pp; 14.2% more completed**) | 8 → 7 (**12.5% fewer**) | 155.4s → 142.9s | **+8.0%** | 175.0s → 237.5s | **-35.7%**† |
| [`srj19`](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/pull/2016#issuecomment-5228364738) | 79.0% → 82.0% (**+3.0 pp; 3.8% more completed**) | 42 → 36 (**14.3% fewer**) | 47.7s → 40.5s | **+15.1%** | 260.6s → 278.3s | **-6.8%**† |
| [`srj20`](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/pull/2016#issuecomment-5228364744) | 69.5% → 70.5% (**+1.0 pp; 1.4% more completed**) | 61 → 59 (**3.3% fewer**) | 40.3s → 35.1s | **+12.9%** | 259.9s → 237.4s | **+8.7%** |
| [`srj21`](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/pull/2016#issuecomment-5228364879) | 100.0% → 100.0% (unchanged) | 0 → 0 (unchanged) | 2.5s → 2.2s | **+12.0%** | 5.1s → 4.1s | **+19.6%** |

† Timing percentiles are calculated over completed routes. On `srj18`, sample 8 changes from timeout to solved in 284.5s. On `srj19`, six former timeouts now complete in 313.1–352.2s. These recovered, long-running routes enter the completed-route population, so P95 rises even while completion improves, timeouts fall, and P50 improves. `srj20` similarly recovers two former timeouts (314.5s and 357.2s), while still improving P95 by 8.7%.

title: Reduce multi-crossing via detours atomically
description: Reduces the number of vias in multi-crossing detours by relocating adjacent vias atomically, ensuring clearance checks and preventing conflicts with existing routes.
body:
## Summary

Follow-up to #2021. A two-via detour can cross several transition sections, so relocating one adjacent via at a time leaves the collapsed detour shorted against the remaining crossings. This change:

- groups blockers by transition route and section, then relocates all required vias atomically with the detour collapse
- handles blockers on different routes and on distinct sections of the same route
- ranks start/end alternatives by total via movement and evaluates at most four combinations
- clearance-checks every modified route against static geometry, unchanged routes, and every other candidate route before applying anything
- rejects an otherwise valid multi-crossing candidate when one of its routes has a pre-existing external copper conflict, preventing downstream path simplification from turning that conflict into a final DRC regression

Each accepted reduction removes exactly two vias.

## `/benchmark-all` via-count results

Results below come from the six [full benchmark workflows](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/pull/2031#issuecomment-5228209802) on `207dcec`. Via totals compare cases solved by both revisions so added completions do not inflate the PR total.

| Dataset | Common solved | `main` vias | This PR | Change | Completion | Relaxed DRC pass rate |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| dataset01 | 85 | 3,333 | 3,327 | **-6** | 85 → 85 | 90.6% → 90.6% |
| srj18 | 7 | 1,153 | 1,153 | 0 | **7 → 8** | 25.0% → 25.0% |
| srj19 | 158 | 12,186 | 12,176 | **-10** | **158 → 159** | 38.0% → 38.0% |
| srj20 | 139 | 11,959 | 11,947 | **-12** | **139 → 140** | 27.0% → 27.0% |
| srj21 | 10 | 121 | 121 | 0 | 10 → 10 | 90.0% → 90.0% |
| srj23 | 75 | 1,006 | 1,006 | 0 | 75 → 75 | 14.5% → 14.5% |
| **Total** | **474** | **29,758** | **29,730** | **-28** | **+3 solved** | **0 common-case DRC flips** |

The reductions are concentrated in 12 cases; no common solved case gains vias:

| Dataset | Improved samples |
| --- | --- |
| dataset01 | #37: -4, #61: -2 |
| srj19 | #36: -2, #70: -2, #86: -2, #136: -2, #185: -2 |
| srj20 | #1: -2, #3: -2, #23: -4, #78: -2, #162: -2 |

The conservative external-conflict guard trades away 10 vias from the initial unguarded result (`-38` → `-28`) and removes its one observed DRC regression.

## Performance

| Dataset | p50 (`main` → PR) | p95 (`main` → PR) |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| dataset01 | 7.8s → 8.3s (+6.3%) | 29.7s → 31.5s (+6.3%) |
| srj18 | 155.4s → 146.8s (-5.5%) | 175.0s → 244.5s* |
| srj19 | 47.7s → 42.0s (-11.8%) | 260.6s → 268.4s (+3.0%)* |
| srj20 | 40.3s → 36.7s (-8.7%) | 259.9s → 248.0s (-4.6%) |
| srj21 | 2.5s → 2.6s (+1.0%) | 5.1s → 4.7s (-7.9%) |
| srj23 | 7.0s → 6.5s (-6.7%) | 137.6s → 126.8s (-7.9%) |

\* srj18 and srj19 each complete an additional long-running case on the PR, making their solved-case p95 population less directly comparable. Four of six p50s improve; the two increases are +0.49s and +0.03s.

The search stays bounded and avoids guaranteed-doomed single-crossing attempts. On a controlled sequential dataset01 run, candidate clearance checks fell from 12,594 to 7,571 (**-39.9%**). The external-conflict scan runs only after a multi-crossing candidate has already passed its normal delta-clearance checks.

## Before / after

![Atomic multi-crossing via reduction](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/207dcec91eba2fbafe89b3c4828103e710ff9d8c/tests/solvers/__snapshots__/crossing-via-reduction-multi-crossing-visual.snap.svg)

The detour drops from two vias to zero while the two already-required transition vias move just past their crossings: **4 vias → 2 vias**.

## Validation

- focused solver and Pipeline7 DRC regression tests: 9 pass
- `bunx tsc --noEmit`
- `bun run build`
- GitHub CI: all 8 test shards, format, type-check, build, and deployment pass
- `/benchmark-all`: all 6 workflows pass

title: Increase Pipeline7 crossing via reductions with delta clearance
description: Validates static obstacles and routes for crossing-swap segments with changed geometry, ensuring clearance checks are incremental and preserving layer isolation during via reductions.
body:
## Summary

- validate static obstacles, immutable routes, mutable peer routes, and the board outline only for crossing-swap segments whose geometry changed
- continue checking every segment against the modified partner route, including segments otherwise unchanged by the swap
- continue checking the relocated via against all routes, obstacles, layers, and the board outline
- recheck the complete detour section that loses its boundary vias at relaxed-DRC clearance, preserving layer isolation when unchanged copper still needs it
- add regression coverage for pre-existing static conflicts, changed-segment obstacles, new partner-route conflicts, and removed layer isolation

## Why

The crossing reducer introduced in #2000 revalidated both complete candidate routes. That rejected safe via reductions whenever an unrelated, pre-existing clearance issue existed elsewhere on either route.

Across a diagnostic run of all 85 `dataset01` cases, 2,707 of 11,325 route-clearance failures first occurred on unchanged geometry. This change makes clearance validation incremental: it proves the swap adds no new violation instead of requiring the input routes to be globally clean already.

The safety guard remains incremental. Only the detour section whose two boundary vias disappear is rechecked as a whole; unrelated route sections and the partner route remain on the delta-only path. This caught an SRJ20 case where removing the vias would have prevented downstream DRC repair, while retaining a safe two-via reduction in the same circuit.

## Before / after

![A three-via crossing simplified to one relocated via](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/275a05573d777ec0c41843763e23c2207cf580aa/tests/solvers/__snapshots__/crossing-via-reduction-visual.snap.svg)

## Local results

The local comparison stops Pipeline7 immediately after trace simplification so downstream DRC repair does not obscure this stage's effect.

| `dataset01` simplification metric | `main` | This PR | Delta |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Crossing reductions | 20 | 37 | +17 |
| Vias removed by crossing reductions | 40 | 74 | +34 |
| Total vias after all simplification phases | 3,372 | 3,338 | -34 |

Targeted performance measurements alternate `main` and this branch in the same checkout environment:

| Workload | `main` median | This PR median | Change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 500 rejected crossing candidates | 65.24 ms | 61.47 ms | -5.8% |
| 100 accepted crossing reductions | 107 ms | 106 ms | -0.9% |

## Validation

- `bun test tests/solvers tests/features/trace-simplification-immutable-routes.test.ts tests/pipeline7-trace-simplification-net-colors.test.ts --timeout 9999999` — 31 pass, 0 fail
- exact bugreport51, bugreport58, and bugreport68 visual repros — 4 pass, 0 fail
- SRJ20 sample177 end-to-end relaxed DRC — 28 → 26 vias, 0 → 0 errors
- `bunx tsc --noEmit`
- `bun run build`
- `bun run format:check`
- full 85-case `dataset01` trace-simplification diagnostic
- GitHub test shards 1–5 and 7–8 pass. Shard 6 reaches the workflow's 10-minute limit on the newly merged Pipeline9 bugreport86 repro, as did [the repro's own PR](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/pull/2022). Direct runs on `main` and this PR fail with the identical Pipeline9 regional-fallback error; Pipeline9 does not enable crossing-via reduction, so this is an upstream baseline failure outside this change's code path.

## `/benchmark-all` results

Final [`/benchmark-all` run](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/pull/2021#issuecomment-5227275336) for commit `275a0557`. Via totals include only samples solved by both revisions.

| Dataset | Paired samples | `main` vias | This PR | Delta | Samples improved | Samples worsened |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| `dataset01` | 85 | 3,369 | 3,333 | -36 | 15 | 0 |
| `srj18` | 8 | 1,466 | 1,454 | -12 | 4 | 0 |
| `srj19` | 164 | 13,537 | 13,359 | -178 | 59 | 0 |
| `srj20` | 140 | 12,255 | 12,157 | -98 | 38 | 0 |
| `srj21` | 10 | 121 | 121 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| `srj23` | 75 | 1,006 | 1,006 | 0 | 0 | 0 |

title: Span small jogs when no straight run fits the inline label
description: Centers inline labels over routes with small jogs instead of floating them, ensuring they remain clear of obstacles and within the routes endpoints.
body: Replaces #793 (closed) per review direction: an inline label should read as a name sitting **on its wire**, never as floating text overhanging a run. ## The case Real geometry from [core#3085](https://github.com/tscircuit/core/pull/3085): soic8 → 0603 LED, 3 units apart. `USER_LED_ANODE` (width 1.8) is longer than every straight run of the routed trace (~0.95), so #792's placement declined and the net fell back to an anchored tag — rendered vertically across the very wire the inline label was meant to keep clean. But the route is straight except for a 0.3-unit elbow jog, and its overall span (1.86) fits the name. A human reads that as one wire and centers the name over it. ## Behavior Placement is now two-stage: 1. **Straight run** the label fully fits on (unchanged, minus the old overhang-at-midpoint): slide within the run, never past its ends. 2. **Span**: if no run fits but the route's perpendicular extent is ≤ `INLINE_NET_LABEL_MAX_SPAN_JOG` (0.4), center the label over the route's overall extent — bridging the jogs, clear of the route's full perpendicular extent, never extending past its endpoints. Anything more meandering still falls back to an anchored label. Obstruction checks (chips, component text, foreign-net traces) apply to both stages. ## Result The test asserts the label stays within the route's endpoints, sits clear of its full perpendicular extent, and overlaps no chip. `bun test`: 175 pass / 0 fail (no churn to existing snapshots — labels that fit a run place identically). title: Add inline net labels for point-to-point traces
description: Adds inline net labels: a net name drawn parallel to the trace it names  above a horizontal wire, or to the left of a vertical one reading bottom-to-top  instead of a tag anchored to the end of it. Keeps the visual line between two pins unbroken on point-to-point signals like USER_LED_ANODE.
body:
Adds **inline net labels**: a net name drawn parallel to the trace it names — above a horizontal wire, or to the left of a vertical one reading bottom-to-top — instead of a tag anchored to the end of it. Keeps the visual line between two pins unbroken on point-to-point signals like `USER_LED_ANODE`.

## Opt-in per connection

The solver never invents one. The caller sets `allowInlineNetLabel: true` on an `InputDirectConnection` (optionally with `inlineNetLabelWidth`/`inlineNetLabelHeight` for measured text metrics — separate fields so the anchored label's `netLabelWidth` is undisturbed):

```ts
directConnections: [
  {
    pinIds: ["U1.1", "D1.1"],
    netId: "USER_LED_ANODE",
    allowInlineNetLabel: true,
  },
]
```

The [companion core PR](https://github.com/tscircuit/core/pulls) decides which connections qualify (two-port signal nets with a user-chosen name).

## How it places

`InlineNetLabelSolver` runs last in the pipeline:

- Only labels connections that actually got **routed** — there's nothing to run parallel to otherwise.
- Walks every axis-aligned run of the trace, preferring runs the label fully fits on, and **slides the label along a run** to dodge a chip crowding one end. Checks chips, component text boxes, and foreign-net traces.
- Skips runs shorter than half the label so a name never floats off a short elbow stub.
- **Declines rather than overlaps**: when nothing is clear it emits no inline label, leaving the net to its regular anchored label.
- A net that gets an inline label has its anchored `NetLabelPlacement` dropped from `getOutput().netLabelPlacements` — a net is never labeled twice.

## Output

New `inlineNetLabelPlacements` on the solver: axis (`x`/`y`), anchor point on the trace, text-box center/width/height, and which side of the wire it sits on. Exported from the package index along with `NetLabelPlacement`.

## Snapshot churn: none

The new stage's `visualize()` mirrors the previous stage's output exactly when a problem has no inline labels, so all 167 pre-existing solver snapshots are byte-identical. New debug page at `site/examples/inline-net-label01.page.tsx`.

`bun test`: 172 pass / 0 fail. `bunx tsc --noEmit` clean.

title: Complete tscircuit-only SPICE validation, repair, and local debugging
description: Accurate TSX loading states Show whether TSX is unavailable, loading, or failed consistently across schematic and analog views.  Isolated simulation execution Run generated circuits exclusively with tsci and persist hash-bound Circuit JSON without performing comparisons.  Complete simulation comparisons Compare saved outputs separately, retain every graph and channel, and expose per-series, per-graph, and overall statistics.  Focused validation UI Remove redundant candidate and validation-scope panels while replacing misleading failure labels with useful comparison states.  Time-budgeted repair Let the agent diagnose whether the model, TSX, or both need changes, then validate candidates with tsci within the selected repair budget.  Atomic candidate updates Promote model, TSX, simulations, and comparisons together so the UI never displays mismatched revisions or incomplete benchmark sets.  Stable repair baselines Restore the exact retained comparison candidate before repair and prevent in-place runs or clones from mixing newer job state into older inputs.  Graceful quality exhaustion Complete repair with the best candidate and a warning when the quality target is missed; reserve failure for infrastructure or contract errors.  Reliable local-run lifecycle Add progress reporting, heartbeats, signal cancellation, interrupted-run reconciliation, and one current Local entry per job.  Portable retained inputs Verify retained files while copying, clean up partial writes, and propagate inherited dependencies through isolated task continuations.  Deleted-job cleanup Ignore Local records whose target jobs were deliberately removed instead of repeatedly reporting checkpoint-refresh failures.  Stronger reference discovery Require each crop to contain its own caption during discovery and prevent later comparison work from modifying immutable crops.  Robust graph verification Handle corroborated microsecond OCR mistakes and antialiased same-hue traces without weakening source-proof requirements.  Bounded agent execution Cap agent shell commands, retry transient provider failures, and report clear transport diagnostics when retries are exhausted.  Honest publication and progress Skip publication for below-target models, retain the development artifacts, and report partial pipelines using their actual completed stage count.  Bounded repair storage and CLI output Discard derived bundles for rejected repair candidates, restore only the selected job, and keep terminal output compact while retaining full summaries on disk.
body:
### Accurate TSX loading states

  Show whether TSX is unavailable, loading, or failed consistently across schematic and analog views.

  ### Isolated simulation execution

  Run generated circuits exclusively with tsci and persist hash-bound Circuit JSON without performing comparisons.

  ### Complete simulation comparisons

  Compare saved outputs separately, retain every graph and channel, and expose per-series, per-graph, and overall statistics.

  ### Focused validation UI

  Remove redundant candidate and validation-scope panels while replacing misleading failure labels with useful comparison states.

  ### Time-budgeted repair

  Let the agent diagnose whether the model, TSX, or both need changes, then validate candidates with tsci within the selected repair budget.

  ### Atomic candidate updates

  Promote model, TSX, simulations, and comparisons together so the UI never displays mismatched revisions or incomplete benchmark sets.

  ### Stable repair baselines

  Restore the exact retained comparison candidate before repair and prevent in-place runs or clones from mixing newer job state into older inputs.

  ### Graceful quality exhaustion

  Complete repair with the best candidate and a warning when the quality target is missed; reserve failure for infrastructure or contract errors.

  ### Reliable local-run lifecycle

  Add progress reporting, heartbeats, signal cancellation, interrupted-run reconciliation, and one current Local entry per job.

  ### Portable retained inputs

  Verify retained files while copying, clean up partial writes, and propagate inherited dependencies through isolated task
  continuations.

  ### Deleted-job cleanup

  Ignore Local records whose target jobs were deliberately removed instead of repeatedly reporting checkpoint-refresh failures.

  ### Stronger reference discovery

  Require each crop to contain its own caption during discovery and prevent later comparison work from modifying immutable crops.

  ### Robust graph verification

  Handle corroborated microsecond OCR mistakes and antialiased same-hue traces without weakening source-proof requirements.

  ### Bounded agent execution

  Cap agent shell commands, retry transient provider failures, and report clear transport diagnostics when retries are exhausted.

  ### Honest publication and progress

  Skip publication for below-target models, retain the development artifacts, and report partial pipelines using their actual completed stage count.

  ### Bounded repair storage and CLI output

  Discard derived bundles for rejected repair candidates, restore only the selected job, and keep terminal output compact while retaining full summaries on disk.

title: Fix rotated plated hole bounds
description: Fixes calculation of bounds for pill-shaped and oval plated holes to prevent bounds collapsing to center coordinates, ensuring accurate spatial indexing for PCB elements.
body:
## Summary

- compute tight bounds for pill-shaped plated holes from `outer_width`, `outer_height`, and `ccw_rotation`
- compute rotated elliptical bounds for oval plated holes
- add regression coverage for the USB-C shell-tab geometry that previously collapsed to a point
- cover arbitrary 45° rotations so bounds are shape-aware rather than only dimension-swapped

## Root cause

`getBoundsOfPcbElements` handled circular plated holes and rectangular-pad variants, but did not handle the valid pill/oval variants that use `outer_width` and `outer_height`. Those elements therefore fell through to the generic path, which only recognizes `width` and `height`, causing their bounds to collapse to their center coordinate.

Consumers that use these bounds for spatial indexing could miss real copper collisions, including a foreign-net trace crossing a rotated USB connector shell tab.

## Validation

- `bun test` — 103 tests passed
- `bunx tsc --noEmit`
- Biome format check on both changed files
- `bun run build`

title: Reject fuzzy EasyEDA component matches
description: Require an exact EasyEDA supplier-part or LCSC number match before fetching component details, rejecting fuzzy-only searches to prevent incorrect component selection.
body:
## What changed

- Require an exact EasyEDA supplier-part or LCSC number match before fetching component details.
- Accept exact matches from the search result's `Supplier Part`, `lcsc.number`, or `szlcsc.number` fields.
- Reject fuzzy-only searches instead of silently selecting the first result.
- Turn the merged C1555 reproduction into a correctness test while retaining its SVG snapshot of the misleading oscillator candidate.

## Why

EasyEDA currently returns `C6083536` (a six-pin oscillator) as the first fuzzy result for `C1555`, while the design expects a 0402 capacitor. The previous fallback fetched that footprint and produced a 0.1081 copper IoU mismatch. `C1555` has no exact result in the search response, so the converter should fail clearly rather than return an unrelated footprint.

## Validation

body:
## What this reproduces

Adds a network-free regression reproduction for the C1555/0402 warning seen downstream in tscircuit builds.

When EasyEDA searches for `C1555`, the first result can be a value-text match for `155.52MHz` (`C6083536`, an `OSC-SMD_6P` oscillator), not an exact supplier-part match for the 0402 capacitor. `fetchEasyEDAComponent` follows that first UUID and returns the six-pad oscillator footprint. The downstream core comparison then reports a very low copper IoU (0.1081) against the requested 0402 land pattern.

The test injects the observed search/detail exchange, verifies the two requests, and records the returned `C6083536` / `OSC-SMD_6P` result. It does not change lookup behavior yet; it provides a deterministic reproduction for the eventual fix.

## Validation

title: Fix positioned subcircuit routing bounds
description: Fixes routing bounds for positioned auto-sized subcircuits to correctly enclose their translated content, preventing autorouting failures.
body:
## What changed
- make explicitly positioned, auto-sized subcircuits derive each auto-sized axis from their actual content bounds
- preserve the authored center for ordinary positioned groups and fixed-size axes
- preserve the existing content-centered behavior for packed groups
- convert the merged positioned-subcircuit repro from `test.failing` into a passing regression and update affected PCB snapshots

## Root cause
`Group.calculatePcbGroupBounds` only used the calculated child-content center for explicitly positioned groups when `pcbContentBounds` was passed by the packing path. Normal positioned subcircuits call the same method without that argument, so their `pcb_group.center` stayed at the authored anchor while their children were translated elsewhere. The local autorouter then received a routing boundary that did not contain its pads and failed the reachability precheck.

## Impact
Positioned auto-sized subcircuits now route inside bounds that enclose their translated content. Ordinary positioned groups, fixed dimensions, packed groups, and `pcbAnchorAlignment` retain their established placement behavior.

## Validation
- positioned-subcircuit routing-bounds regression
- CO₂ `pcbPack` ordinary-group placement regression
- nested subcircuit anchor snapshot regression
- `bun test tests/subcircuits` — 48 passed, 1 pre-existing skip
- related group sizing and anchor-alignment tests
- `bunx tsc --noEmit`
- `bun run build`
- Biome formatting check

title: Fix imported React symbol port offsets
description: Fixes the issue of duplicated explicit symbol ports and incorrect positioning of imported React symbols by deferring port creation until the React symbol subtree is available and applying the correct schematic transform to ports.

## Summary

- defer inferred port creation until a React symbol subtree and its explicit ports are available
- apply the host component's schematic transform to explicit ports and stems inside `<symbol>`

## Root cause

`NormalComponent.initPorts()` ran during construction before the React `<symbol>` subtree existed, so `pinLabels` created one pair of ports and the symbol later created another. Explicit symbol ports also returned raw `schX`/`schY` values as page coordinates instead of passing through the same parent transform used by the symbol graphics.

## Impact

Imported React symbols can now be placed away from the origin without separating their ports and stems from the symbol body. `pinLabels` no longer duplicates explicit symbol ports.

title: Expand SRJ bounds to include connection points
description: Expands generated Simple Route JSON bounds to include all non-off-board connection points, ensuring valid routing for all endpoints.
body:
## What changed

- expands generated Simple Route JSON bounds to contain every non-off-board `pointsToConnect` coordinate
- preserves `connection.isOffBoard` as the explicit exception for intentionally external endpoints
- adds a focused regression test covering left/top expansion and the off-board exception

## Why

The ESP32-P4 SPI display interceptor produced a routing problem whose bounds excluded 25 of 174 connection points across 17 connections. Eight host-header ports were 4.213 mm beyond the left bound, their breakout bridge points were 2.413 mm beyond it, and one reset-related endpoint was 1.65 mm above the top bound.

Because core generated that invalid routing problem, it should make the bounds valid by construction rather than leaving the autorouter to fail or forcing the circuit build to throw.

Autorouter report: https://api.tscircuit.com/autorouting/bug_reports/view?autorouting_bug_report_id=e921c12b-afce-4f7a-9166-8af3448907a2

Related autorouter fixture PR: https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/pull/2047

## Root cause

For non-board subcircuits, `getSimpleRouteJsonFromCircuitJson` derives bounds from the fixed `pcb_group` rectangle before it assembles all connection endpoints. Cross-boundary ports and breakout points can therefore fall outside the selected bounds.

After assembling connections, core now widens each bound with the non-off-board connection coordinates. The reported problem changes from:

```text
x=-21.787..26.213, y=-22.725..21.275
```

to:

```text
x=-26..26.213, y=-22.725..22.925
```

All 174 routable points are then contained. Intentionally external endpoints do not widen the copper routing area when their connection uses `isOffBoard`.

This is complementary to #3066, which keeps a fanout-specific shared boundary within the routable bounds.

## Validation

- exact bug report after expansion: 0 routable points outside bounds
- `bun test tests/utils/autorouting tests/breakout --timeout 9999999` — 48 pass, 2 pre-existing skips
- `bun test tests/utils/autorouting/expand-srj-bounds-to-include-connection-points.test.ts --timeout 9999999`
- `bunx tsc --noEmit`
- `bun run build`
- `git diff --check`

title: Update autorouter and apply adapted phase traces
description: Updates the autorouter to handle trace replacements based on PCB trace IDs and enhances the autorouting process with new validation tests.
body:
## Summary

- update `@tscircuit/capacity-autorouter` from `^0.0.772` to `^0.0.782`
- treat traces returned by a later autorouting phase as replacements when they reuse an accumulated `pcb_trace_id`
- add a two-phase regression proving that an adapted preloaded trace replaces the earlier geometry instead of creating a duplicate
- assert that the real `beta_pipeline9` multiphase flow emits unique Circuit JSON trace IDs
- refresh the routing snapshots changed by the autorouter upgrade

## Why

Pipeline9 can load pre-routed traces into its hypergraph and return modified geometry for them. Core previously appended every phase's output, so both the original trace and the adapted trace survived when they shared a `pcb_trace_id`.

The phase accumulator now treats the latest returned trace as authoritative for that ID while preserving unrelated accumulated traces.

title: Identify capacitor chip footprints for CAD rendering
description: Prefixes supported capacitor chip-package footprinter strings with cap for CAD components, ensuring correct material application in rendering.
body:
## Summary

- prefix supported capacitor chip-package footprinter strings with `cap` when generating CAD components
- cover `01005`, `0201`, `0402`, `0603`, `0805`, `1206`, `1210`, `2010`, and `2512`
- leave modified and unrelated footprint strings unchanged
- update the affected simple-3D snapshot

## Why

A package-only footprinter string such as `0402` is interpreted as a generic resistor-style chip by `jscad-electronics`. Emitting `cap0402` identifies the component type, allowing `jscad-electronics` to apply its capacitor-specific muted ceramic material (`#856c4d`) while retaining metallic terminals. This keeps material selection in the renderer instead of hard-coding a bright color in core.

## Validation

- `bun test tests/components/normal-components/capacitor-color-for-cad-component.test.tsx tests/components/primitive-components/via-connect-trace.test.tsx`

title: Update circuit-json-util for plated pill-hole bounds
description: Updates the tscircuitcircuit-json-util package to version 0.0.106 to resolve issues with DRC spatial indexing for plated holes, ensuring accurate detection of traces overlapping rotated pill-shaped plated holes.
body:
## Summary

- update `@tscircuit/circuit-json-util` from `^0.0.104` to `^0.0.106`
- update the circuit-json-util override so nested DRC dependencies resolve the fixed geometry implementation

`@tscircuit/checks@0.0.152` was already added automatically by #3126.

## Why

The previous utility version could collapse pill/oval plated-hole bounds to a point during DRC spatial indexing. As a result, a foreign-net trace crossing a rotated USB shell tab could be missed.

The updated utility supplies tight bounds based on `outer_width`, `outer_height`, and `ccw_rotation`. The installed checks package includes a regression test for the reproduced CC2-to-GND overlap.

## Impact

Core's board DRC pipeline now detects traces overlapping rotated pill-shaped plated holes. Merging this package update will publish a new core version and trigger the configured upstream update workflow.

## Validation

- reproduced the USB pill-pad collision through installed `@tscircuit/checks@0.0.152` and `@tscircuit/circuit-json-util@0.0.106`
- `bun test tests/features/drc-error-detection.test.tsx tests/repros/repro6-USB-C-route.test.tsx`

Adding `pcbX`/`pcbY` to an auto-sized subcircuit leaves `pcb_group.center` at the anchor while its child content is translated. Local autorouting uses that displaced group box as its boundary, so a previously clean child route fails reachability.

title: Add repro for imported symbol port offset bug
description: Adds a focused regression reproduction for an imported two-pin ferrite-bead component implemented as a chip with an inline symbol containing explicit ports and schematic paths, addressing the issue of incorrect port duplication and offset rendering.
body:
## What changed

Adds a focused regression reproduction for an imported two-pin ferrite-bead component implemented as a `<chip>` with an inline `<symbol>` containing explicit ports and schematic paths.

The test places the component at a non-zero schematic offset and asserts that:

- only the two declared source ports exist
- schematic port centers include the host component offset
- both schematic ports remain connected
- both requested schematic stems are generated on the component

It also includes a schematic snapshot that makes the misplaced ports and stems visible.

## Why

Imported JLCPCB/EasyEDA symbols can supply their own port coordinates and short stem lengths. Core currently creates four source ports for this two-pin component instead of two, while the inline symbol paths follow the host component offset but the explicit symbol port/stem geometry does not. This separates the visible symbol from its traces and leaves the stems near the unshifted local coordinates.

## Impact

Fixing this behavior will allow imported two-pin symbols such as ferrite beads and inductors to render at their actual component position with connected traces and visible stems.

## Validation

On current `main`, the focused test fails as expected:

```text
Expected length: 2
Received length: 4
```

Command used:

```bash
bun test tests/repros/repro-imported-symbol-port-offset.test.tsx
```

title: Detect traces overlapping rotated pill plated holes
description: Fixes a bug where traces could overlap with rotated pill plated holes without triggering a DRC error due to incorrect bounding box calculations.
body:
## Summary

- update `@tscircuit/circuit-json-util` to `^0.0.106`
- add a regression test for a trace crossing a rotated pill-shaped USB shell tab

## Root cause

Pill and oval plated holes previously collapsed to a point when `checks` requested their bounds from `getBoundsOfPcbElements`. This could exclude the pad from the spatial collision query and allow a foreign-net trace to cross the copper without a DRC error.

`@tscircuit/circuit-json-util@0.0.106` supplies tight bounds based on `outer_width`, `outer_height`, and `ccw_rotation`.

## Impact

The trace-overlap check now considers rotated pill plated-hole copper and reports the reproduced USB shell-tab collision.

title: Integrate adaptive outside-in partial-rip routing
description: Integrates the outside-in partial-rip solver, enhancing routing efficiency and performance metrics for specific route counts while preserving existing topologies and metadata compatibility.
body:
## Summary

- integrate the outside-in partial-rip solver from tscircuit/tiny-hypergraph#159
- retain unaffected trace prefixes and suffixes, reopening only a bounded hot span and routing inward from both retained ends with a hard frontier-distance limit and a one-ended fallback
- use one full-rip warmup followed by bounded partial-rip rounds only in the validated 100–350-route window
- anchor candidate selection to the first completed state, limiting complexity tradeoffs to 20% max-region-cost and 10% total-region-cost growth
- preserve the established topology path below 100 routes, above 350 routes, and whenever traces are preloaded
- preserve dependency-boundary compatibility by keeping serialized metadata penalties out of the duplicate-port topology prepass and avoiding metadata-penalty double application
- expose tiny-hypergraph, partial-rip, outside-in-frontier, region-cost, and high-density telemetry in benchmark JSON

This supersedes #2048 and depends on tscircuit/tiny-hypergraph#159.

## Final `/benchmark-all` results

| Dataset | Cases | Main completion | PR completion | Main DRC | PR DRC | Main P50 | PR P50 |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| dataset01 | 85 | 100.0% | 100.0% | 90.6% | 90.6% | 7.0s | 5.9s |
| SRJ18 | 16 | 50.0% | **56.3%** | 25.0% | **31.3%** | 144.4s | **89.3s** |
| SRJ19 | 200 | 82.5% | 82.5% | 37.0% | 37.0% | 42.8s | 41.0s |
| SRJ20 | 200 | 70.0% | **70.5%** | 30.5% | 30.5% | 32.8s | 33.5s |
| SRJ21 | 10 | 100.0% | 100.0% | 90.0% | 90.0% | 2.3s | 2.4s |
| SRJ23 | 76 | 98.7% | 98.7% | 14.5% | 14.5% | 6.3s | 6.4s |

- weighted completion: **485/587 (82.62%)** versus 483/587 (82.28%) on main
- weighted relaxed DRC: **237/587 (40.37%)** versus 236/587 (40.20%) on main
- SRJ18 P50: **1.62x faster**, with one additional completed case and one additional DRC pass
- outside SRJ18, 570/571 cases exactly reproduce main's completion/timeout/DRC/via outcome; the only difference is SRJ20 sample125 completing in 355.5s instead of timing out at 360s

The small P50 movements on gated datasets are runner variance: their routing outcomes are preserved. The strategy is deliberately conditional because the holdout experiments found real completion regressions when it was applied to 41–62-route graphs and an unfavorable tail above 350 routes.

## Region-cost and core performance evidence

Across the eight completed SRJ18 cases where partial ripping is active:

- average max region cost: 1.661 → **1.268** (**23.7% better**)
- average total region cost: 15.414 → **14.015** (**9.1% better**)
- selected segment count: **6.8% lower**
- worst individual movement: +7.2% max cost and +8.4% total cost, inside both hard envelopes

The paired tiny-hypergraph `/benchmark` run reports:

- 8/8 cases and 2,001/2,001 routes complete on both branches
- 107.536s total versus 256.486s on main: **2.39x faster**
- 4.877s P50 versus 29.878s on main: **6.13x faster median**
- average max region cost 1.713 versus 2.333 on main: **26.6% better**
- average iterations 429,535 versus 1,335,850: **67.8% fewer**

The package benchmark's 361-route case is the unfavorable P95 outlier; the integration's 350-route upper bound excludes it.

## Policy

- fewer than 100 routes: compatibility behavior
- 100–350 routes: one full-rip warmup, then up to ten bounded partial-rip attempts
- more than 350 routes: compatibility behavior
- preloaded traces: partial ripping and outside-in routing disabled
- selection: region-cost-first, with complexity eligibility anchored to the first completed state

## Validation

- `bun run build`
- `bunx tsc --noEmit`
- focused terminal-ID, tiny bridge, topology, immutability, Pipeline9 materialization/splice, and preloaded-occupancy tests
- bugreport58 connectivity assertions pass with the first-state cost guard
- bugreport80 passes locally in 90.6s and on final Linux CI with a test-specific 360s budget; the corresponding current-main shard had exceeded the inherited 300s ceiling
- all eight Linux test shards pass with exactly the six intentional active-window snapshot updates
- build, format, type-check, deployment, and Vercel CI checks pass

The checked-in tiny-hypergraph experiment log records accepted and rejected window, frontier, round-count, density-selection, warmup, and scale-bound trials.

title: Materialize Pipeline9 hypergraph preload changes
description: Preserves explicit trace ID, route-position, and original-copper endpoint metadata on serialized preload assignments while exposing accepted hypergraph changes as high-density connections, ensuring that unchanged preload assignments remain fixed and that the materialized preload geometry is integrated into global and joint DRC processes.
body:
## Summary

- preserve explicit trace ID, route-position, and original-copper endpoint metadata on serialized preload assignments
- expose accepted hypergraph changes as high-density connections while leaving unchanged preload assignments fixed
- release only the changed interval from the original fixed copper, route and stitch its replacement, then rebuild it under the original `pcb_trace_id`
- pass the materialized preload geometry into global and joint DRC so joint DRC is cleanup rather than the first stage that applies the movement

## Why

Pipeline9 could accept a changed preloaded-trace assignment in the hypergraph, but `getOutput()` filtered all preloaded assignments from the high-density input and B01 loaded the complete original trace as fixed copper. That discarded the accepted movement before high-density routing.

This keeps the preload identity in explicit metadata rather than inferring it from an ID format. It also records endpoints projected onto the original copper, since graph-port coordinates are not guaranteed to lie exactly on that copper.

## Validation

- `bunx tsc --noEmit`
- `bun run build`
- 8 focused preload/Pipeline9 tests: 8 passed, 0 failed
- individually reran the Pipeline9 cases that timed out in the concurrent full run (samples 21, 46, 52, 53, and 70); all passed
- full `bun test`: 479 passed and 57 skipped, but not clean: 26 timeout-marked failures under concurrent load plus local SVG-renderer diffs
- GitHub CI: all build, formatting, type, preview, and 8 test-shard checks pass; one unchanged Pipeline7 test near its 300-second timeout passed on the failed-shard retry

## Allwinner follow-up

This PR materializes changes that survive as accepted final hypergraph assignments. The current Allwinner phase-2 probe still reports zero accepted changed preload sections, so that board likely also needs follow-up in hypergraph selection/optimization before this path is exercised there.

## Summary

- preserve `pointId`/`connectsTo` connectivity when preloaded traces are converted for joint DRC
- resolve preloaded endpoint ports from structurally declared SRJ connectivity instead of Circuit JSON route fields or ID prefixes
- add optional, typed `circuitJsonMetadata` to obstacles and use it only in the Circuit JSON conversion adapter
- migrate historical benchmark/bug-report fixtures from their documented obstacle ordering without parsing IDs
- make regional fallback reroute only preloaded sections that touch the active connection layers
- compare geometric DRC findings against the original prerouted baseline while continuing to repair missing connections
- make the merged bugreport86 motherboard reproduction pass and retain its solved SVG snapshot

## Root cause

Pipeline9 did include preloaded traces in topology planning, but three later behaviors made the F1C100S case pathological:

1. The regional high-density fallback promoted every preloaded section crossing a node in XY, including 127 top-layer-only fragments for an inner-layer routing problem.
2. Joint DRC treated 152 geometric findings already present in the supplied prerouted board as candidate regressions.
3. Circuit JSON reconstruction lost preloaded fanout ownership and classified SRJ IDs by text prefixes, even though IDs are opaque.

That caused false accidental-contact findings and selected nearly all preloaded traces for repair instead of focusing on interactions introduced by the new routes.

## Circuit JSON metadata boundary

`Obstacle.circuitJsonMetadata` is optional and typed for the Circuit JSON IDs and readable source names that Core carries through SRJ. Routing solvers must not read it. Only the testing/DRC Circuit JSON adapter uses the ID fields to restore entity identities. Pipeline9 determines routing connectivity from `connectsTo`, connection points, and the connectivity map.

Historical benchmark data and the bug report predate this field. A testing-only immutable adapter migrates their documented obstacle ordering into `circuitJsonMetadata` without parsing ID strings. Core now emits the field directly following merged PR https://github.com/tscircuit/core/pull/3120.

## Impact

`beta_pipeline9` solves bug report `40bf8e8c-5c86-4cd4-85a2-e022ecd8ee5a` with all 76 preloaded traces present. Existing Pipeline9 regional/joint-repair regressions remain green.

Follow-up to reproduction PR #2022.

title: Optimize obstacle detour validation
description: Optimizes the obstacle detour validation process in the autorouting algorithm, significantly reducing validation time and maintaining the integrity of via reductions.
body:
## Summary

- isolate exhaustive obstacle-detour validation from the generic layer-move hot path
- restore `canSectionMoveToLayer` byte-for-byte to the PR base behavior for non-detour simplification
- cache exact segment clearance and same-net classification only inside detour searches
- precompute the first segment to reject and avoid per-candidate section/order allocations
- preserve every via reduction and DRC decision from the exhaustive implementation

## Why

The obstacle-detour fallback added in #2034 removes useful via pairs, but its rejection funnel is expensive. On a representative srj23 case, one successful rewrite was surrounded by **51,923 failed candidate validations**; individual failed searches contained as many as **9,540 ranked candidates**.

A rank cutoff is unsafe: valid candidates appeared at ranks 521, 611, and 3,030, and the earlier 256-candidate cap regressed bugreport76 from 12 to 16 vias and bugreport82 from 62 to 64 vias.

This stays exhaustive. Small searches use low-setup string keys; searches with 256+ candidates use exact numeric point/segment IDs. The new validator also caches same-net classification, reuses points already on the target layer, and checks the precomputed longest segment first. Those detour-specific branches no longer tax ordinary layer-move checks.

## Same-worker performance profiles

The workflow profiles the PR and exact main sequentially on the same worker. Success and iteration counts are identical.

| Dataset / solver | Main | PR | Change |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| srj23, 75 solved — SingleRouteUselessViaRemovalSolver | 18.9s | **9.5s** | **-49.7%** |
| srj23, 75 solved — UselessViaRemovalSolver | 19.5s | **10.1s** | **-48.2%** |

title: Support rotated rectangle pad clearances
description: Copper pours now respect the real orientation and pad margin of rotated rectangular SMT pads, ensuring they are treated as obstacles in the solver.
body:
## Summary

- Convert `rotated_rect` SMT pads into solver input obstacles instead of silently omitting them.
- Preserve each pad's center, dimensions, and counter-clockwise rotation.
- Add a rotated-box polygon primitive and apply the configured pad margin in the pad's local axes.
- Update the merged TSX reproduction snapshot to assert clearance around both ordinary and rotated rectangular pads.

The circuit-JSON adapter handled `rect`, `circle`, `pill`, and `rotated_pill` SMT pads, but had no branch for `rotated_rect`. Those pads were therefore absent from `InputProblem.pads`, so the copper-pour solver had no obstacle to subtract and could pour copper directly over them.

## Impact

Copper pours now respect the real orientation and pad margin of rotated rectangular SMT pads. Existing axis-aligned rectangles and other pad shapes are unchanged.

body:
## Summary

- retain each affected trace's unchanged prefix and suffix, reopening only a bounded window around its hottest segment
- route the reopened window outside-in from both retained ends, with a hard maximum travel distance per frontier and a safe one-ended fallback
- provide an inclusive route-count window so callers can use partial ripping only at graph scales where it wins
- preserve the legacy hot path when partial ripping and outside-in routing are disabled
- choose completed states region-cost-first, allowing lower-complexity alternatives only inside explicit max-region and total-region-cost envelopes anchored to the first completed state
- expose routing/rip/frontier/cost telemetry and keep a checked-in log of the accepted and rejected experiments

This supersedes #158. The paired integration is tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter#2051.

## Official package benchmark

The final `/benchmark` run on all eight committed SRJ18 Pipeline7 inputs reports:

- 8/8 cases and 2,001/2,001 routes complete on both main and this PR
- 107.536s total versus 256.486s on main: **2.39x faster**
- 4.877s P50 versus 29.878s on main: **6.13x faster median**
- average max region cost 1.713 versus 2.333 on main: **26.6% better**
- average iterations 429,535 versus 1,335,850 on main: **67.8% fewer**

The package benchmark's P95 is 66.033s versus 47.871s because its 361-route sample is outside the reliable scale range. The autorouter integration therefore enables the strategy only for 100–350 routes; graphs below and above that window use the compatibility path.

## Integration policy

- fewer than 100 routes: compatibility behavior
- 100–350 routes: one full-rip warmup, then bounded partial-rip attempts with region-cost-first selection
- more than 350 routes: compatibility behavior
- preloaded traces: partial ripping and outside-in routing disabled
- complexity tie-breaking: capped relative to the first completed state at 20% max-region-cost growth and 10% total-region-cost growth

## Verification

- `bun run typecheck`
- `bun run build`
- focused outside-in, partial-rip, duplicate-topology, port-penalty, and route-completion suite: 22 passing tests
- repository CI: test, format, typecheck, and deployment checks passing
- `git diff --check`

Detailed trial commands, timings, route completion, and region-cost results are recorded in `experiments/outside-in-partial-rip.md`.

title: Fix orthogonal SMT pad rotation in Gerber masks
description: Fixes incorrect rendering of orthogonally rotated rounded rectangular SMT pads in Gerber masks, aligning them with PCB-mode rendering to prevent false geometry.
body:
## Summary

- bake 90° and 270° `rotated_rect` SMT pad rotations into swapped aperture dimensions before Gerber mask rendering
- tolerate small floating-point drift around orthogonal rotations
- add a raster-level regression test based on the dimensions and corner radius of the reported U3 pads

## Root cause

The Circuit JSON is correct: U3's pads are `rotated_rect` elements with `ccw_rotation: 90`. `circuit-json-to-gerber` represents that with a Gerber `%LR90*%` aperture transform. The `gerber-to-svg` renderer used by `check-shorts` does not apply that transform to the rounded-rectangle aperture, so the bitmap used for short detection loads each 1.0 mm × 0.6 mm pad horizontally instead of vertically.

For orthogonal quarter turns, swapping the aperture width and height is lossless and avoids relying on the unsupported transform. The input Circuit JSON is not mutated.

## Impact

Gerber-mode short detection now places orthogonally rotated rounded rectangular SMT pads in the same orientation as PCB-mode rendering, preventing false geometry around parts such as U3 in the reported biscuit-board circuit.

## Validation

- `bun test` — 15 tests passed
- `bun run build`
- `bun run typecheck`
- `bun run format:check` (passes with the existing oversized BlinkBuddy fixture warning)
- compared all five U3 pads from the supplied circuit: PCB and Gerber masks have 99.22% pixel intersection-over-union; the remaining edge difference is antialiasing around rounded corners

## What changed

- Build a bounded, deterministic `reference-graph-preflight.json` from the immutable PDF before attempt one.
- Give the agent source-derived figure identity, regular grid runs, anchor spans, printed scale candidates, explicit tick calibration, and units-per-pixel guidance.
- Reuse immutable render/OCR/PDF analysis in the authoritative source-proof builder instead of repeating it.
- Keep crop immutability, pixel proof, source proof, electrical binding, tolerances, and bounded correction retries unchanged.
- Retain per-graph preflight artifacts and add scalar attempt, retry, first-pass, preflight, and agent-time metrics.

## Why

The retained TPS63802 baseline used 23 agent attempts for 11 graphs. Its 12 corrections were dominated by information the server could safely derive before attempt one: 8 axis/calibration failures, 2 trace-pixel/color failures, 1 coverage/schema failure, and 1 electrical-timing failure.

## TPS63802 paired A/B benchmark

Three completed pairs used the same public datasheet, retained job, provider/model, and graph concurrency (`2`). Order alternated `main -> feature`, `feature -> main`, `main -> feature`.

- Main: `638201572d23e06c9adc7480545fa206c59df754`
- Feature: `1dce1ef4d121caca548345314b6fd4d393be279f`

| Pair | Main wall | Feature wall | Wall change | Main attempts/retries | Feature attempts/retries |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | 25m02s | 20m06s | **-19.7%** | 19 / 8 | 17 / 6 |
| 2 | 23m50s | 25m26s | +6.7% | 19 / 8 | 20 / 9 |
| 3 | 30m49s | 23m50s | **-22.6%** | 23 / 12 | 22 / 11 |

| Metric | Main | Feature | Change |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Median graph-stage wall | 25m02s | 23m50s | **-4.8%** |
| Median summed graph-agent time | 44m59s | 41m43s | **-7.3%** |
| Aggregate graph-stage wall | 79m42s | 69m22s | **-13.0%** |
| Aggregate agent attempts | 61 | 59 | **-3.3%** |
| Aggregate retries | 28 | 26 | **-7.1%** |
| Aggregate first-attempt successes | 13/33 (39.4%) | 19/33 (57.6%) | **+18.2 pp** |
| Median preflight cost | — | 18.0s | 1.3% of median feature wall |

Pair 2 included a roughly 3.5-minute feature-side provider response gap and is retained in the result. Provider/model variance remains large: median attempts moved from 19 to 20 and median retries from 8 to 9 even though aggregate attempts, retries, first-pass success, agent time, and wall time improved. The claim is therefore a modest paired median wall-time improvement with better aggregate retry behavior, not a guaranteed per-run speedup.

Earlier single-run and timed-out diagnostics are excluded from the paired statistics. One diagnostic exposed a Figure 10-30 preflight bug: right-edge non-grid pixels selected anchor `562` instead of the regular plot edge near `523`, shifting focused OCR past the printed `2 V/div` control. The final code selects the longest contiguous regular grid run; real Poppler/Tesseract replay recovers anchors `106.3–522.7`, a `1.001 ms` span, and the printed `2 V/div` scale.

title: Preserve endpoints for shared-net traces
description: Preserves every traces declared source and target endpoints while expanding one-point shared-net routes along already-routed same-net copper when emitting Circuit JSON.
body:
## Summary

- expand one-point shared-net routes along already-routed same-net copper when emitting Circuit JSON
- preserve every trace's declared source and target endpoints
- add a regression for a branch whose endpoints already lie on an earlier shared-net route

## Why

The rip-and-replace solver can correctly treat multiple connections sharing a terminal as one electrical net. When a later branch was already electrically connected by an earlier route, its internal route could contain one node. Emitting that internal shortcut directly produced a one-point PCB trace that tscircuit reported as missing its destination pad.

The build phase now reconstructs the branch path through the existing same-net route graph, preserving the efficient solver behavior while generating valid Circuit JSON.

## Validation

- `bunx tsc --noEmit`
- `bun run format:check`
- `bun test` (15 tests, 191 assertions)
- exact moved-USB RP2040 input: 97 traces solved in about 57 seconds; affected trace expands from 1 to 7 route points

title: Speed up rp2040 repro solve 4.6x with semantics-preserving caching
description: Reduces the solve time for the RP2040 autorouting problem from 346.9 seconds to 74.6 seconds by implementing caching and precomputation techniques in the A algorithm without altering the cost model.
body:
## Summary

Profiling `benchmark.sh` (repro02, the captured RP2040 problem) showed the rip-up A* loop spending most of its time recomputing static values: ~33% in `getForeignOwners` redoing segment-to-segment geometry on every expansion, plus string state keys, string cache keys, and repeated pure penalty computation.

This PR removes that waste without touching the cost model. On the same machine, repro02 goes **346.9s → 74.6s (4.6x)**:

| Run | Solve time | Speedup |
|---|---|---|
| Baseline (`main`) | 346.9s | — |
| Caching + numeric state keys | 112.8s | 3.1x |
| Incremental edge-occupancy index | 106.7s | 3.3x |
| Typed arrays + penalty caches | **74.6s** | **4.6x** |

## Changes

- **`getForeignOwners`**: replaced per-expansion conflict-list rescans with an incremental edge-occupancy index (`occupancyByEdge`) maintained on route commit/uncommit, an ownership-versioned result cache, and conflict-pair segment distances precomputed once per edge.
- **A\* state keys**: packed into numbers (`Map<number, number>`) instead of template strings.
- **Pure per-demand lookups** cached: terminal-escape constraints (WeakMap keyed by demand instead of string keys built 3x per edge), edge/node allowance (`Uint8Array` per demand), fanout and route-geometry penalties (symmetric in the edge endpoints, so cached per edge).
- **Per-search invariants** (layer penalties, route history, congestion cost, geometry flags, guide targets) hoisted out of `considerEdge`.
- **History costs** stored in `Float64Array`s indexed by edge/node id.
- **`addConflictPairs`** (graph generation): numeric bucket keys, stamp-based dedupe instead of a per-edge `Set`, and an AABB prefilter before the exact distance test.
- Added `scripts/visualize-rp2040.ts` to render a solution JSON to SVG for visual debugging.

## Why this is safe

Every change is caching/precomputation of values that are provably constant over the relevant scope — none alters costs, orderings, or tolerances. The benchmark's final stats act as a bit-exact fingerprint of the search trajectory, and they are **identical before and after**: 1,595 rips, 22,157,733 expanded states, 81 negotiation passes, 44 via transitions, 97 traces, 0 manufactured vias, 0 clearance violations. The rendered solution is pixel-identical to `repros/fixtures/repro02-biscuit-board-rp2040.solved.json`.

`bun test`: 11 pass / 0 fail. `bunx tsc --noEmit` clean.

## Follow-up opportunity

Remaining solve time is dominated by negotiation churn (81 rip-up passes over the same conflicting pairs). Tuning the congestion/history schedule could cut solve time further but changes routing outcomes, so it is deliberately out of scope here.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

description: Summary implement meaningful visualize() output for the pipeline input and every solver stage render obstacles, pads, prefabricated vias, terminals, unrouted guides, routed paths, and clearance-conflict overlays add dependency-aware multi-terminal routing so branches can terminate on an existing same-net tree and are invalidated together during rip-up add sparse 45-degree terminal escapes, fine-pitch layer preferences, per-conflict-component Pathfinder penalties, and deterministic alternate-layer fallback post-process traces connected to used prefabricated vias without exempting unrelated nearby vias from clearance checks solve the exact BiscuitBoard RP2040 repro02 with all 97 routing demands, no manufactured vias, and no clearance violations check in the built and post-processed solved fixtures plus an SVG snapshot of the solved post-processing visualization extend benchmark.sh to reproduce and optionally write both solved artifacts  Why The previous repro02 snapshot only rendered the unrouted input, and the draft solver stalled at 9597 routes. Multi-terminal branches could also retain stale tree anchors after a dependency was ripped up, while small independent conflict components were prevented from applying local layer negotiation. body:
## Summary

- implement meaningful `visualize()` output for the pipeline input and every solver stage
- render obstacles, pads, prefabricated vias, terminals, unrouted guides, routed paths, and clearance-conflict overlays
- add dependency-aware multi-terminal routing so branches can terminate on an existing same-net tree and are invalidated together during rip-up
- add sparse 45-degree terminal escapes, fine-pitch layer preferences, per-conflict-component Pathfinder penalties, and deterministic alternate-layer fallback
- post-process traces connected to used prefabricated vias without exempting unrelated nearby vias from clearance checks
- solve the exact BiscuitBoard RP2040 repro02 with all 97 routing demands, no manufactured vias, and no clearance violations
- check in the built and post-processed solved fixtures plus an SVG snapshot of the solved post-processing visualization
- extend `benchmark.sh` to reproduce and optionally write both solved artifacts

## Why

The previous repro02 snapshot only rendered the unrouted input, and the draft solver stalled at 95/97 routes. Multi-terminal branches could also retain stale tree anchors after a dependency was ripped up, while small independent conflict components were prevented from applying local layer negotiation.

## Result

The deterministic RP2040 benchmark now completes with:

- 97/97 routed demands and 97 Circuit JSON traces
- 44 transitions through existing prefabricated vias
- 0 manufactured vias
- 0 clearance violations at the captured board's 0.1 mm clearance
- 1,290 raw segments simplified to 391 post-processed segments

The repro02 SVG snapshot is generated from the solved post-processing stage and includes pads, obstacles, prefabricated vias, raw paths, and final simplified traces.

## Validation

- `bun run test` (11 pass)
- `bun run build`
- `bun run format:check`
- `bun run build:site`
- `git diff --check`
- `./benchmark.sh --json --debug --max-ms=300000` (solved in approximately 231 seconds)

## Summary

- resolve hover labels from `source_trace.name`, directly associated `source_net.name`, or a connected source net

PCB trace hover text previously depended on trace-length metadata and `source_trace.display_name`. Constant-width line traces were also hit-tested but dropped before overlay rendering.

Trace interactions additionally considered overlapping traces from every copper layer. Once a connected trace was marked, the renderer reused that highlight on every layer canvas instead of constraining it to the selected layer.

## Impact

Hovering a PCB trace now shows its meaningful source trace or net name at the cursor without requiring trace-length overlays to be enabled. When layers overlap, only traces on the selected copper layer can be hovered or highlighted.

title: fix: honor solder mask colors in 3d
description: Fixes rendering of solder mask colors in 3D previews by updating the circuit-json-to-gltf dependency to a version that supports color metadata.
body:
## What

- Update `circuit-json-to-gltf` from `^0.0.111` to `^0.0.116`.

## Why

`pcb_board.solder_mask_color` is present in circuit JSON, but the renderer version currently pinned by `tscircuit` ignores it and renders board textures green. `circuit-json-to-gltf` v0.0.116 includes tscircuit/circuit-json-to-gltf#180, which derives face, copper-under-mask, side, and silkscreen colours from the board metadata.

Because this package is still in the `0.0.x` range, `^0.0.111` does not resolve to `0.0.116`; the dependency must be bumped explicitly.

## Impact

Boards using `solderMaskColor`, such as red BoosterPack boards, render with the requested solder-mask colour in the 3D preview. Existing boards without colour metadata retain the green fallback.

## Checks

- `bun run build`
- `bun test` (3 pass)
- Direct renderer regression: red and blue board metadata produce different textures; red resolves to `#8b1e1e` with side colour `#6a1717`

Received: 2

title: Preserve early-rendered copper during autorouting
description: Fixes autorouting failure by preserving manually rendered copper traces during the autorouting process, ensuring that existing copper is not overwritten or crossed by new routes.
body:
## Summary

- preserve PCB copper that already exists in the current routing scope when the standard Simple Route JSON input is built
- rely on the existing render order: `PcbManualTraceRender` runs before `PcbTraceRender`, so `pcbStraightLine` and `pcbPath` traces naturally become fixed input to every later autorouting phase
- add an end-to-end regression where the autorouter changes layer instead of crossing an early-rendered straight-line trace

## Root cause

Manual traces already execute in the earliest relevant render phase, before autorouting begins. The SRJ preservation filter only retained routed descendant-subcircuit copper, however, and dropped already-rendered copper belonging to the subcircuit currently being routed. The autorouter therefore could not see it.

The fix broadens the existing preservation filter to the complete relevant routing scope. There is no `pcbStraightLine` branch, trace-ID plumbing, synthetic routing phase, or new property-specific routing behavior.

title: Expand phased autorouting bounds around connection points
description: Expands phased autorouting bounds around the phases non-off-board connection points to ensure consistent routing behavior and avoid invalid autorouter issues.
body:
## Summary

- expand phased autorouting bounds around the phase's non-off-board connection points
- preserve explicit phase bounds when they already contain every routed point
- add a regression test covering a phase-specific bounds override and an unrelated out-of-phase connection

## Root cause

`getSimpleRouteJsonFromCircuitJson` expands the base SimpleRouteJson bounds around all non-off-board connection points. During phased autorouting, `Group_filterSimpleRouteJsonForPhase` can subsequently replace those expanded bounds with `phasePlan.routingBounds`. A point outside those phase-specific bounds then reaches the autorouter even though the base SRJ was corrected.

The phase filter now expands its final bounds after filtering connections and applying the optional phase-specific bounds override. Only connections routed in that phase influence the expansion.

## Impact

Custom and built-in autorouters receive bounds containing every non-off-board point routed in the current phase. This makes phased routing consistent with the base SRJ bounds behavior and avoids invalid autorouter problems that are difficult to diagnose.

## Validation

- `bun test tests/utils/autorouting`
- `bunx tsc --noEmit`
- `bun run build`

title: Detect via-to-pad clearance violations
description: Add a via-to-pad copper edge clearance check that ignores pads connected to the same net and pads on non-overlapping layers, reuses pad geometry for various pad shapes, and runs the new check as part of routing DRC, including a visual SVG snapshot of the fine-pitch escape-via failure.
body:
## Summary
- add a via-to-pad copper edge clearance check
- ignore pads connected to the same net and pads on non-overlapping layers
- reuse pad geometry for rectangular, rotated, pill, polygon, and circular pads
- run the new check as part of routing DRC
- include a visual SVG snapshot of the fine-pitch escape-via failure

## Root cause
Existing checks cover pad-to-pad, pad-to-trace, via-to-trace, and via-to-via spacing, but no check compares a via's outer copper diameter with an unrelated pad. A 0.6 mm escape via beside 0.35 mm-pitch pads could therefore have only 0.002 mm clearance without emitting a DRC error.

## Verification
- focused numeric and SVG snapshot regression: pass
- TypeScript noEmit: pass

title: Fix low-count trace-crossing repair in bugreport88
description: Fixes low-count trace-crossing repair in bugreport88 by addressing same-layer trace conflicts and improving the exact-DRC solvers handling of trace topology.
body: ## Before Trace overlap: ## After ## Summary - pin `high-density-repair03` to the trace-topology repair - re-enable the full bugreport88 regression with its zero-DRC assertion and SVG snapshot check - update the active exact-DRC diagnostic snapshot for the repaired dependency Depends on [tscircuit/high-density-repair03#65](https://github.com/tscircuit/high-density-repair03/pull/65). ## Root cause The three originally reported failures are same-layer trace conflicts: - `source_trace_146_mst2_0` crosses `source_trace_145_mst2_0` - `source_trace_146_mst4_0` crosses `source_trace_145_mst2_0` - `source_trace_125_0` crosses `source_trace_95_mst15_0` The exact-DRC solver admitted boards with a few remaining errors but only ran its legacy trace topology detours after the board had already reached one error. This board stalled at three. Some trace pairs also contact in multiple segments, so the first reported contact is not always the deepest collision. The dependency fix preserves legacy first-contact behavior globally, but records worst-contact metadata. Only a stage whose initial snapshot contains two or three trace-pair errors enables solver-local worst-contact scoring and the bounded span/waypoint portfolio. Candidates remain board-bounded and transactionally DRC-scored. ## Rebase and snapshot note Rebased onto `main` at `c4db236e`. Newer routing work on `main` had already updated bugreport88 to the same final SVG produced by this branch. Consequently, the re-enabled test verifies the zero-DRC result and snapshot, but GitHub shows no bugreport SVG file diff against the current base. The historical before/after routing is shown above. ## Validation - `BUN_UPDATE_SNAPSHOTS=1 bun test tests/bugs/bugreport88-9a86ed.test.ts --timeout 9999999` — 1 passed, 0 failed; snapshot unchanged; 0 DRC errors - control run on current `main` with the old repair dependency — also passed and generated the same SVG, confirming the lack of a current-base SVG diff - `bun test tests/autorouting-dataset18-sample10-exact-drc-residue-visual.test.ts tests/bugs/bugreport88-9a86ed.test.ts --timeout 9999999` — diagnostic passed and bugreport test is active - active diagnostic: 1 input benchmark DRC error → 0 output errors - `bun run build` - dependency: `bun run typecheck`, `bun run formatcheck`, and 58 tests / 438 assertions

title: Honor via-to-pad clearance for escape vias
description: Honor Simple Route JSONs explicit minimum via-edge-to-pad-edge clearance when placing copper-pour escape vias, ensuring that the stricter of the generic obstacle margin and the explicit via-to-pad clearance is used for sizing and validating escape-via candidates.
body:
## Summary
- honor Simple Route JSON's explicit minimum via-edge-to-pad-edge clearance when placing copper-pour escape vias
- include that clearance in the initial escape offset and candidate obstacle rejection
- add a minimal fine-pitch pad regression using a 0.6 mm via

## Root cause
EscapeViaLocationSolver used only defaultObstacleMargin when sizing and validating escape-via candidates. When that generic margin was smaller than minViaEdgeToPadEdgeClearance, a candidate could be accepted despite violating the board's via-to-pad DRC. The reproduction produced 0.0953 mm clearance for a required 0.1 mm.

## Impact
Escape vias now use the stricter of the generic obstacle margin and the explicit via-to-pad clearance. Existing designs without the explicit field preserve their current behavior.

## Verification
- focused new regression plus existing escape-via regression suite: 4 passed, 0 failed
- TypeScript noEmit: pass
- package build including declarations: pass

title: Lower partial-rip congestion and stop at convergence
description: Tightens the partial-rip max-region-cost growth envelope from 20 to 5, stops SRJ18 partial-rip integration after round 7, and documents region-costruntime tuning trials.
body:
## What

- tighten the partial-rip max-region-cost growth envelope from 20% to 5%
- pin [tiny-hypergraph #160](https://github.com/tscircuit/tiny-hypergraph/pull/160), which keeps the threshold ramp independent from the partial-rip attempt cap
- stop the SRJ18 partial-rip integration after round 7 instead of round 10
- document the accepted and rejected region-cost/runtime tuning trials

## Why

Strict region-cost-first selection made detailed routing slower and reduced DRC coverage. The narrower 5% peak-cost envelope removes the observed large congestion regression without discarding the simpler topologies that help downstream routing.

Frontier telemetry then showed that every selected completed SRJ18 candidate had already been found by round 7. The tiny-hypergraph fix lets the integration stop there without compressing the congestion-threshold ramp, so rounds 8–10 can be removed while preserving the selected topology and region costs.

## Impact

- sample 3 max region cost: 1.736 → 1.142 (-34.2%)
- sample 3 total region cost: 14.896 → 11.997 (-19.5%)
- across 8 completed active cases, average max cost falls 5.9% and average total cost falls 2.6%
- matched five-case runtime: 408.1s → 378.0s (-7.4%)
- clean pinned-dependency confirmation: 408.1s → 385.5s (-5.5%)
- relaxed DRC remains 4/5 and average vias remain exactly 166.60
- samples 4 and 13 still time out in the same downstream exact-DRC and high-density phases
- dataset01, SRJ19, SRJ20, SRJ21, and preloaded SRJ23 remain outside the 100–350 route activation window in stored telemetry

## Hosted `/benchmark-all`

All six workflows completed successfully on the final commit `1436ca2`:

| Dataset | Completion (main → PR) | DRC (main → PR) | Timeouts (main → PR) | P50 (main → PR) |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| dataset01 | 100.0% → 100.0% | 90.6% → 90.6% | 0 → 0 | 7.5s → 6.1s |
| SRJ18 | 50.0% → 56.3% | 31.3% → 31.3% | 8 → 7 | 88.1s → 84.7s |
| SRJ19 | 80.0% → 82.5% | 37.0% → 37.0% | 40 → 35 | 46.7s → 41.2s |
| SRJ20 | 70.0% → 70.0% | 30.5% → 30.5% | 60 → 60 | 41.2s → 31.4s |

| SRJ23 | 98.7% → 98.7% | 14.5% → 14.5% | 0 → 0 | 6.6s → 6.3s |

No dataset loses completion or relaxed-DRC coverage. P50 improves on five datasets and is unchanged on SRJ21; SRJ18 and SRJ19 also retain their completion/timeout gains.
