title: Enable partial ripping for Pipeline9 preloads
description: Enables partial ripping for Pipeline9 preloads when preloaded trace occupancy is present, optimizing routing efficiency and reducing rerip times.
body:
## Summary

- opt Pipeline9 into outside-in partial ripping when preloaded trace occupancy is present
- use the greater of logical route count and preloaded assignment count when applying the existing 100–350 partial-rip scale bounds
- preserve the general tiny-hypergraph behavior for other pipelines and keep partial ripping disabled outside the validated scale window
- enable complexity-aware selection for eligible preloaded graphs so a qualifying local improvement stops further ripping

## Root cause

The partial-rip integration deliberately disabled itself whenever the serialized hypergraph contained preloaded occupancy. Pipeline9 always has that occupancy, so it continued using full rerips. Its logical route count can also understate the size of the routing problem: the Allwinner SPI reproduction has 27 logical routes but 193 preloaded assignments.

This left Pipeline9 doing ten full rerips and restoring the original preload assignments, producing zero accepted changed preload sections.

## Allwinner SPI reproduction

Input: the phase-2 SimpleRouteJson from `motherboard-allwinner-f1c100s`.

Before this change:

- 10 rerips
- 0 changed preloaded trace sections
- max region cost 0.937
- Pipeline9 reached joint DRC in about 41 seconds with 15 initial issues and 15 movable preloaded traces

After this change:

- one full-rip warmup followed by one partial-rip round
- 6 partially ripped routes, 87 ripped segments, and 131 retained segments
- 6 changed preloaded trace sections accepted and materialized
- max region cost reduced from 0.937 to 0.432; total region cost reduced from 2.245 to 0.749
- Pipeline9 reached joint DRC in 18.4 seconds with 13 initial issues and 14 movable preloaded traces

The downstream joint DRC repair still stalls on this board, so this does not claim to complete the full route. It fixes the earlier Pipeline9 failure to adapt any preloaded hypergraph sections and gives joint repair a smaller, better input.

## Validation

- `bun run build`
- `bunx tsc --noEmit`
- `bun test tests/features/partial-rip-preloaded-trace-occupancy.test.ts tests/features/pipeline9-minimal-preloaded-trace-graph.test.ts tests/features/preloaded-fixed-segment-occupancy.test.ts tests/features/pipeline9-materializes-hypergraph-preloaded-section.test.ts tests/features/pipeline9-splices-hypergraph-preloaded-section.test.ts --timeout 9999999`

title: Derive board colors from solder-mask metadata
description: Derives board surface, covered copper, substrate edge, and silkscreen colors from solder-mask metadata, ensuring consistent rendering based on board properties.

## Summary

- use `pcb_board.solder_mask_color` as the default board-surface color
- derive covered-copper, substrate-edge, and contrasting silkscreen colors from that mask
- honor `pcb_board.silkscreen_color`, while keeping explicit renderer options highest priority
- support named tscircuit board colors, hex/rgb values, and the legacy `soldermask_color` spelling

## Why

The renderer treated the board surface, mask-covered traces, and substrate sides as independent defaults. As a result, changing a board's solder-mask color could still leave hardcoded green materials in the 3D render. This centralizes those defaults around the board metadata introduced by the circuit and follows up on #179.

Callers can now set `solderMaskColor` and `silkscreenColor` on the tscircuit board instead of reproducing a renderer-specific color palette.

title: Fix different-net copper pour clearance
description: Fixes the copper pour clearance issue by allowing different-net regions on the same layer to have physical clearance, ensuring that later regions take priority over earlier ones during the pour process.
body:
## What

- Solve all pour regions in one ordered geometry pass instead of treating each region independently.
- Give later regions higher priority and subtract higher-priority, different-net copper from lower-priority pours using the larger requested pour clearance.
- Keep same-net pours and pours on different layers independent.
- Preserve per-region output ownership through `brep_shapes_by_region` while retaining the existing flattened `brep_shapes` output.
- Allow Circuit JSON conversion to accept an ordered options array for pours in the same subcircuit.
- Turn the merged overlap repro into a passing regression and add focused priority, clearance, same-net, and layer-isolation coverage.

## Why

The previous pipeline iterated `regionsForPour` but solved every region only against pads, traces, holes, and cutouts. Already-solved copper was never added as blocker geometry, so same-layer pours on different nets could occupy the same physical area.

The fix keeps solved regions as Manifold cross-sections. When solving a lower-priority region, higher-priority copper on the same layer and a different connectivity key is offset by the larger of the two `pourMargin` values and subtracted from the candidate pour.

This fixes the solver-level failure recorded in #75 without adding DRC-only suppression, test-specific cutouts, or placement workarounds.

## Behavior

- Input array order defines priority; later regions win.
- Different-net regions on the same layer receive physical clearance.
- Same-net regions do not block each other.
- Regions on different layers do not block each other.
- Output shapes remain associated with their input region for correct net assignment by callers.

## Checks

- `bun test` — 40 pass
- `bunx tsc --noEmit`
- `bun run format:check`
- `bun run build`

## What

- Add a minimal expected-failing regression using an actual tscircuit TSX board.
- Define a full-board bottom GND `<copperpour>` and an inset bottom AISEN `<copperpour>`.

- Assert that no board point belongs to more than one different-net pour.

## Why

The solver currently processes each pour independently. Other same-layer, different-net pours are not included in the blocker geometry, so both generated B-Rep shapes contain the board-center point.

With the `test.failing` wrapper removed, the TSX regression reports:

```text
Expected: <= 1
Received: 2
```

The expected-failing wrapper keeps CI green while preserving the desired invariant. It should be removed when pour-to-pour clearance is implemented.

## Impact

This reproduces the solver-level cause of same-layer, different-net copper overlap from the public tscircuit component API, which can create an electrical short in generated PCB copper. The annotated snapshot makes the two intended pour regions and their electrical overlap understandable without reading the test source.

title: Decouple partial-rip cap from threshold ramp
description: Decouples the partial-rip attempt cap from the threshold ramp, allowing for independent ramp scheduling and improved routing policy without affecting earlier candidates or their region costs.
body:
## What changed

- keep `RIP_THRESHOLD_RAMP_ATTEMPTS` as the denominator for the congestion-threshold ramp
- use `PARTIAL_RIP_MAX_ATTEMPTS` only to cap how many completed rerip rounds run
- add a regression test covering a shorter partial-rip cap than the configured ramp

## Why

The partial-rip attempt cap previously compressed the threshold ramp whenever it was lower than `RIP_THRESHOLD_RAMP_ATTEMPTS`. That coupled a runtime budget to routing policy: reducing the number of rounds changed which regions were ripped and could change the selected topology.

Keeping the ramp schedule independent lets integrations stop once their observed candidate frontier has converged without perturbing earlier candidates or their region costs.

## Validation

title: Repair low-count trace topology conflicts
description: Fixes autorouting failure when low-count trace topology conflicts occur, allowing for better handling of trace pairs with multiple crossings.
body:
## What changed

- preserve the legacy first-contact DRC error while recording the deepest contact for solver-local scoring
- enable an enhanced bounded segment/span/waypoint portfolio only when a stage initially contains two or three trace-pair errors
- keep that enhanced mode active for follow-on obstacle errors exposed by the trace repair
- preserve the legacy one-error detour ordering and count-only acceptance for all other stages
- reject new span/waypoint candidates outside board bounds and score candidates against full-board DRC
- centralize trace-segment/span selection and worst-clearance severity scoring so repair strategies reuse the same helpers

This branch is based on the dependency commit currently pinned by tscircuit-autorouter (`6943de1`), preserving its three downstream commits.

## Root cause

The global DRC solver allowed low-count boards but only attempted its legacy trace topology repair after the current best count was already one. Bugreport88 therefore stalled at three same-layer trace crossings. Some trace pairs contact in more than one segment, so the first reported location can also be shallower than the segment that must be moved.

## Safety

Legacy stages retain first-contact behavior. Worst-contact scoring and the expanded portfolio are solver-local and require a stable initial eligibility condition (2–3 trace-pair errors), preventing unrelated trace-to-pad boards from entering the new path. Candidate phases remain transactional and are accepted by exact full-board DRC.

## Validation

- `bun run typecheck`
- `bun run formatcheck`
- `bun test --timeout 9999999` — 58 passed, 0 failed, 438 assertions
- downstream bugreport88 — 3 DRC errors reduced to 0
- downstream SRJ20 sample169 remains at 0 DRC
- representative legacy autorouter snapshots pass unchanged

Downstream PR: [tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter#2054](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/pull/2054)

`source_component → zero-size pcb_component → cad_component.model_jscad`

Published `circuit-json-to-gltf` renders that path, so geometry can ship and Core can migrate while remaining on the existing interchange contract. A later Circuit JSON/renderer PR will replace this compatibility exporter with one typed `cad_fdm_enclosure` record per base/lid part.

title: Route SRJ29 power pins independently
description: Splits each SRJ29 VCCGND connection into independently assigned fanout buses, allowing for improved routing without discarding valid breakouts due to pin fitting issues.
body:
## What changed

- split each SRJ29 VCC/GND connection into an independently assigned fanout bus
- retain the existing left-side VCC and right-side GND escape corridors
- preserve shared electrical-net identity, same-net copper merging, boundary breakout validation, capacitor endpoints, and all different-net DRC checks
- test that every power connection receives exactly one boundary-terminated bus in the intended direction
- snapshot three fully validated SRJ29 solutions (samples 001, 005, and 009) as SVG visual regressions

## Why

VCC and GND were modeled as two atomic multi-pin buses. If one power pin could not fit the bus plan, the solver discarded every otherwise valid breakout on that net. Power pins do not need signal-bus length matching or a common escape layer, so they should choose layers independently and merge only where same-net copper is valid.

## Benchmark impact

Full 200-sample Blacksmith run at 256 layer assignments:

- validated solves: **13/200 -> 105/200** (+92)
- routed connections: **5,987/7,676 (78.0%) -> 7,459/7,676 (97.17%)** (+1,472)
- partial/errors/timeouts: **187/0/0 -> 95/0/0**
- wall time: **341.36s -> 804.37s**
- aggregate solver time: **5,068.78s -> 17,485.10s**

[Blacksmith benchmark run](https://github.com/tscircuit/fanout-solver/actions/runs/31440897029)

Local first-ten comparison at the same assignment budget:

On the first 10 SRJ29 samples at 256 layer assignments:

- solved: **1/10 -> 7/10**
- routed connections: **264/340 (77.7%) -> 335/340 (98.5%)**
- remaining partials: sample004 41/42, sample006 55/58, sample007 54/55

## Summary

## Validation contract

The final validator checks:

- exactly one plan for every input connection, with the correct source pad and bus termination
- continuous trace/via geometry matching the declared route plan
- a continuous same-net copper path from every package pin to the shared boundary (including legal merged branches)

- trace-to-different-net-pad clearance on the occupied layer
- via-to-different-net-obstacle clearance on every layer in the via span
- different-net trace/trace, trace/via, and via/via intersections and clearance
- route containment within the SRJ/shared-boundary routing area

title: Add nominal trace expansion
description: Adds a fifth, obstacle-aware trace-expansion phase to the autorouter, allowing for the expansion of routed traces toward their nominal width while preserving existing vias and compacting the expanded result without creating new vias.
body:
## Summary

- add a fifth, obstacle-aware trace-expansion phase backed by `@tscircuit/power-trace-expander`
- separate minimum routable width from the requested nominal trace width
- preserve existing vias and compact the expanded result without manufacturing new vias
- add RP2040 and STM32 regressions for 0.3 mm nominal-width coverage

## Why

The initial autorouter can produce legal narrow escape routes, but it had no final phase that recovers width where surrounding clearance permits. That left the RP2040 and STM32 examples substantially below their intended 0.3 mm width even in open board areas.

## Impact

The routing pipeline now attempts to expand each routed trace toward its nominal width after routing and post-processing. Expansion remains obstacle-aware, retains fixed vias, and falls back conservatively around constrained pad transitions. The regressions require more than 80% nominal-width coverage with low normalized width deficit.

## Checks

- `bun run format:check`
- `bun run build`
- RP2040 repro regression
- STM32 repro regression
- fixed-via invariant suite (5/5)
- `git diff --check`

title: Automatically repair rotated obstacle routes

- make terminal escape guides clearance-aware for wider traces

title: Add easyedats schematic conversion
description: Adds a BunTypeScript converter package for EasyEDA schematics to Circuit JSON, enabling lossless conversion and diagnostics for unsupported records.
body:
## What changed

- bootstraps the Bun/TypeScript converter package and CI workflows
- uses easyedats as the only EasyEDA parser and typed semantic model
- converts schematic wires, junctions, labels, text, rectangles, circles, ellipses, lines, polylines, polygons, buses, bus entries, no-connect marks, and nested library graphics
- transforms EasyEDA 10 mil Y-down coordinates into Circuit JSON millimeter Y-up coordinates with transformation-matrix
- returns source-linked diagnostics for invalid, lossy, and unsupported records
- supports typed schematic-list sheet selection
- adds ten side-by-side SVG parity fixtures rendered by easyedats and circuit-to-svg with stack-svgs and toMatchSvgSnapshot

## Why

Teda needs a reproducible Circuit JSON view of losslessly preserved EasyEDA source. This establishes the first conversion slice without copying the legacy converter's parallel EasyEDA schema or string DSL parsing.

## Impact

Consumers can convert standalone EasyEDA schematic documents or already parsed EasyEdaDocument instances. PCB conversion and compound symbol pins/paths remain explicit follow-up coverage rather than being silently approximated.

## Validation

- bun run check
- 16 tests, including 10 committed side-by-side SVG parity snapshots
- every emitted element is checked with circuit-json's any_circuit_element schema
